[1630](https://docs.rs#1630)    fn c_abi_type_table() {
[1631](https://docs.rs#1631)        assert_eq!(c_abi_type(&Type::I64), Some("::std::os::raw::c_int"));
[1632](https://docs.rs#1632)        assert_eq!(c_abi_type(&Type::Bool), Some("::std::os::raw::c_int"));
[1633](https://docs.rs#1633)        assert_eq!(c_abi_type(&Type::F64), Some("::std::os::raw::c_double"));
[1634](https://docs.rs#1634)        // PMAT-911: a 32-bit C float rides the DISTINCT c_float slot — never
[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)        // widened through the 64-bit c_double.
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)        assert_eq!(
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)            c_abi_type(&Type::F32),
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)            Some("::std::os::raw::c_float"),
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)            "float must ride the 32-bit c_float ABI slot, not c_double"
[1640](https://docs.rs#1640)        );
[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)        assert_ne!(
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)            c_abi_type(&Type::F32),
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)            c_abi_type(&Type::F64),
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)            "F32 and F64 must map to distinct C ABI slots"
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)        );
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)        assert_eq!(wrapper_native(&Type::F32), "f32");
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)        // PMAT-909: a wider C integer is NOT narrowed to c_int.
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)        assert_eq!(
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)            c_abi_type(&Type::CLong),
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)            Some("::std::os::raw::c_longlong"),
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)            "long/int64_t must ride the 64-bit c_longlong ABI slot, not c_int"
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)        );
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)        assert_eq!(wrapper_native(&Type::CLong), "i64");
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)        // PMAT-918: a 32-bit UNSIGNED C int rides the DISTINCT c_uint slot —
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)        // never the signed c_int (a value ≥ 2³¹ would otherwise flip sign).
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)        assert_eq!(
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)            c_abi_type(&Type::CUInt),
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)            Some("::std::os::raw::c_uint"),
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)            "unsigned/uint32_t must ride the unsigned c_uint ABI slot, not c_int"
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)        );
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)        assert_ne!(
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)            c_abi_type(&Type::CUInt),
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)            c_abi_type(&Type::I64),
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)            "CUInt and I64 must map to distinct (signedness) C ABI slots"
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)        );
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)        assert_eq!(
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)            wrapper_native(&Type::CUInt),
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)            "u32",
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)            "unsigned wrapper must speak u32, never fall through to the i64 default"
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)        );
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)        // PMAT-921: a 64-bit UNSIGNED C int rides the DISTINCT c_ulonglong slot —
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)        // never the 32-bit c_uint (truncation) nor the signed c_longlong (a
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)        // value ≥ 2⁶³ would otherwise flip sign).
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)        assert_eq!(
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)            c_abi_type(&Type::CULong),
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)            Some("::std::os::raw::c_ulonglong"),
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)            "unsigned long/uint64_t must ride the unsigned 64-bit c_ulonglong ABI slot"
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)        );
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)        assert_ne!(
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)            c_abi_type(&Type::CULong),
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)            c_abi_type(&Type::CLong),
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)            "CULong and CLong must map to distinct (signedness) C ABI slots"
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)        );
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)        assert_ne!(
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)            c_abi_type(&Type::CULong),
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)            c_abi_type(&Type::CUInt),
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)            "CULong and CUInt must map to distinct (width) C ABI slots"
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)        );
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)        assert_eq!(
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)            wrapper_native(&Type::CULong),
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)            "u64",
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)            "unsigned long wrapper must speak u64, never fall through to the i64 default"
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)        );
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)        for ty in [
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)            Type::Str,
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)            Type::List(Box::new(Type::I64)),
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)            Type::Dict(Box::new(Type::Str), Box::new(Type::I64)),
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)            Type::Set(Box::new(Type::I64)),
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)            Type::Tuple(vec![Type::I64]),
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)            Type::BigInt,
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)            Type::Optional(Box::new(Type::I64)),
[1702](https://docs.rs#1702)            Type::Struct("P".into()),
[1703](https://docs.rs#1703)            Type::ShellString,
[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)            Type::ExitCode,
[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)        ] {
[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)            assert_eq!(c_abi_type(&ty), None, "{ty:?} must be refused");
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)        }
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)    }

[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)    #[test]
[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)    fn c_abi_render_pointer_is_abi_honest_no_cast() {
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)        // PMAT-924: a non-`char` C pointer (`int*`) renders as a raw `*mut c_int`
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)        // whose native form IS the ABI form (RawPtr, no cast — a self-cast would
[1714](https://docs.rs#1714)        // trip clippy::unnecessary_cast). A bare `int` still casts (i64 -> c_int).
[1715](https://docs.rs#1715)        let p = c_abi_render(&Type::Ptr {
[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)            mutable: true,
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)            pointee: Box::new(Type::I64),
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)        })
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)        .expect("int* is ABI-mappable");
[1720](https://docs.rs#1720)        assert_eq!(p.abi, "*mut ::std::os::raw::c_int");
[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)        assert_eq!(p.native_param, "*mut ::std::os::raw::c_int");
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)        assert_eq!(p.native_ret, "*mut ::std::os::raw::c_int");
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)        assert!(
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)            matches!(p.marshal, Marshal::RawPtr),
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)            "a non-char raw pointer is its own native form — no marshalling"
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)        );
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)        // PMAT-925: `char*` is the canonical C string — the ABI slot is still a
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)        // raw `*mut c_char`, but the wrapper speaks `&str` in / owned `String`
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)        // out and marshals via a CString/CStr round-trip (Marshal::CStr).
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)        let pc = c_abi_render(&Type::Ptr {
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)            mutable: true,
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)            pointee: Box::new(Type::CChar),
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)        })
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)        .expect("char* is ABI-mappable");
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)        assert_eq!(pc.abi, "*mut ::std::os::raw::c_char");
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)        assert_eq!(pc.native_param, "&str", "char* param speaks &str");
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)        assert_eq!(pc.native_ret, "String", "char* return speaks owned String");
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)        assert!(
[1740](https://docs.rs#1740)            matches!(pc.marshal, Marshal::CStr),
[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)            "char* marshals via CString/CStr, not a raw pointer pass-through"
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)        );
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)        // A scalar still needs the i64 -> c_int cast.
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)        let s = c_abi_render(&Type::I64).expect("scalar");
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)        assert!(
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)            matches!(s.marshal, Marshal::ScalarCast),
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)            "a scalar param casts to its C ABI slot"
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)        );
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)        // Refuse-rather-than-mis-marshal: a pointer to a NON-mappable pointee
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)        // (a container) is refused (None), not silently emitted.
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)        assert!(
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)            c_abi_render(&Type::Ptr {
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)                mutable: true,
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)                pointee: Box::new(Type::Str),
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)            })
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)            .is_none(),
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)            "pointer to a non-ABI-mappable pointee must be refused"
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)        );
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)    }

[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)    #[test]
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)    fn emit_shims_pointer_param_compiles_abi_honest() {
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)        // PMAT-924/925 end-to-end: a C `char*` param marshals to `&str` (PMAT-925)
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)        // while a NON-char `int*` param stays an ABI-honest raw pointer (PMAT-924).
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)        // The extern decl keeps both as raw pointers; the wrapper speaks `&str`
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)        // for the string and the raw pointer for `int*`, compiling under

[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)        let out = emit_for(
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)            "scan",
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)            vec![
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)                (
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)                    "s",
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)                    Type::Ptr {
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)                        mutable: true,
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)                        pointee: Box::new(Type::CChar),
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)                    },
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)                ),
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)                (
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)                    "out",
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)                    Type::Ptr {
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)                        mutable: true,
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)                        pointee: Box::new(Type::I64),
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)                    },
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)                ),
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)            ],
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)            Type::I64,
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)        )
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)        .expect("emits");
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)        assert!(
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)            out.contains(
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)                "fn scan(s: *mut ::std::os::raw::c_char, out: *mut ::std::os::raw::c_int) -> ::std::os::raw::c_int;"
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)            ),
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)            "ABI-honest raw-pointer extern decl (both params stay raw pointers): {out}"
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)        );
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)        // PMAT-925: the `char*` param surfaces as `&str`, the `int*` stays raw.
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)        assert!(
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)            out.contains("pub fn scan_shim(s: &str, out: *mut ::std::os::raw::c_int) -> i64 {"),
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)            "wrapper marshals char* -> &str, keeps int* raw: {out}"
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)        );
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)        // The CString is bound BEFORE the unsafe call (so its buffer outlives it).
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)        assert!(
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)            out.contains("let __c_s = ::std::ffi::CString::new(s).expect(")

[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)        );
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)        // The non-char `int*` arg must NOT be self-cast (clippy::unnecessary_cast).
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)        assert!(
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)            !out.contains("out as *mut"),
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)            "a raw int* arg must not be self-cast: {out}"
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)        );

[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)    fn emit_shims_cstr_roundtrip_marshals_string() {
[1856](https://docs.rs#1856)        // PMAT-925 — the LAST decy ABI ceiling: a `char* upper(char*)` boundary
[1857](https://docs.rs#1857)        // marshals a borrowed `&str` IN (via a NUL-checked CString whose buffer
[1858](https://docs.rs#1858)        // outlives the call) and an owned `String` OUT (via a CStr view). The
[1859](https://docs.rs#1859)        // safe wrapper NEVER exposes a raw `*mut c_char` — `unsafe` raw-pointer
[1860](https://docs.rs#1860)        // handling is confined to the shim. The extern decl stays ABI-honest raw
[1861](https://docs.rs#1861)        // pointers; the whole thing compiles under -D warnings.
[1862](https://docs.rs#1862)        let out = emit_for(
[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)            "upper",
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)            vec![(
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)                "s",
[1866](https://docs.rs#1866)                Type::Ptr {
[1867](https://docs.rs#1867)                    mutable: true,
[1868](https://docs.rs#1868)                    pointee: Box::new(Type::CChar),
[1869](https://docs.rs#1869)                },
[1870](https://docs.rs#1870)            )],
[1871](https://docs.rs#1871)            Type::Ptr {
[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)                mutable: true,
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)                pointee: Box::new(Type::CChar),
[1874](https://docs.rs#1874)            },
[1875](https://docs.rs#1875)        )
[1876](https://docs.rs#1876)        .expect("emits");
[1877](https://docs.rs#1877)        // ABI boundary: both sides are raw `*mut c_char` in the extern block.
[1878](https://docs.rs#1878)        assert!(
[1879](https://docs.rs#1879)            out.contains(
[1880](https://docs.rs#1880)                "fn upper(s: *mut ::std::os::raw::c_char) -> *mut ::std::os::raw::c_char;"
[1881](https://docs.rs#1881)            ),
[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)            "extern decl keeps raw c_char pointers: {out}"
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)        );
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)        // Safe surface: `&str` in, owned `String` out — no raw pointer leaks.
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)        assert!(
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)            out.contains("pub fn upper_shim(s: &str) -> String {"),
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)            "wrapper marshals char* both ways to &str/String: {out}"
[1888](https://docs.rs#1888)        );
[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)        assert!(
[1890](https://docs.rs#1890)            !out.contains("_shim(s: *mut"),
[1891](https://docs.rs#1891)            "the safe wrapper must NOT expose a raw *mut c_char: {out}"
[1892](https://docs.rs#1892)        );
[1893](https://docs.rs#1893)        // Param marshal: a pre-call NUL-checked CString, borrowed for the call.
[1894](https://docs.rs#1894)        assert!(
[1895](https://docs.rs#1895)            out.contains("let __c_s = ::std::ffi::CString::new(s).expect(")
[1896](https://docs.rs#1896)                && out.contains("__c_s.as_ptr() as *mut ::std::os::raw::c_char"),
[1897](https://docs.rs#1897)            "char* param marshals via a pre-call CString binding: {out}"
[1898](https://docs.rs#1898)        );
[1899](https://docs.rs#1899)        // Return marshal: a CStr view copied into an owned String (lossy-UTF-8 to
[1900](https://docs.rs#1900)        // stay total on non-UTF-8 bytes).
[1901](https://docs.rs#1901)        assert!(
[1902](https://docs.rs#1902)            out.contains(
[1903](https://docs.rs#1903)                "unsafe { ::std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr(__r).to_string_lossy().into_owned() }"
[1904](https://docs.rs#1904)            ),
[1905](https://docs.rs#1905)            "char* return marshals via a CStr -> owned String view: {out}"
[1906](https://docs.rs#1906)        );
[1907](https://docs.rs#1907)        assert!(
[1908](https://docs.rs#1908)            rustc_lib_compiles("cstr", &out),
[1909](https://docs.rs#1909)            "emitted CStr-marshalling shim must compile under -D warnings"
[1910](https://docs.rs#1910)        );
[1911](https://docs.rs#1911)    }

[1941](https://docs.rs#1941)
[1942](https://docs.rs#1942)    /// Compile `src` as a standalone Rust lib under `-D warnings`, on BOTH
[1943](https://docs.rs#1943)    /// edition 2021 and edition 2024. Returns `true` if rustc is unavailable
[1944](https://docs.rs#1944)    /// (constrained CI skips the gate) or the source compiles under every
[1945](https://docs.rs#1945)    /// edition. The emitted shim is meant to be dropped into a user crate of
[1946](https://docs.rs#1946)    /// unknown edition — and `cargo new` defaults to 2024 — so a 2021-only gate
[1947](https://docs.rs#1947)    /// would mask the bare-`extern "C"` regression (a hard error in 2024). `tag`
[1948](https://docs.rs#1948)    /// keeps concurrent compile-gate tests off each other's temp files (a bare
[1949](https://docs.rs#1949)    /// pid collides when tests run in parallel threads).
[1950](https://docs.rs#1950)    fn rustc_lib_compiles(tag: &str, src: &str) -> bool {
[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)        if std::process::Command::new("rustc")
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)            .arg("--version")
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)            .output()
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)            .is_err()
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)        {
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)            eprintln!("rustc unavailable — skipping compile gate");
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)            return true;
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)        }
[1959](https://docs.rs#1959)        let dir = std::env::temp_dir();
[1960](https://docs.rs#1960)        let pid = std::process::id();
[1961](https://docs.rs#1961)        for edition in ["2021", "2024"] {
[1962](https://docs.rs#1962)            let src_path = dir.join(format!("xpile_shim_gate_{tag}_{edition}_{pid}.rs"));
[1963](https://docs.rs#1963)            let rlib = dir.join(format!("libxpile_shim_gate_{tag}_{edition}_{pid}.rlib"));
[1964](https://docs.rs#1964)            std::fs::write(&src_path, src).expect("write shim");
[1965](https://docs.rs#1965)            let status = std::process::Command::new("rustc")
[1966](https://docs.rs#1966)                .args([
[1967](https://docs.rs#1967)                    "--crate-type",
[1968](https://docs.rs#1968)                    "lib",
[1969](https://docs.rs#1969)                    "--edition",
[1970](https://docs.rs#1970)                    edition,
[1971](https://docs.rs#1971)                    "-D",
[1972](https://docs.rs#1972)                    "warnings",
[1973](https://docs.rs#1973)                ])
[1974](https://docs.rs#1974)                .arg(&src_path)
[1975](https://docs.rs#1975)                .arg("-o")
[1976](https://docs.rs#1976)                .arg(&rlib)
[1977](https://docs.rs#1977)                .status()
[1978](https://docs.rs#1978)                .expect("spawn rustc");
[1979](https://docs.rs#1979)            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&src_path);
[1980](https://docs.rs#1980)            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&rlib);
[1981](https://docs.rs#1981)            if !status.success() {
[1982](https://docs.rs#1982)                eprintln!("emitted shim failed to compile under edition {edition}");
[1983](https://docs.rs#1983)                return false;
[1984](https://docs.rs#1984)            }
[1985](https://docs.rs#1985)        }
[1986](https://docs.rs#1986)        true
[1987](https://docs.rs#1987)    }
[1988](https://docs.rs#1988)
[1989](https://docs.rs#1989)    #[test]
[1990](https://docs.rs#1990)    fn emit_shims_output_compiles_under_rustc() {
[1991](https://docs.rs#1991)        // The load-bearing gate: the emitted shim is type/arity/ABI compile-
[1992](https://docs.rs#1992)        // checkable with NO C object (the extern symbol stays unresolved at lib
[1993](https://docs.rs#1993)        // build). Gated on rustc being spawnable so constrained CI skips it.
[1994](https://docs.rs#1994)        let out = emit_for("square_sum", vec![("x", Type::I64)], Type::I64).expect("emits");
[1995](https://docs.rs#1995)        assert!(

[1999](https://docs.rs#1999)    }
[2000](https://docs.rs#2000)
[2001](https://docs.rs#2001)    /// Build [driver-module-with-boundary, target-module-defining-symbol],
[2002](https://docs.rs#2002)    /// resolve `to_lang` from the exporting sibling, reconcile, and emit — the
[2003](https://docs.rs#2003)    /// generic shape behind the per-paradigm tests below.
[2004](https://docs.rs#2004)    fn emit_cross(
[2005](https://docs.rs#2005)        from: SourceLang,
[2006](https://docs.rs#2006)        target: SourceLang,
[2007](https://docs.rs#2007)        symbol: &str,
[2008](https://docs.rs#2008)    ) -> Result<String, FfiEmitError> {
[2009](https://docs.rs#2009)        let mut modules = vec![
[2010](https://docs.rs#2010)            module("driver", from, vec![boundary(from, target, symbol)]),
[2011](https://docs.rs#2011)            module_defining("target", target, symbol),
[2012](https://docs.rs#2012)        ];
[2013](https://docs.rs#2013)        resolve_boundary_to_langs(&mut modules);
[2014](https://docs.rs#2014)        assert_eq!(
[2015](https://docs.rs#2015)            modules[0].ffi_boundaries[0].to_lang, target,
[2016](https://docs.rs#2016)            "to_lang should resolve to the exporting sibling"
[2017](https://docs.rs#2017)        );
[2018](https://docs.rs#2018)        let manifest = FfiManifest::reconcile(&modules).expect("reconciles");
[2019](https://docs.rs#2019)        manifest.emit_rust_shims(&modules)
[2020](https://docs.rs#2020)    }

[2048](https://docs.rs#2048)    #[test]
[2049](https://docs.rs#2049)    fn emit_shims_cpp_boundary_emits_pybind11_shim() {
[2050](https://docs.rs#2050)        // PMAT-927: a Rust→C++ boundary now lowers to a real pybind11 shim (was
[2051](https://docs.rs#2051)        // an `Err(pybind11 gap)`). The C++ symbol is name-mangled, so the shim
[2052](https://docs.rs#2052)        // calls the pybind11-registered binding by its Python-visible name
[2053](https://docs.rs#2053)        // through the embedded interpreter — never a guessed `extern "C"`.
[2054](https://docs.rs#2054)        // `module_defining` exports `kernel` as a nullary `-> i64` in module
[2055](https://docs.rs#2055)        // "target"; from != to (Rust→Cpp) so reconcile keeps the boundary.
[2056](https://docs.rs#2056)        let out = emit_cross(SourceLang::Rust, SourceLang::Cpp, "kernel").expect("emits");
[2057](https://docs.rs#2057)        // No extern block / no unsafe in the EMITTED CODE: a mangled C++ symbol
[2058](https://docs.rs#2058)        // must NOT be declared as a flat C symbol (it would mis-link), and the
[2059](https://docs.rs#2059)        // honest path goes through pybind11. The doc-comment prose names both
[2060](https://docs.rs#2060)        // `extern "C"` and `unsafe` to explain WHY they are absent, so scan only
[2061](https://docs.rs#2061)        // non-comment lines for the actual tokens.
[2062](https://docs.rs#2062)        let code_only: String = out
[2063](https://docs.rs#2063)            .lines()
[2064](https://docs.rs#2064)            .filter(|l| !l.trim_start().starts_with("//") && !l.trim_start().starts_with("///"))
[2065](https://docs.rs#2065)            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
[2066](https://docs.rs#2066)            .join("\n");
[2067](https://docs.rs#2067)        assert!(
[2068](https://docs.rs#2068)            !code_only.contains("extern \"C\""),
[2069](https://docs.rs#2069)            "a name-mangled C++ symbol must not be declared extern \"C\": {out}"
[2070](https://docs.rs#2070)        );
[2071](https://docs.rs#2071)        assert!(
[2072](https://docs.rs#2072)            !code_only.contains("unsafe"),
[2073](https://docs.rs#2073)            "the pybind11 wrapper code is unsafe-free: {out}"
[2074](https://docs.rs#2074)        );
[2075](https://docs.rs#2075)        assert!(
[2076](https://docs.rs#2076)            out.contains("pub fn kernel_shim() -> i64 {"),
[2077](https://docs.rs#2077)            "nullary -> i64 pybind11 wrapper: {out}"
[2078](https://docs.rs#2078)        );
[2079](https://docs.rs#2079)        // Embeds the interpreter, imports the pybind11 EXTENSION module by name,
[2080](https://docs.rs#2080)        // and getattrs the Python-visible binding name (not a mangled symbol).
[2081](https://docs.rs#2081)        assert!(out.contains("::pyo3::Python::with_gil(|py|"), "{out}");
[2082](https://docs.rs#2082)        assert!(
[2083](https://docs.rs#2083)            out.contains("::pyo3::types::PyModule::import(py, \"target\")"),
[2084](https://docs.rs#2084)            "imports the pybind11 module by name: {out}"
[2085](https://docs.rs#2085)        );
[2086](https://docs.rs#2086)        assert!(out.contains(".getattr(\"kernel\")"), "{out}");
[2087](https://docs.rs#2087)        assert!(out.contains(".call1(())"), "0-arg call passes (): {out}");
[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)        assert!(
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)            out.contains(".extract().expect("),
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)            "non-Unit return is extracted: {out}"
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)        );
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)        // Honesty: the wrapper doc names the mangling reality + the pybind11 binding.
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)        assert!(
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)            out.contains("name-mangled") && out.contains("m.def"),
[2095](https://docs.rs#2095)            "shim must document the name-mangling reality + pybind11 binding: {out}"
[2096](https://docs.rs#2096)        );
[2097](https://docs.rs#2097)        // Capability-ahead-of-contract — no citation yet (C-FFI-PYBIND11-EMBED queued).
[2098](https://docs.rs#2098)        assert!(
[2099](https://docs.rs#2099)            !out.contains("xpile-contract:"),
[2100](https://docs.rs#2100)            "pybind11 embedding is capability-ahead-of-contract (no citation): {out}"
[2101](https://docs.rs#2101)        );
[2102](https://docs.rs#2102)    }

[2439](https://docs.rs#2439)    #[test]
[2440](https://docs.rs#2440)    fn emit_pyo3_shim_compiles_against_pyo3() {
[2441](https://docs.rs#2441)        // The load-bearing gate (mirrors the C arm's rustc compile gate, but for
[2442](https://docs.rs#2442)        // a real external dep): the emitted pyo3 shim must COMPILE against pyo3.
[2443](https://docs.rs#2443)        // pyo3 needs libpython at LINK time, but `cargo check` only TYPE-checks,
[2444](https://docs.rs#2444)        // so a Python *dev* install (headers via pyo3-build) suffices and no
[2445](https://docs.rs#2445)        // interpreter must run. Gated on cargo + a buildable pyo3 — skips
[2446](https://docs.rs#2446)        // gracefully (returns) when pyo3 cannot be built (offline / no python).
[2447](https://docs.rs#2447)        let out = emit_cross(SourceLang::Rust, SourceLang::Python, "embed").expect("emits");
[2448](https://docs.rs#2448)        pyo3_shim_checks(&out);
[2449](https://docs.rs#2449)    }
[2450](https://docs.rs#2450)
[2451](https://docs.rs#2451)    /// `cargo check` the emitted pyo3 shim as a tiny standalone crate that
[2452](https://docs.rs#2452)    /// depends on pyo3 (`auto-initialize` so no `Python::initialize` boilerplate
[2453](https://docs.rs#2453)    /// is needed for a type-check). Skips (returns) gracefully if `cargo` is
[2454](https://docs.rs#2454)    /// absent or pyo3 cannot be resolved/built (offline CI / no Python dev
[2455](https://docs.rs#2455)    /// headers) — the structural string assertions above always run; this adds
[2456](https://docs.rs#2456)    /// the real-compiler gate when the toolchain is present.
[2457](https://docs.rs#2457)    fn pyo3_shim_checks(shim: &str) {
[2458](https://docs.rs#2458)        if std::process::Command::new("cargo")
[2459](https://docs.rs#2459)            .arg("--version")
[2460](https://docs.rs#2460)            .output()
[2461](https://docs.rs#2461)            .is_err()
[2462](https://docs.rs#2462)        {
[2463](https://docs.rs#2463)            eprintln!("cargo unavailable — skipping pyo3 compile gate");
[2464](https://docs.rs#2464)            return;
[2465](https://docs.rs#2465)        }
[2466](https://docs.rs#2466)        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
[2467](https://docs.rs#2467)            "xpile_pyo3_gate_{}_{:?}",
[2468](https://docs.rs#2468)            std::process::id(),
[2469](https://docs.rs#2469)            std::thread::current().id()
[2470](https://docs.rs#2470)        ));
[2471](https://docs.rs#2471)        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
[2472](https://docs.rs#2472)        if std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("src")).is_err() {
[2473](https://docs.rs#2473)            eprintln!("temp dir unavailable — skipping pyo3 compile gate");
[2474](https://docs.rs#2474)            return;
[2475](https://docs.rs#2475)        }
[2476](https://docs.rs#2476)        // pyo3 0.23 — pinned minor so the emitted `PyModule::import`/`call1`/
[2477](https://docs.rs#2477)        // `extract` API surface is stable. `auto-initialize` lets a type-check
[2478](https://docs.rs#2478)        // proceed without an explicit interpreter init.
[2479](https://docs.rs#2479)        std::fs::write(
[2480](https://docs.rs#2480)            dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
[2481](https://docs.rs#2481)            "[package]\nname = \"xpile-pyo3-gate\"\nversion = \"0.0.0\"\nedition = \"2021\"\n\n[dependencies]\npyo3 = { version = \"0.23\", features = [\"auto-initialize\"] }\n",
[2482](https://docs.rs#2482)        )
[2483](https://docs.rs#2483)        .expect("write Cargo.toml");
[2484](https://docs.rs#2484)        std::fs::write(dir.join("src").join("lib.rs"), shim).expect("write shim");
[2485](https://docs.rs#2485)        let out = std::process::Command::new("cargo")
[2486](https://docs.rs#2486)            .current_dir(&dir)
[2487](https://docs.rs#2487)            .arg("check")
[2488](https://docs.rs#2488)            .arg("--target-dir")
[2489](https://docs.rs#2489)            .arg(dir.join("target"))
[2490](https://docs.rs#2490)            .output();
[2491](https://docs.rs#2491)        match out {
[2492](https://docs.rs#2492)            Ok(o) if o.status.success() => {}
[2493](https://docs.rs#2493)            Ok(o) => {
[2494](https://docs.rs#2494)                let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stderr);
[2495](https://docs.rs#2495)                // A pyo3/libpython *resolution or build* failure (no Python dev
[2496](https://docs.rs#2496)                // env, offline) is a SKIP, not a test failure — the structural
[2497](https://docs.rs#2497)                // assertions already validated the shim shape. Only a genuine
[2498](https://docs.rs#2498)                // type error in OUR emitted code should fail. Heuristic: if the
[2499](https://docs.rs#2499)                // failure mentions one of our shim symbols (`_shim`) it's our bug;
[2500](https://docs.rs#2500)                // otherwise it's an environment/dep issue → skip.
[2501](https://docs.rs#2501)                if stderr.contains("error[") && stderr.contains("_shim") {
[2502](https://docs.rs#2502)                    panic!("emitted pyo3 shim failed to type-check:\n{stderr}");
[2503](https://docs.rs#2503)                }
[2504](https://docs.rs#2504)                eprintln!(
[2505](https://docs.rs#2505)                    "pyo3 could not be built (offline / no Python dev env) — skipping pyo3 compile gate"
[2506](https://docs.rs#2506)                );
[2507](https://docs.rs#2507)            }
[2508](https://docs.rs#2508)            Err(_) => eprintln!("cargo spawn failed — skipping pyo3 compile gate"),
[2509](https://docs.rs#2509)        }
[2510](https://docs.rs#2510)        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
[2511](https://docs.rs#2511)    }

[2659](https://docs.rs#2659)    #[test]
[2660](https://docs.rs#2660)    fn emit_shims_f32_boundary_maps_c_float() {
[2661](https://docs.rs#2661)        // PMAT-911: a C `float` boundary rides the DISTINCT 32-bit c_float
[2662](https://docs.rs#2662)        // ABI slot with an f32 wrapper — never widened through c_double.
[2663](https://docs.rs#2663)        // Compiles end-to-end under -D warnings on both editions.
[2664](https://docs.rs#2664)        let out = emit_for("scalef", vec![("x", Type::F32)], Type::F32).expect("emits");
[2665](https://docs.rs#2665)        assert!(
[2666](https://docs.rs#2666)            out.contains("fn scalef(x: ::std::os::raw::c_float) -> ::std::os::raw::c_float;"),
[2667](https://docs.rs#2667)            "float boundary must use c_float, not c_double:\n{out}"
[2668](https://docs.rs#2668)        );
[2669](https://docs.rs#2669)        assert!(out.contains("pub fn scalef_shim(x: f32) -> f32 {"));
[2670](https://docs.rs#2670)        assert!(out.contains("__r as f32"));
[2671](https://docs.rs#2671)        // The 32↔64 ABI honesty: an f32 boundary must NEVER widen to c_double.
[2672](https://docs.rs#2672)        let extern_block = out
[2673](https://docs.rs#2673)            .split("extern \"C\" {")
[2674](https://docs.rs#2674)            .nth(1)
[2675](https://docs.rs#2675)            .unwrap()
[2676](https://docs.rs#2676)            .split('}')
[2677](https://docs.rs#2677)            .next()
[2678](https://docs.rs#2678)            .unwrap();
[2679](https://docs.rs#2679)        assert!(
[2680](https://docs.rs#2680)            !extern_block.contains("c_double"),
[2681](https://docs.rs#2681)            "an F32 boundary must not widen to c_double:\n{extern_block}"
[2682](https://docs.rs#2682)        );
[2683](https://docs.rs#2683)        assert!(
[2684](https://docs.rs#2684)            rustc_lib_compiles("f32", &out),
[2685](https://docs.rs#2685)            "emitted f32 shim must compile under -D warnings"
[2686](https://docs.rs#2686)        );
[2687](https://docs.rs#2687)    }

# FfiEmitError in xpile_ffi_manifest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-ffi-manifest/0.1.615/xpile_ffi_manifest/struct.FfiEmitError.html

## Expand description

PMAT-899 (Sprint-2 Tier 2): a reconciled boundary could not be lowered to a
Rust FFI shim because a recovered parameter/return type has no ABI-honest C
mapping (a pointer/string/struct/container the first-cut emitter refuses
rather than mis-marshal). Mirrors [ FfiReconcileError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiReconcileError.html): surfacing the gap
beats emitting a wrong-ABI shim.

#### pub fn [reconcile](https://docs.rs#method.reconcile)(modules: &[[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)]) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[FfiManifest](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html), [FfiReconcileError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiReconcileError.html)>

Phase 2 of the hybrid transpile flow (`hybrid-transpile-flow.md` §16):
reconcile every cross-language FFI boundary across the dispatched modules
into a single manifest, or fail listing the unresolved boundaries.

A boundary `{from_lang, to_lang, symbol, signature}` is a call that
crosses from `from_lang` into `to_lang`. It RESOLVES when a sibling module
of `to_lang` is present in the dispatched set (the target language was
actually transpiled). Each resolved boundary becomes an [ FfiEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEntry.html) with a
deterministic

`shim_id`; any boundary whose target language is absent fails
reconciliation (the `manifest_completeness` invariant of
`C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT`). Same-language boundaries (`from == to`) are no-ops.PMAT-895: resolution is SYMBOL-LEVEL — a boundary resolves only when a
module of `to_lang` actually DEFINES an item (function/const) named
`symbol`. A target-language module that is present but does NOT export the
symbol still fails reconciliation (the `manifest_completeness` invariant is
about the symbol crossing the line, not just the language being present).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/xpile_ffi_manifest/lib.rs.html#304-391)#### pub fn [emit_rust_shims](https://docs.rs#method.emit_rust_shims)(
    &self,
    modules: &[[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)],
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [FfiEmitError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEmitError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/xpile_ffi_manifest/lib.rs.html#304-391)

#### pub fn [emit_rust_shims](https://docs.rs#method.emit_rust_shims)(
    &self,
    modules: &[[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)],
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [FfiEmitError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEmitError.html)>

PMAT-899 — Phase 4 of the hybrid flow (`hybrid-transpile-flow.md` §16):
emit a self-contained Rust FFI shim file for every reconciled
cross-language boundary, dispatched per target paradigm. `modules` is the
same set passed to [ reconcile](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html#method.reconcile) — it is the ONLY source
of real param/return types (an

[carries placeholder signatures).](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEntry.html)

`FfiEntry`Per-paradigm strategy (see [`shim_part_for`]):

- **C**→ a real- `extern "C"`foreign declaration + a safe- `*_shim`wrapper confining- `unsafe`, citing- `C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT`.
- **Shell**→ a real- `std::process::Command`-based wrapper (shell speaks argv + exit codes — no C ABI, no- `unsafe`), citing- `C-FFI-SHELL-SUBPROCESS`.
- **Ruchy / Rust**→ a real same-crate direct-call forwarder (both lower to native Rust in the same crate — a plain in-crate call, no- `unsafe`, no- `extern`).
- **Python**→ a real pyo3 CPython-embedding shim (PMAT-926): under the GIL it imports the defining module and calls the function, marshalling scalar args/return through pyo3 (- `i64`/- `f64`/- `bool`/- `String`).
- **Cpp**→ a real pybind11 C++ shim (PMAT-927): the C++ symbol is name-mangled, so this calls the pybind11-registered binding by its Python-visible name through the embedded interpreter (the same path Python uses), refusing rather than guessing a mangled- `extern "C"`. Six of seven arms are now real (C, Shell, Ruchy, Rust, Python, Cpp).
- **Cuda / Lean**→ a specific, mechanism-named- `FfiEmitError`

All-or-nothing (mirrors `reconcile`’s `manifest_completeness`): if ANY
boundary cannot be shimmed, nothing is emitted and the gaps are returned —
a half-shimmed hybrid build is not a build.

Compile-checkable WITHOUT the foreign object: a C extern symbol stays
unresolved at lib-build time and a shell shim needs no symbol at all, so
type/arity/ABI are validated by `rustc --crate-type lib` alone (linking is
only needed to *run*).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/xpile_ffi_manifest/lib.rs.html#407-447)#### pub fn [emit_hybrid_workspace](https://docs.rs#method.emit_hybrid_workspace)(

    rust_src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),

PMAT-901 — Phase 5a of the hybrid flow (`hybrid-transpile-flow.md` §16):
emit a self-contained, BUILDABLE Cargo workspace for the hybrid module.
Files: `Cargo.toml` (a bin crate); `build.rs` ([`HYBRID_BUILD_RS`] —
cc-compiles every `csrc/*.c` and links it); `csrc/<name>.c` (each C source
verbatim, from `c_sources`); `src/ffi_shims.rs` (the reconciled shims from
[ emit_rust_shims](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html#method.emit_rust_shims)); and

`src/main.rs` (`rust_src`,
the caller’s lowering of the non-C modules, plus `mod ffi_shims;`).`cargo build` on the result compiles the Rust side AND cc-compiles + links
the C side through the emitted `extern "C"` shim — the first *executing*
hybrid artifact (Phase 5a). `rust_src` is supplied by the caller (the rust
backend’s lowering of the entry module) so this crate stays codegen-free.
All-or-nothing: an unshimmable boundary fails via [ FfiEmitError](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiEmitError.html) before
anything is written past the shim step.

# defining_function in xpile_ffi_manifest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-ffi-manifest/0.1.615/xpile_ffi_manifest/fn.defining_function.html

## Expand description

Recover the real defining [ Function](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Function.html) for a reconciled entry, mirroring

[’s symbol/](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html#method.reconcile)

`FfiManifest::reconcile``to_lang` match. `reconcile` guarantees an
entry exists only when the symbol is defined, so a miss here is an internal
invariant violation (surfaced as an unsupported boundary by the caller).
The defining function for a reconciled boundary: the `Item::Function` named
`entry.symbol` in the module whose `source_lang` is `entry.to_lang`. Public so
the `--verify` flow (PMAT-902) can read the C callee’s param/return types to
build the CPython-side ctypes ABI binding for the differential reference.

# resolve_boundary_to_langs in xpile_ffi_manifest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-ffi-manifest/0.1.615/xpile_ffi_manifest/fn.resolve_boundary_to_langs.html

`pub fn resolve_boundary_to_langs(modules: &mut [`[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)])## Expand description

PMAT-898 (Sprint-2 Tier 2): resolve each module’s FFI-boundary `to_lang` from
the full dispatched module set. A single-file frontend can’t see its siblings,
so `depyler-frontend::detect_ffi_boundaries` records a PROVISIONAL `to_lang`
(C, the canonical CPython-extension shape) for every relative import. With the
whole `Vec<Module>` in hand (the `xpile hybrid` CLI), rewrite each boundary’s
`to_lang` to the `source_lang` of whichever sibling module actually DEFINES
the symbol. Consequences once `reconcile` runs:

- a relative import of a *Python*sibling becomes`Python → Python`, which reconcile drops via its same-language skip (NOT a false FFI boundary);
- a relative import of a *C*sibling stays`Python → C`and resolves;
- a symbol no module defines is left as-is, so reconcile reports it
unresolved (the `manifest_completeness`invariant of C-FFI-CPYTHON-EXT).

Call this BEFORE [ FfiManifest::reconcile](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html#method.reconcile).

---

# retype_float_ffi_sites in xpile_ffi_manifest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-ffi-manifest/0.1.615/xpile_ffi_manifest/fn.retype_float_ffi_sites.html

`pub fn retype_float_ffi_sites(manifest: &`[FfiManifest](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiManifest.html), modules: &mut [[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html)])## Expand description

PMAT-931 (HUNT correctness — the PMAT-930 `c_double` two-arg divergence):
after reconciliation, re-type the FFI call sites of every reconciled symbol
whose `to_lang` definition returns `Type::F64` so the float-repr path is
selected in the calling (Python) module.

The Python frontend lowers `app.py` BEFORE the C sibling is dispatched, so a
call to a `double`-returning C symbol is typed with the unknown-callee I64
default. That makes `print(scale2(...))` print a whole double as `10` (not
Python’s `10.0`) and `let r: float = scale2(...)` emit `let r: i64` (rustc
E0308). This walks each non-`to_lang` module and corrects those sites via
[ xpile_meta_hir::retype_ffi_float_call_sites](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/fn.retype_ffi_float_call_sites.html). Idempotent / no-op when no
reconciled symbol returns F64.

# xpile_contract_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/xpile-contract-backend/0.1.615/target-redirect/xpile_contract_backend/

## Expand description

ContractBackend trait — proof-lane rendering abstraction.

Renders parsed [ xpile_contracts::Contract](https://docs.rs/xpile-contracts/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_contracts/struct.Contract.html) into LaTeX (math +
theorem environments), Lean 4 theorem text (with

`@[xpile_contract]`
attribute carrying the verbatim contract ID), or mdBook.Architectural invariants codified in
`contracts/xpile-contract-backend-trait-v1.yaml`. The citation bridge
uses **format-native structured constructs** parseable by the host
elaborator/parser, NOT regex over body text. See
`docs/specifications/sub/contract-backend-trait.md` §“Citation bridge”.

Render a contract under the given config.

Invariants: deterministic per `(contract, config)`; every cited
contract ID is parseable from `primary` via the host format’s
structured parser (Lean elaborator, LaTeX label machinery,
mdBook preprocessor) — NOT regex over text.

# xpile-backend 0.1.615 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/xpile-backend/0.1.615

Backend trait — code-lane emission abstraction.

Every target language in xpile (Rust, Ruchy, PTX, WGSL, SPIR-V, Lean)
provides one type implementing [`Backend`]. The trait is intentionally
narrow: take meta-HIR and a config, return an [`Artifact`].

Sibling of `xpile-frontend::Frontend`. Architectural invariants
codified in `contracts/xpile-backend-trait-v1.yaml`.

---

# serde_json - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde_json/^1/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-json)Serde JSON

JSON is a ubiquitous open-standard format that uses human-readable text to transmit data objects consisting of key-value pairs.

```
{
    "name": "John Doe",
    "age": 43,
    "address": {
        "street": "10 Downing Street",
        "city": "London"
    },
    "phones": [
        "+44 1234567",
        "+44 2345678"
    ]
}
```
There are three common ways that you might find yourself needing to work with JSON data in Rust.

- **As text data.**An unprocessed string of JSON data that you receive on an HTTP endpoint, read from a file, or prepare to send to a remote server.
- **As an untyped or loosely typed representation.**Maybe you want to check that some JSON data is valid before passing it on, but without knowing the structure of what it contains. Or you want to do very basic manipulations like insert a key in a particular spot.
- **As a strongly typed Rust data structure.**When you expect all or most of your data to conform to a particular structure and want to get real work done without JSON’s loosey-goosey nature tripping you up.

Serde JSON provides efficient, flexible, safe ways of converting data between each of these representations.

[§](https://docs.rs#operating-on-untyped-json-values)Operating on untyped JSON values

Any valid JSON data can be manipulated in the following recursive enum
representation. This data structure is [ serde_json::Value](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html).

```
enum Value {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Number(Number),
    String(String),
    Array(Vec<Value>),
    Object(Map<String, Value>),
}
```
A string of JSON data can be parsed into a `serde_json::Value` by the
[ serde_json::from_str](https://docs.rs/fn.from_str.html) function. There is also

[for parsing from a byte slice](https://docs.rs/fn.from_slice.html)

`from_slice``&[u8]` and [for parsing from any](https://docs.rs/fn.from_reader.html)

`from_reader``io::Read` like a File or a TCP stream.```
use serde_json::{Result, Value};
fn untyped_example() -> Result<()> {
    // Some JSON input data as a &str. Maybe this comes from the user.
    let data = r#"
        {
            "name": "John Doe",
            "age": 43,
            "phones": [
                "+44 1234567",
                "+44 2345678"
            ]
        }"#;
    // Parse the string of data into serde_json::Value.
    let v: Value = serde_json::from_str(data)?;
    // Access parts of the data by indexing with square brackets.
    println!("Please call {} at the number {}", v["name"], v["phones"][0]);
    Ok(())
}
```
The result of square bracket indexing like `v["name"]` is a borrow of the
data at that index, so the type is `&Value`. A JSON map can be indexed with
string keys, while a JSON array can be indexed with integer keys. If the
type of the data is not right for the type with which it is being indexed,
or if a map does not contain the key being indexed, or if the index into a
vector is out of bounds, the returned element is `Value::Null`.

When a `Value` is printed, it is printed as a JSON string. So in the code
above, the output looks like `Please call "John Doe" at the number "+44 1234567"`. The quotation marks appear because `v["name"]` is a `&Value`
containing a JSON string and its JSON representation is `"John Doe"`.
Printing as a plain string without quotation marks involves converting from
a JSON string to a Rust string with [ as_str()](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html#method.as_str) or avoiding the use of

`Value` as described in the following section.The `Value` representation is sufficient for very basic tasks but can be
tedious to work with for anything more significant. Error handling is
verbose to implement correctly, for example imagine trying to detect the
presence of unrecognized fields in the input data. The compiler is powerless
to help you when you make a mistake, for example imagine typoing `v["name"]`
as `v["nmae"]` in one of the dozens of places it is used in your code.

[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-json-as-strongly-typed-data-structures)Parsing JSON as strongly typed data structures

Serde provides a powerful way of mapping JSON data into Rust data structures largely automatically.

```
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Result;
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Person {
    name: String,
    age: u8,
    phones: Vec<String>,
}
fn typed_example() -> Result<()> {
    // Some JSON input data as a &str. Maybe this comes from the user.
    let data = r#"
        {
            "name": "John Doe",
            "age": 43,
            "phones": [
                "+44 1234567",
                "+44 2345678"
            ]
        }"#;
    // Parse the string of data into a Person object. This is exactly the
    // same function as the one that produced serde_json::Value above, but
    // now we are asking it for a Person as output.
    let p: Person = serde_json::from_str(data)?;
    // Do things just like with any other Rust data structure.
    println!("Please call {} at the number {}", p.name, p.phones[0]);
    Ok(())
}
```
This is the same `serde_json::from_str` function as before, but this time we
assign the return value to a variable of type `Person` so Serde will
automatically interpret the input data as a `Person` and produce informative
error messages if the layout does not conform to what a `Person` is expected
to look like.

Any type that implements Serde’s `Deserialize` trait can be deserialized
this way. This includes built-in Rust standard library types like `Vec<T>`
and `HashMap<K, V>`, as well as any structs or enums annotated with
`#[derive(Deserialize)]`.

Once we have `p` of type `Person`, our IDE and the Rust compiler can help us
use it correctly like they do for any other Rust code. The IDE can
autocomplete field names to prevent typos, which was impossible in the
`serde_json::Value` representation. And the Rust compiler can check that
when we write `p.phones[0]`, then `p.phones` is guaranteed to be a
`Vec<String>` so indexing into it makes sense and produces a `String`.

[§](https://docs.rs#constructing-json-values)Constructing JSON values

Serde JSON provides a [ json! macro](https://docs.rs/macro.json.html) to build

`serde_json::Value`
objects with very natural JSON syntax.```
use serde_json::json;
fn main() {
    // The type of `john` is `serde_json::Value`
    let john = json!({
        "name": "John Doe",
        "age": 43,
        "phones": [
            "+44 1234567",
            "+44 2345678"
        ]
    });
    println!("first phone number: {}", john["phones"][0]);
    // Convert to a string of JSON and print it out
    println!("{}", john.to_string());
}
```
The `Value::to_string()` function converts a `serde_json::Value` into a
`String` of JSON text.

One neat thing about the `json!` macro is that variables and expressions can
be interpolated directly into the JSON value as you are building it. Serde
will check at compile time that the value you are interpolating is able to
be represented as JSON.

```
let full_name = "John Doe";
let age_last_year = 42;
// The type of `john` is `serde_json::Value`
let john = json!({
    "name": full_name,
    "age": age_last_year + 1,
    "phones": [
        format!("+44 {}", random_phone())
    ]
});
```
This is amazingly convenient, but we have the problem we had before with
`Value`: the IDE and Rust compiler cannot help us if we get it wrong. Serde
JSON provides a better way of serializing strongly-typed data structures
into JSON text.

[§](https://docs.rs#creating-json-by-serializing-data-structures)Creating JSON by serializing data structures

A data structure can be converted to a JSON string by
[ serde_json::to_string](https://docs.rs/fn.to_string.html). There is also

[which serializes to a](https://docs.rs/fn.to_vec.html)

`serde_json::to_vec``Vec<u8>` and
[which serializes to any](https://docs.rs/fn.to_writer.html)

`serde_json::to_writer``io::Write`
such as a File or a TCP stream.```
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Result;
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Address {
    street: String,
    city: String,
}
fn print_an_address() -> Result<()> {
    // Some data structure.
    let address = Address {
        street: "10 Downing Street".to_owned(),
        city: "London".to_owned(),
    };
    // Serialize it to a JSON string.
    let j = serde_json::to_string(&address)?;
    // Print, write to a file, or send to an HTTP server.
    println!("{}", j);
    Ok(())
}
```
Any type that implements Serde’s `Serialize` trait can be serialized this
way. This includes built-in Rust standard library types like `Vec<T>` and
`HashMap<K, V>`, as well as any structs or enums annotated with
`#[derive(Serialize)]`.

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

As long as there is a memory allocator, it is possible to use serde_json without the rest of the Rust standard library. Disable the default “std” feature and enable the “alloc” feature:

```
[dependencies]
serde_json = { version = "1.0", default-features = false, features = ["alloc"] }
```
For JSON support in Serde without a memory allocator, please see the
[ serde-json-core](https://github.com/rust-embedded-community/serde-json-core) crate.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- Deserialize JSON data to a Rust data structure.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- When serializing or deserializing JSON goes wrong.
- [map](https://docs.rs/map/index.html)
- A map of String to serde_json::Value.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)- `std`
- Serialize a Rust data structure into JSON data.
- [value](https://docs.rs/value/index.html)
- The Value enum, a loosely typed way of representing any valid JSON value.

- Construct a `serde_json::Value`from a JSON literal.

- Deserialize an instance of type `T`from a string of JSON text.

- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_string.html)- string - `std`
- Serialize the given data structure as a String of JSON.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_string_pretty.html)- string_ - pretty - `std`
- Serialize the given data structure as a pretty-printed String of JSON.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_value.html)- value
- Convert a `T`into`serde_json::Value`which is an enum that can represent any valid JSON data.
- [to_vec](https://docs.rs/fn.to_vec.html)- `std`
- Serialize the given data structure as a JSON byte vector.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_vec_pretty.html)- vec_ - pretty - `std`
- Serialize the given data structure as a pretty-printed JSON byte vector.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_writer.html)- writer - `std`
- Serialize the given data structure as JSON into the I/O stream.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_writer_pretty.html)- writer_ - pretty - `std`
- Serialize the given data structure as pretty-printed JSON into the I/O stream.

# xpile_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/xpile-backend/0.1.615/target-redirect/xpile_backend/

## Expand description

Backend trait — code-lane emission abstraction.

Every target language in xpile (Rust, Ruchy, PTX, WGSL, SPIR-V, Lean)
provides one type implementing [ Backend](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html). The trait is intentionally
narrow: take meta-HIR and a config, return an

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Artifact.html)

`Artifact`Sibling of `xpile-frontend::Frontend`. Architectural invariants
codified in `contracts/xpile-backend-trait-v1.yaml`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Artifact](https://docs.rs/struct.Artifact.html)
- Emitted artifact — primary source/IR text plus sidecar files plus the structural citation chain to Layer-5 compile contracts.
- [Backend](https://docs.rs/struct.BackendConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration passed to `Backend::lower`
- [Emitted](https://docs.rs/struct.EmittedText.html)- Text
- Plain text emitted by a single `TargetEmitter``Artifact``QuorumStatus`(that’s chosen by the wrapper).
- [Multi](https://docs.rs/struct.MultiEmitterBackend.html)- Emitter - Backend
- Multi-emitter backend wrapper. Composes a general emitter
(mandatory) + an optional specialist under a `QuorumPolicy``Backend``TranspileSession`.
- [ViaEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.ViaEntry.html)
- A single emitter entry from `compile_targets.via`in the YAML schema. Mirrors the structured-record form spec’d in`sub/layer5-multi-emitter-quorum.md`§“Contract YAML schema extension”.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Backend](https://docs.rs/enum.BackendError.html)- Error
- [Diff](https://docs.rs/enum.DiffExecResult.html)- Exec - Result
- Result of a `DiffExec`quorum policy execution. Two PTX (or WGSL/ SPIR-V) programs were run on test inputs; the engine compared their numerical outputs.
- [Emitter](https://docs.rs/enum.EmitterRole.html)- Role
- Role of a backend emitter within a multi-emitter quorum.
- [HwProfile](https://docs.rs/enum.HwProfile.html)
- Hardware profile for targets whose emission depends on hardware
capabilities (PTX `compute_capability`, WGSL feature set, SPIR-V version).
- [Profile](https://docs.rs/enum.Profile.html)
- Lowering profile — the two-mHIR asymmetric decision for Rust↔Ruchy.
- [Quorum](https://docs.rs/enum.QuorumPolicy.html)- Policy
- Policy for combining outputs when both General and Specialist
emitters fire on the same input. Configured per Layer-5 contract
via `compile_targets.quorum_policy`in the YAML.
- [Quorum](https://docs.rs/enum.QuorumStatus.html)- Status
- Status of a multi-emitter quorum vote, attached to an `Artifact`
- [Target](https://docs.rs/enum.Target.html)
- Target language a backend can emit.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Backend](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html)
- Code-lane emission trait. See `docs/specifications/sub/backend-trait.md`.
- [Diff](https://docs.rs/trait.DiffExecEngine.html)- Exec - Engine
- PMAT-486 (§30 Track 4): engine that executes two emitted programs on contract-fixture inputs and numerically compares the outputs within a tolerance — the Runtime-stratum half of the §29 quorum. The trait + hook land here (free CI); the real CUDA / Vulkan implementations (PMAT-488 / PMAT-490) run out-of-band on self-hosted GPU runners.
- [Target](https://docs.rs/trait.TargetEmitter.html)- Emitter
- Single-emitter trait — sub-trait of a multi-emitter backend.
One `TargetEmitter``MultiEmitterBackend`

[55](https://docs.rs#55)    ForjarYaml,

[95](https://docs.rs#95)/// Emitted artifact — primary source/IR text plus sidecar files plus
[96](https://docs.rs#96)/// the structural citation chain to Layer-5 compile contracts.
[97](https://docs.rs#97)///
[98](https://docs.rs#98)/// The `citations` field is the structural channel that closes the
[99](https://docs.rs#99)/// audit chain: every target-specific IR construct in `primary` cites
[100](https://docs.rs#100)/// a Layer-5 compile contract by ID. Recovery is via this field, NOT
[101](https://docs.rs#101)/// via regex over `primary` text. See
[102](https://docs.rs#102)/// `contracts/xpile-backend-trait-v1.yaml` equation `compile_contract_citation`.
[103](https://docs.rs#103)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[104](https://docs.rs#104)pub struct Artifact {

[108](https://docs.rs#108)    /// Optional binaries, manifests, debug maps, accompanying the primary.
[109](https://docs.rs#109)    pub sidecars: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>,
[110](https://docs.rs#110)    /// Layer-5 compile contracts sanctioning every target-specific
[111](https://docs.rs#111)    /// construct in `primary`. Structural — not regex-recoverable.
[112](https://docs.rs#112)    pub citations: Vec<ContractId>,
[113](https://docs.rs#113)    /// Multi-emitter quorum status (PMAT-262 / Section 29). At v0.1.0
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    /// every Backend impl emits exactly one artifact, so this is always
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    /// `QuorumStatus::Single { emitter: <backend_name> }`. Multi-emitter
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    /// backends (future rustc_codegen_nvvm + aprender-gpu quorum on PTX)
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    /// populate `QuorumStatus::Multi { ... }` with the diff_exec result.
[118](https://docs.rs#118)    ///
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    /// Defaults via serde to `Single { emitter: "unknown" }` for
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    /// backward-compatible deserialization of older JSON payloads.
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    #[serde(default = "default_quorum_status")]
[122](https://docs.rs#122)    pub quorum_status: QuorumStatus,
[123](https://docs.rs#123)}

[126](https://docs.rs#126)    QuorumStatus::Single {
[127](https://docs.rs#127)        emitter: "unknown".to_string(),
[128](https://docs.rs#128)    }

[168](https://docs.rs#168)/// Role of a backend emitter within a multi-emitter quorum.
[169](https://docs.rs#169)///
[170](https://docs.rs#170)/// `compile_targets.via.role` in the YAML schema corresponds to this
[171](https://docs.rs#171)/// enum. At most one `General` per quorum (the mandatory fallback);
[172](https://docs.rs#172)/// any number of `Specialist` (each with its own `shape_filter`).
[173](https://docs.rs#173)#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[174](https://docs.rs#174)#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
[175](https://docs.rs#175)pub enum EmitterRole {
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    /// Handles any contract-conforming input. Mandatory fallback —
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    /// `pv lint` (post-PMAT-262) will require at least one `General`
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    /// emitter per Layer-5 contract's `compile_targets.via`.
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    /// Examples: `rustc_codegen_nvvm` (PTX), `naga` (WGSL),
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    /// `rspirv` (SPIR-V).
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    General,
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    /// Handles a domain-specific subset via hand-tuned templates.
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    /// Optional — degrades gracefully to single-emitter when missing.
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    /// Examples: `aprender-gpu` (GEMM/MMA PTX kernels),
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    /// `bashrs-realistic` (corpus-tuned POSIX patterns).
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    Specialist,
[187](https://docs.rs#187)}
[188](https://docs.rs#188)
[189](https://docs.rs#189)/// Policy for combining outputs when both General and Specialist
[190](https://docs.rs#190)/// emitters fire on the same input. Configured per Layer-5 contract
[191](https://docs.rs#191)/// via `compile_targets.quorum_policy` in the YAML.
[192](https://docs.rs#192)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[193](https://docs.rs#193)#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case", tag = "kind")]
[194](https://docs.rs#194)pub enum QuorumPolicy {
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    /// If the specialist handles the kernel, use its output. Falls
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    /// back to general otherwise. Single-vote Runtime stratum.
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    PreferSpecialist,
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    /// Emit via BOTH, run BOTH on test inputs, compare numerical
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// outputs within tolerance. Multi-vote Runtime stratum.
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// **Falsifies the contract on divergence** — this is the
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// stratum-upgrading policy that closes the §4 "Run=1 demo
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    /// fixture" caveat from audit-design.md.
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    DiffExec {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)        /// Maximum allowed absolute difference between corresponding
[205](https://docs.rs#205)        /// numerical outputs of the two emitters.
[206](https://docs.rs#206)        tolerance: f64,
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    },
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    /// Strict text-equality between PTX outputs. Useful for
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    /// regression-locking, NOT for falsification — different valid
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    /// PTX programs commonly produce identical execution results via
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    /// different instruction sequences.
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    Strict,
[213](https://docs.rs#213)}
[214](https://docs.rs#214)
[215](https://docs.rs#215)/// Status of a multi-emitter quorum vote, attached to an [`Artifact`]
[216](https://docs.rs#216)/// produced by a multi-emitter backend.
[217](https://docs.rs#217)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[218](https://docs.rs#218)#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
[219](https://docs.rs#219)pub enum QuorumStatus {
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    /// Only one emitter fired (specialist missing for this shape, or
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    /// quorum policy is `PreferSpecialist` and specialist matched).
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// Runtime stratum vote count: 1.
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    Single { emitter: String },
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    /// Both emitters fired; outputs were combined under the policy.
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// Runtime stratum vote count: 2.
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    Multi {
[227](https://docs.rs#227)        emitters: Vec<String>,
[228](https://docs.rs#228)        diff_exec: Option<DiffExecResult>,
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    },
[230](https://docs.rs#230)}
[231](https://docs.rs#231)
[232](https://docs.rs#232)/// Result of a `DiffExec` quorum policy execution. Two PTX (or WGSL/
[233](https://docs.rs#233)/// SPIR-V) programs were run on test inputs; the engine compared
[234](https://docs.rs#234)/// their numerical outputs.
[235](https://docs.rs#235)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[236](https://docs.rs#236)#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
[237](https://docs.rs#237)pub enum DiffExecResult {
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    /// Outputs matched within tolerance. Records the max absolute
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    /// difference observed for audit trail.
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    Match { max_abs_diff: f64 },
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    /// Outputs diverged beyond tolerance. **Contract violation** —
[242](https://docs.rs#242)    /// CI fails. Records the divergence for diagnosis.
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    Divergent { max_abs_diff: f64, tolerance: f64 },
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    /// Engine did not run (e.g., test hardware unavailable). Vote
[245](https://docs.rs#245)    /// downgrades from Runtime to a placeholder. The substrate
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    /// records this rather than silently dropping it.
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    NotRun { reason: String },
[248](https://docs.rs#248)}
[249](https://docs.rs#249)
[250](https://docs.rs#250)/// A single emitter entry from `compile_targets.via` in the YAML

[253](https://docs.rs#253)///
[254](https://docs.rs#254)/// At v0.1.0 the YAML schema is still a flat `[String]`; this struct
[255](https://docs.rs#255)/// is the v0.2.0+ target representation `pv lint` will deserialize.
[256](https://docs.rs#256)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[257](https://docs.rs#257)pub struct ViaEntry {

[260](https://docs.rs#260)    /// Role within the quorum.
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    pub role: EmitterRole,

[263](https://docs.rs#263)    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    pub crate_name: Option<String>,

[268](https://docs.rs#268)    pub cross_repo: Option<String>,
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// Optional shape filter — for specialists, identifies which

[273](https://docs.rs#273)    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    pub shape_filter: Option<String>,
