[277](https://docs.rs#277)// ─── PMAT-263 / Section 29: TargetEmitter trait + MultiEmitterBackend ────
[278](https://docs.rs#278)//
[279](https://docs.rs#279)// Routing layer for multi-emitter backends. A [`MultiEmitterBackend`]
[280](https://docs.rs#280)// composes a general emitter (mandatory fallback) + an optional
[281](https://docs.rs#281)// specialist emitter under a [`QuorumPolicy`]. Single-emitter and
[282](https://docs.rs#282)// multi-emitter cases produce explicit `QuorumStatus` on the emitted
[283](https://docs.rs#283)// [`Artifact`].
[284](https://docs.rs#284)
[285](https://docs.rs#285)/// Plain text emitted by a single [`TargetEmitter`] before the
[286](https://docs.rs#286)/// multi-emitter routing decides what to put in the final [`Artifact`].
[287](https://docs.rs#287)/// Doesn't carry `QuorumStatus` (that's chosen by the wrapper).
[288](https://docs.rs#288)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[289](https://docs.rs#289)pub struct EmittedText {
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    pub primary: String,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    pub citations: Vec<ContractId>,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)}
[294](https://docs.rs#294)
[295](https://docs.rs#295)/// Single-emitter trait — sub-trait of a multi-emitter backend.
[296](https://docs.rs#296)/// One [`TargetEmitter`] handles emission for one logical path
[297](https://docs.rs#297)/// (general vs specialist). Each [`MultiEmitterBackend`] wraps
[298](https://docs.rs#298)/// one mandatory general emitter and optionally one specialist.
[299](https://docs.rs#299)pub trait TargetEmitter: Send + Sync {
[300](https://docs.rs#300)    /// Human-readable emitter name (used in [`QuorumStatus`]).
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    fn name(&self) -> &str;
[302](https://docs.rs#302)
[303](https://docs.rs#303)    /// Attempt to emit for this input. Specialists return `None`
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    /// when their shape filter doesn't match — the wrapper then
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    /// uses only the general emitter. General emitters should
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    /// always return `Some(...)` for any contract-conforming input.
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    fn try_emit(
[308](https://docs.rs#308)        &self,
[309](https://docs.rs#309)        module: &Module,
[310](https://docs.rs#310)        config: &BackendConfig,
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    ) -> Option<Result<EmittedText, BackendError>>;
[312](https://docs.rs#312)}
[313](https://docs.rs#313)
[314](https://docs.rs#314)/// PMAT-486 (§30 Track 4): engine that executes two emitted programs on
[315](https://docs.rs#315)/// contract-fixture inputs and numerically compares the outputs within a
[316](https://docs.rs#316)/// tolerance — the Runtime-stratum half of the §29 quorum. The trait +
[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// hook land here (free CI); the real CUDA / Vulkan implementations
[318](https://docs.rs#318)/// (PMAT-488 / PMAT-490) run out-of-band on self-hosted GPU runners.
[319](https://docs.rs#319)///
[320](https://docs.rs#320)/// Error posture (per the §30 Track-4 review): with **no engine
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// installed** the `DiffExec` policy records `NotRun { reason: no-engine }`
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// (benign — free CI stays green). An **installed** engine that returns
[323](https://docs.rs#323)/// `Err` propagates a hard [`BackendError`] that fails the job — a broken
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// GPU run must NOT masquerade as "not run".
[325](https://docs.rs#325)pub trait DiffExecEngine: Send + Sync {
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    /// Execute `general_text` and `specialist_text` on the contract's
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    /// fixture inputs and compare. `Ok(Match|Divergent)` records the
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    /// vote; `Err(msg)` is a hard failure (e.g. driver fault / launch
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    /// error) the caller turns into a `BackendError`.
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    fn execute_and_compare(
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        &self,
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        general_text: &str,
[333](https://docs.rs#333)        specialist_text: &str,
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        module: &Module,
[335](https://docs.rs#335)        config: &BackendConfig,
[336](https://docs.rs#336)        tolerance: f64,
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    ) -> Result<DiffExecResult, String>;
[338](https://docs.rs#338)}
[339](https://docs.rs#339)
[340](https://docs.rs#340)/// Multi-emitter backend wrapper. Composes a general emitter
[341](https://docs.rs#341)/// (mandatory) + an optional specialist under a [`QuorumPolicy`].
[342](https://docs.rs#342)/// Implements [`Backend`] so it slots into the existing dispatch
[343](https://docs.rs#343)/// without touching `TranspileSession`.
[344](https://docs.rs#344)pub struct MultiEmitterBackend {
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    /// Single target this multi-emitter backend serves
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    /// (e.g., [`Target::Ptx`]).
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    pub target: Target,
[348](https://docs.rs#348)    /// Mandatory general emitter. Must handle any
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    /// contract-conforming input as a fallback.
[350](https://docs.rs#350)    pub general: Box<dyn TargetEmitter>,
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    /// Optional specialist emitter. Returns `None` from `try_emit`
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    /// when its shape filter doesn't match the input.
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    pub specialist: Option<Box<dyn TargetEmitter>>,
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    /// How to combine outputs when both emitters fire.
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    pub quorum_policy: QuorumPolicy,
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    /// PMAT-486: optional `DiffExec` execution engine. `None` (the
[357](https://docs.rs#357)    /// default) records `NotRun { no-engine }` under `QuorumPolicy::
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    /// DiffExec`; `Some(engine)` runs the Runtime-stratum comparison.
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    pub diff_exec_engine: Option<std::sync::Arc<dyn DiffExecEngine>>,
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    /// PMAT-1006: names of ADDITIONAL categorically-independent emitters the
[361](https://docs.rs#361)    /// installed `DiffExec` engine runs INTERNALLY beyond `general`+`specialist`
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    /// (e.g. the PTX §29 3-way quorum's `rustc-nvptx` arm, self-generated inside
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    /// the engine). When the engine reports a `Match`/`Divergent` (i.e. it
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    /// actually executed), these are appended to the reported `emitters` list so
[365](https://docs.rs#365)    /// `QuorumStatus::Multi` HONESTLY names every toolchain that voted. Empty for
[366](https://docs.rs#366)    /// every other backend (no behaviour change).
[367](https://docs.rs#367)    pub diff_exec_extra_emitters: Vec<String>,
[368](https://docs.rs#368)}
[369](https://docs.rs#369)
[370](https://docs.rs#370)impl MultiEmitterBackend {
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    pub fn new_single(target: Target, general: Box<dyn TargetEmitter>) -> Self {
[372](https://docs.rs#372)        Self {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)            target,
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            general,
[375](https://docs.rs#375)            specialist: None,
[376](https://docs.rs#376)            quorum_policy: QuorumPolicy::PreferSpecialist,
[377](https://docs.rs#377)            diff_exec_engine: None,
[378](https://docs.rs#378)            diff_exec_extra_emitters: Vec::new(),
[379](https://docs.rs#379)        }
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    }
[381](https://docs.rs#381)
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    pub fn new_with_specialist(
[383](https://docs.rs#383)        target: Target,
[384](https://docs.rs#384)        general: Box<dyn TargetEmitter>,
[385](https://docs.rs#385)        specialist: Box<dyn TargetEmitter>,
[386](https://docs.rs#386)        quorum_policy: QuorumPolicy,
[387](https://docs.rs#387)    ) -> Self {
[388](https://docs.rs#388)        Self {
[389](https://docs.rs#389)            target,
[390](https://docs.rs#390)            general,
[391](https://docs.rs#391)            specialist: Some(specialist),
[392](https://docs.rs#392)            quorum_policy,
[393](https://docs.rs#393)            diff_exec_engine: None,
[394](https://docs.rs#394)            diff_exec_extra_emitters: Vec::new(),
[395](https://docs.rs#395)        }
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    }
[397](https://docs.rs#397)
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    /// PMAT-486: install a `DiffExec` engine (builder style). The real
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    /// CUDA / Vulkan engines (PMAT-488 / PMAT-490) plug in here on the
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// self-hosted GPU runners; on free CI the engine stays `None`.
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    pub fn with_diff_exec_engine(mut self, engine: std::sync::Arc<dyn DiffExecEngine>) -> Self {
[402](https://docs.rs#402)        self.diff_exec_engine = Some(engine);
[403](https://docs.rs#403)        self
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// PMAT-1006: declare additional emitters the installed `DiffExec` engine
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    /// runs internally (beyond general+specialist), so an EXECUTED `Multi`
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    /// result names every toolchain that voted (the PTX 3-way §29 quorum).
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    pub fn with_diff_exec_extra_emitters(mut self, names: Vec<String>) -> Self {
[410](https://docs.rs#410)        self.diff_exec_extra_emitters = names;
[411](https://docs.rs#411)        self
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    }
[413](https://docs.rs#413)}
[414](https://docs.rs#414)
[415](https://docs.rs#415)impl Backend for MultiEmitterBackend {
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        // The wrapper name is generic; per-emitter names live in
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        // QuorumStatus on each emitted Artifact for audit recovery.
[419](https://docs.rs#419)        "multi-emitter"
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    }
[421](https://docs.rs#421)
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    fn targets(&self) -> &[Target] {
[423](https://docs.rs#423)        std::slice::from_ref(&self.target)
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    }
[425](https://docs.rs#425)
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    fn lower(&self, module: &Module, config: &BackendConfig) -> Result<Artifact, BackendError> {
[427](https://docs.rs#427)        let general_result = self.general.try_emit(module, config).ok_or_else(|| {
[428](https://docs.rs#428)            BackendError::Lower(format!(
[429](https://docs.rs#429)                "general emitter {} must always match contract-conforming input",
[430](https://docs.rs#430)                self.general.name()
[431](https://docs.rs#431)            ))
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        })??;
[433](https://docs.rs#433)
[434](https://docs.rs#434)        let specialist_result = self.specialist.as_ref().and_then(|s| {
[435](https://docs.rs#435)            s.try_emit(module, config)
[436](https://docs.rs#436)                .map(|r| (s.name().to_string(), r))
[437](https://docs.rs#437)        });
[438](https://docs.rs#438)
[439](https://docs.rs#439)        match specialist_result {
[440](https://docs.rs#440)            None => {
[441](https://docs.rs#441)                // Only general fired — Single-vote Runtime stratum.
[442](https://docs.rs#442)                Ok(Artifact {
[443](https://docs.rs#443)                    primary: general_result.primary,
[444](https://docs.rs#444)                    sidecars: Vec::new(),
[445](https://docs.rs#445)                    citations: general_result.citations,
[446](https://docs.rs#446)                    quorum_status: QuorumStatus::Single {
[447](https://docs.rs#447)                        emitter: self.general.name().to_string(),
[448](https://docs.rs#448)                    },
[449](https://docs.rs#449)                })
[450](https://docs.rs#450)            }
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            Some((specialist_name, specialist_emit)) => {
[452](https://docs.rs#452)                let specialist_text = specialist_emit?;
[453](https://docs.rs#453)                match &self.quorum_policy {
[454](https://docs.rs#454)                    QuorumPolicy::PreferSpecialist => {
[455](https://docs.rs#455)                        // Use specialist's output; general was emitted for
[456](https://docs.rs#456)                        // sanity but isn't reported as a vote.
[457](https://docs.rs#457)                        Ok(Artifact {
[458](https://docs.rs#458)                            primary: specialist_text.primary,
[459](https://docs.rs#459)                            sidecars: Vec::new(),
[460](https://docs.rs#460)                            citations: specialist_text.citations,
[461](https://docs.rs#461)                            quorum_status: QuorumStatus::Single {
[462](https://docs.rs#462)                                emitter: specialist_name,
[463](https://docs.rs#463)                            },
[464](https://docs.rs#464)                        })
[465](https://docs.rs#465)                    }
[466](https://docs.rs#466)                    QuorumPolicy::Strict => {
[467](https://docs.rs#467)                        // Text-equality check.
[468](https://docs.rs#468)                        let diff_exec = if general_result.primary == specialist_text.primary {
[469](https://docs.rs#469)                            Some(DiffExecResult::Match { max_abs_diff: 0.0 })
[470](https://docs.rs#470)                        } else {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)                            Some(DiffExecResult::Divergent {
[472](https://docs.rs#472)                                max_abs_diff: f64::INFINITY,
[473](https://docs.rs#473)                                tolerance: 0.0,
[474](https://docs.rs#474)                            })
[475](https://docs.rs#475)                        };
[476](https://docs.rs#476)                        Ok(Artifact {
[477](https://docs.rs#477)                            primary: general_result.primary.clone(),
[478](https://docs.rs#478)                            sidecars: vec![(
[479](https://docs.rs#479)                                "specialist_emission".to_string(),
[480](https://docs.rs#480)                                specialist_text.primary.into_bytes(),
[481](https://docs.rs#481)                            )],
[482](https://docs.rs#482)                            citations: general_result.citations,
[483](https://docs.rs#483)                            quorum_status: QuorumStatus::Multi {
[484](https://docs.rs#484)                                emitters: vec![self.general.name().to_string(), specialist_name],
[485](https://docs.rs#485)                                diff_exec,
[486](https://docs.rs#486)                            },
[487](https://docs.rs#487)                        })
[488](https://docs.rs#488)                    }
[489](https://docs.rs#489)                    QuorumPolicy::DiffExec { tolerance } => {
[490](https://docs.rs#490)                        // PMAT-486: run the installed engine, or record
[491](https://docs.rs#491)                        // NotRun{no-engine} when none is installed (free
[492](https://docs.rs#492)                        // CI). An installed engine that errors propagates
[493](https://docs.rs#493)                        // a hard BackendError — a broken GPU run must NOT
[494](https://docs.rs#494)                        // masquerade as "not run".
[495](https://docs.rs#495)                        let diff_exec = match &self.diff_exec_engine {
[496](https://docs.rs#496)                            Some(engine) => engine
[497](https://docs.rs#497)                                .execute_and_compare(
[498](https://docs.rs#498)                                    &general_result.primary,
[499](https://docs.rs#499)                                    &specialist_text.primary,
[500](https://docs.rs#500)                                    module,
[501](https://docs.rs#501)                                    config,
[502](https://docs.rs#502)                                    *tolerance,
[503](https://docs.rs#503)                                )
[504](https://docs.rs#504)                                .map_err(|e| {
[505](https://docs.rs#505)                                    BackendError::Lower(format!(
[506](https://docs.rs#506)                                        "DiffExec engine for {:?} failed: {e}",
[507](https://docs.rs#507)                                        self.target
[508](https://docs.rs#508)                                    ))
[509](https://docs.rs#509)                                })?,
[510](https://docs.rs#510)                            None => DiffExecResult::NotRun {
[511](https://docs.rs#511)                                reason: format!(
[512](https://docs.rs#512)                                    "no DiffExec engine installed (tolerance was {tolerance})"
[513](https://docs.rs#513)                                ),
[514](https://docs.rs#514)                            },
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                        };
[516](https://docs.rs#516)                        // PMAT-1006: the base voters are general + specialist.
[517](https://docs.rs#517)                        // When the engine actually EXECUTED (Match/Divergent, not
[518](https://docs.rs#518)                        // NotRun), append the extra toolchains it ran internally
[519](https://docs.rs#519)                        // (e.g. the PTX 3-way `rustc-nvptx` arm) so the reported
[520](https://docs.rs#520)                        // quorum HONESTLY names every voter. A non-executed run
[521](https://docs.rs#521)                        // (NotRun, no GPU) reports only the emitters that fired.
[522](https://docs.rs#522)                        let mut emitters = vec![self.general.name().to_string(), specialist_name];
[523](https://docs.rs#523)                        if matches!(
[524](https://docs.rs#524)                            diff_exec,
[525](https://docs.rs#525)                            DiffExecResult::Match { .. } | DiffExecResult::Divergent { .. }
[526](https://docs.rs#526)                        ) {
[527](https://docs.rs#527)                            emitters.extend(self.diff_exec_extra_emitters.iter().cloned());
[528](https://docs.rs#528)                        }
[529](https://docs.rs#529)                        Ok(Artifact {
[530](https://docs.rs#530)                            primary: general_result.primary.clone(),
[531](https://docs.rs#531)                            sidecars: vec![(
[532](https://docs.rs#532)                                "specialist_emission".to_string(),
[533](https://docs.rs#533)                                specialist_text.primary.into_bytes(),
[534](https://docs.rs#534)                            )],
[535](https://docs.rs#535)                            citations: general_result.citations,
[536](https://docs.rs#536)                            quorum_status: QuorumStatus::Multi {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)                                emitters,
[538](https://docs.rs#538)                                diff_exec: Some(diff_exec),
[539](https://docs.rs#539)                            },
[540](https://docs.rs#540)                        })
[541](https://docs.rs#541)                    }
[542](https://docs.rs#542)                }
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            }
[544](https://docs.rs#544)        }
[545](https://docs.rs#545)    }
[546](https://docs.rs#546)}

[974](https://docs.rs#974)    #[test]
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    fn strict_divergence_preserves_general_citations_not_specialist() {
[976](https://docs.rs#976)        // Security invariant: under `Strict`, citations come from
[977](https://docs.rs#977)        // `general`. The proof lane relies on this — citations identify
[978](https://docs.rs#978)        // which contracts the artifact was authored against. A
[979](https://docs.rs#979)        // specialist that disagrees with general must not be able to
[980](https://docs.rs#980)        // silently swap its own citations into the audit trail.
[981](https://docs.rs#981)        let backend = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[982](https://docs.rs#982)            Target::Ptx,
[983](https://docs.rs#983)            Box::new(MockGeneralWithCitations {
[984](https://docs.rs#984)                body: "general output".into(),
[985](https://docs.rs#985)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-GENERAL-CITED")],
[986](https://docs.rs#986)            }),
[987](https://docs.rs#987)            Box::new(MockSpecialistWithCitations {
[988](https://docs.rs#988)                body: "different output".into(),
[989](https://docs.rs#989)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-SPECIALIST-CITED")],
[990](https://docs.rs#990)            }),
[991](https://docs.rs#991)            QuorumPolicy::Strict,
[992](https://docs.rs#992)        );
[993](https://docs.rs#993)        let artifact = backend.lower(&dummy_module(), &dummy_config()).unwrap();
[994](https://docs.rs#994)        assert_eq!(artifact.citations.len(), 1);
[995](https://docs.rs#995)        assert_eq!(artifact.citations[0].as_str(), "C-GENERAL-CITED");
[996](https://docs.rs#996)        // Specialist's body is still recoverable from the sidecar even
[997](https://docs.rs#997)        // though its citations are dropped.
[998](https://docs.rs#998)        assert_eq!(artifact.sidecars.len(), 1);
[999](https://docs.rs#999)        assert_eq!(
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)            artifact.sidecars[0].1,
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)            b"different output".to_vec(),
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)            "specialist body should be preserved in sidecar"
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)        );
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)    }

[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)    #[test]
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)    fn prefer_specialist_hides_divergence_by_design() {
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)        // Documented trade-off: `PreferSpecialist` is the
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)        // single-vote-runtime stratum — it intentionally does NOT
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)        // compare general vs specialist. Use `Strict` or `DiffExec`
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)        // when divergence detection matters. This test pins down the
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)        // behavior so a future "helpful" refactor can't accidentally
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)        // turn this into a quiet divergence detector.
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)        let backend = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)            Target::Ptx,
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)            Box::new(MockGeneralWithCitations {
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)                body: "general thinks the answer is 42".into(),
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-GENERAL")],
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)            }),
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)            Box::new(MockSpecialistWithCitations {
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)                body: "specialist thinks the answer is 99".into(),
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)                citations: vec![ContractId::new("C-SPECIALIST")],
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)            }),
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)            QuorumPolicy::PreferSpecialist,
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)        );
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)        let artifact = backend.lower(&dummy_module(), &dummy_config()).unwrap();
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)        // Specialist's body wins; specialist's citations win;
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)        // QuorumStatus reports Single (no divergence captured).
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)        assert!(artifact.primary.contains("99"));
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)        assert_eq!(artifact.citations[0].as_str(), "C-SPECIALIST");
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)        match artifact.quorum_status {
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)            QuorumStatus::Single { emitter } => {
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)                assert_eq!(emitter, "specialist-with-cites");
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)            }
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)            other => panic!("expected Single quorum status, got {other:?}"),
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)        }
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)        // No sidecar — general's emission isn't even captured.
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)        assert!(artifact.sidecars.is_empty());
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)    }

[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)    fn diff_exec_not_run_reason_records_tolerance_for_observability() {
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)        // The `NotRun` reason is the user-facing breadcrumb pointing
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)        // at "DiffExec engine not yet wired" — and it must carry the
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)        // configured tolerance so debug output is actionable.
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)        let backend = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)            Target::Ptx,
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)            Box::new(MockGeneral {
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)                name: "general",
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)                body: "g".into(),
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)            }),
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)            Box::new(MockSpecialist {
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)                name: "specialist",
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)                matches: true,
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)                body: "s".into(),
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)            }),
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)            QuorumPolicy::DiffExec { tolerance: 2.5e-4 },
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)        );
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)        let artifact = backend.lower(&dummy_module(), &dummy_config()).unwrap();
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)        match artifact.quorum_status {
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)            QuorumStatus::Multi {
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)                diff_exec: Some(DiffExecResult::NotRun { reason }),
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)                ..
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)            } => {
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)                assert!(
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)                    reason.contains("0.00025")
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)                        || reason.contains("2.5e-4")
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)                        || reason.contains("0.000250"),
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)                    "tolerance should appear in NotRun reason; got: {reason}"
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)                );
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)            }
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)            other => panic!("expected Multi NotRun status, got {other:?}"),
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)        }
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)    }
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)    #[test]
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)    fn diff_exec_does_not_short_circuit_on_text_equality() {
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)        // Architectural invariant: even when general and specialist
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)        // emit byte-identical text, `DiffExec` policy must still
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)        // record `NotRun` (because the real engine compares numerical
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)        // outputs after execution, not source text). A future
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)        // optimization that says "skip diff if text matches" would
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)        // break this invariant — the engine's job is to check the
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)        // RUNTIME behavior, and identical source could still produce
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)        // divergent runtime values on different hardware.
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)        let backend = MultiEmitterBackend::new_with_specialist(
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)            Target::Ptx,
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)            Box::new(MockGeneral {
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)                name: "general",
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)                body: "byte identical".into(),
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)            }),
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)            Box::new(MockSpecialist {
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)                name: "specialist",
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)                matches: true,
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)                body: "byte identical".into(),
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)            }),
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)            QuorumPolicy::DiffExec { tolerance: 1e-6 },
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)        );
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)        let artifact = backend.lower(&dummy_module(), &dummy_config()).unwrap();
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)        match artifact.quorum_status {
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)            QuorumStatus::Multi { diff_exec, .. } => {
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)                assert!(
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)                    matches!(diff_exec, Some(DiffExecResult::NotRun { .. })),
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)                    "DiffExec policy must NOT short-circuit on text equality \
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)                     — engine compares runtime values, not source text"
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)                );
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)            }
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)            other => panic!("expected Multi quorum status, got {other:?}"),
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)        }
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)    }

Lower a meta-HIR module under the given config to an [ Artifact](https://docs.rs/struct.Artifact.html).

Invariants: deterministic per `(module, config)`; frame-pure
(no mutation of inputs); every target-specific IR construct
in `Artifact.primary` cited via `Artifact.citations`.

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# Artifact in xpile_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/xpile_backend/struct.Artifact.html

```
pub struct Artifact {
    pub primary:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub sidecars: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>)>,
    pub citations: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[ContractId](https://docs.rs/xpile-contracts/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_contracts/struct.ContractId.html)>,
    pub quorum_status: [QuorumStatus](https://docs.rs/enum.QuorumStatus.html),
}## Expand description

Emitted artifact — primary source/IR text plus sidecar files plus the structural citation chain to Layer-5 compile contracts.

The `citations` field is the structural channel that closes the
audit chain: every target-specific IR construct in `primary` cites
a Layer-5 compile contract by ID. Recovery is via this field, NOT
via regex over `primary` text. See
`contracts/xpile-backend-trait-v1.yaml` equation `compile_contract_citation`.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.primary)

`primary: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Emitted source / IR text (Rust source, Ruchy source, PTX text, WGSL source, SPIR-V text, Lean source).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.sidecars)

`sidecars: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>)>Optional binaries, manifests, debug maps, accompanying the primary.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.citations)

`citations: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[ContractId](https://docs.rs/xpile-contracts/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_contracts/struct.ContractId.html)>Layer-5 compile contracts sanctioning every target-specific
construct in `primary`. Structural — not regex-recoverable.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.quorum_status)

`quorum_status: `[QuorumStatus](https://docs.rs/enum.QuorumStatus.html)Multi-emitter quorum status (PMAT-262 / Section 29). At v0.1.0
every Backend impl emits exactly one artifact, so this is always
`QuorumStatus::Single { emitter: <backend_name> }`. Multi-emitter
backends (future rustc_codegen_nvvm + aprender-gpu quorum on PTX)
populate `QuorumStatus::Multi { ... }` with the diff_exec result.

Defaults via serde to `Single { emitter: "unknown" }` for
backward-compatible deserialization of older JSON payloads.

the engine). When the engine reports a `Match`/`Divergent` (i.e. it

# QuorumPolicy in xpile_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/xpile_backend/enum.QuorumPolicy.html

```
pub enum QuorumPolicy {
    PreferSpecialist,
    DiffExec {
        tolerance:
```
[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    },
    Strict,
}## Expand description

Policy for combining outputs when both General and Specialist
emitters fire on the same input. Configured per Layer-5 contract
via `compile_targets.quorum_policy` in the YAML.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.PreferSpecialist)

### PreferSpecialist

If the specialist handles the kernel, use its output. Falls back to general otherwise. Single-vote Runtime stratum.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DiffExec)

### DiffExec

Emit via BOTH, run BOTH on test inputs, compare numerical
outputs within tolerance. Multi-vote Runtime stratum.
**Falsifies the contract on divergence** — this is the
stratum-upgrading policy that closes the §4 “Run=1 demo
fixture” caveat from audit-design.md.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Strict)

### Strict

Strict text-equality between PTX outputs. Useful for regression-locking, NOT for falsification — different valid PTX programs commonly produce identical execution results via different instruction sequences.

Result of a `DiffExec` quorum policy execution. Two PTX (or WGSL/
SPIR-V) programs were run on test inputs; the engine compared
their numerical outputs.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Match)

### Match

Outputs matched within tolerance. Records the max absolute difference observed for audit trail.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Divergent)

### Divergent

Outputs diverged beyond tolerance. **Contract violation** —
CI fails. Records the divergence for diagnosis.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NotRun)

### NotRun

Engine did not run (e.g., test hardware unavailable). Vote downgrades from Runtime to a placeholder. The substrate records this rather than silently dropping it.

# EmitterRole in xpile_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/xpile_backend/enum.EmitterRole.html

```
pub enum EmitterRole {
    General,
    Specialist,
}
```
## Expand description

Role of a backend emitter within a multi-emitter quorum.

`compile_targets.via.role` in the YAML schema corresponds to this
enum. At most one `General` per quorum (the mandatory fallback);
any number of `Specialist` (each with its own `shape_filter`).

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.General)

### General

Handles any contract-conforming input. Mandatory fallback —
`pv lint` (post-PMAT-262) will require at least one `General`
emitter per Layer-5 contract’s `compile_targets.via`.
Examples: `rustc_codegen_nvvm` (PTX), `naga` (WGSL),
`rspirv` (SPIR-V).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Specialist)

### Specialist

Handles a domain-specific subset via hand-tuned templates.
Optional — degrades gracefully to single-emitter when missing.
Examples: `aprender-gpu` (GEMM/MMA PTX kernels),
`bashrs-realistic` (corpus-tuned POSIX patterns).

# Target in xpile_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/xpile_backend/enum.Target.html

```
pub enum Target {
    Rust,
    Ruchy,
    Ptx,
    Wgsl,
    Spirv,
    Wasm,
    Lean,
    Shell,
    ForjarYaml,
}
```
## Expand description

Target language a backend can emit.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Rust)

### Rust

Idiomatic Rust source. Implemented by `xpile-rust-codegen`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Ruchy)

### Ruchy

Ruchy source. Implemented by `xpile-ruchy-codegen`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Ptx)

### Ptx

NVIDIA PTX text. Implemented by `xpile-ptx-codegen`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Wgsl)

### Wgsl

WebGPU Shading Language. Implemented by `xpile-wgsl-codegen`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Spirv)

### Spirv

SPIR-V — the native Vulkan IR. Implemented by `xpile-spirv-codegen`
(PMAT-960). REUSES the WGSL emission and compiles it WGSL→naga→spv
(NOT a hand-written SPIR-V assembler); the §29 cross-emitter witness
RUNS the emitted SPIR-V on a real wgpu Vulkan adapter. The native-IR
sibling of `Target::Wgsl`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Wasm)

### Wasm

WebAssembly Text format (WAT). Implemented by `xpile-wasm-codegen`.
The EMIT half of first-class bidirectional native WASM (PMAT-951) —
lowers the meta-HIR scalar/control subset directly to WAT text, NOT
via the Ruchy `WasmEmitter` hop. See `project-bidirectional-wasm`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Lean)

### Lean

Lean 4 executable code (def, partial def, inductive, …).
Implemented by `xpile-lean-codegen`. The proof-lane Lean (theorems)
goes through `xpile-lean-contract-backend` instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Shell)

### Shell

POSIX shell (sh / bash / zsh) — the bashrs merger domain.
Implemented by `bashrs-backend` (scaffold at v0.1.0; full emit
at v0.2.0 once the bashrs source folding lands). PMAT-037 /
XPILE-BASHRS-MERGER-001. See `sub/bashrs-merger.md` Layer A.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ForjarYaml)

### ForjarYaml

forjar.yaml IaC manifest text. Implemented by
`xpile-forjar-codegen` (PMAT-953). The BACKEND-ONLY forjar
integration (NOT merge/federate) — a declarative ops/deployment
output lane, peer to bashrs-backend’s shell lane. Lowers a
SHELL-origin meta-HIR `Module` (the `Stmt::Cmd` / `Stmt::Pipeline`
command sequence) to forjar `type: file` / `type: task` resources.
REFUSES non-shell modules and any shell idempotence guard /
conditional (the meta-HIR shell lane has no `Stmt::ShellIf`), so
only unconditional resources emit — forjar re-adds convergence at
apply time. See `project-forjar-output-backend`.

# DiffExecEngine in xpile_backend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/xpile-backend/0.1.615/xpile_backend/trait.DiffExecEngine.html

`pub trait DiffExecEngine: `[Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html) {
    // Required method
    fn [execute_and_compare](https://docs.rs#tymethod.execute_and_compare)(
        &self,
        general_text: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
        specialist_text: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
        module: &[Module](https://docs.rs/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xpile_meta_hir/struct.Module.html),
        config: &[BackendConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.BackendConfig.html),
        tolerance: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    ) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[DiffExecResult](https://docs.rs/enum.DiffExecResult.html), [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>;
}## Expand description

PMAT-486 (§30 Track 4): engine that executes two emitted programs on contract-fixture inputs and numerically compares the outputs within a tolerance — the Runtime-stratum half of the §29 quorum. The trait + hook land here (free CI); the real CUDA / Vulkan implementations (PMAT-488 / PMAT-490) run out-of-band on self-hosted GPU runners.

Error posture (per the §30 Track-4 review): with **no engine
installed** the `DiffExec` policy records `NotRun { reason: no-engine }`
(benign — free CI stays green). An **installed** engine that returns
`Err` propagates a hard [ BackendError](https://docs.rs/enum.BackendError.html) that fails the job — a broken
GPU run must NOT masquerade as “not run”.

Execute `general_text` and `specialist_text` on the contract’s
fixture inputs and compare. `Ok(Match|Divergent)` records the
vote; `Err(msg)` is a hard failure (e.g. driver fault / launch
error) the caller turns into a `BackendError`.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# xpile_meta_hir - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/xpile-meta-hir/0.1.615/target-redirect/xpile_meta_hir/

## Expand description

Canonical meta-HIR.

Every frontend in xpile lowers its language-specific AST to this
shared, intentionally minimal IR. The federated approach (see
`docs/specifications/xpile-architecture-v1.md`) means we start
lossy and grow as hybrid-transpile cases demand.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html)
- [FfiBoundary](https://docs.rs/struct.FfiBoundary.html)
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.Function.html)
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.Module.html)
- [Param](https://docs.rs/struct.Param.html)
- [SortKey](https://docs.rs/struct.SortKey.html)
- PMAT-502z (Tranche 2): a `sorted(xs, key=lambda p: e)`sort key — the lambda’s single parameter name plus its (already-lowered) body. The body is lowered with`param`left unbound (an`Ident`), so it works for bodies that don’t need the param’s precise static type (arithmetic,`len(p)`, most builtins); the backend emits`let <param> = __k.clone();`to bind it by value at runtime. Str-method keys (`p.upper()`) are deferred.
- [TryHandler](https://docs.rs/struct.TryHandler.html)
- PMAT-1059: one `except`clause of a multi-handler statement-form`Stmt::TryCatch``as <name>`message binding, and handler statement block.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [BinOp](https://docs.rs/enum.BinOp.html)
- [Dict](https://docs.rs/enum.DictViewKind.html)- View - Kind
- PMAT-502v (Tranche 2): dict view methods carried by `Expr::DictView`
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)
- [FloatOp](https://docs.rs/enum.FloatOp.html)
- PMAT-477 (R8): float arithmetic operators. Carried by
`Expr::FloatBinOp``Add`/`Sub`/`Mul`/`Div`emit plain infix (`f64`saturates, no`checked_*`);`Div`is IEEE-754 true division. PMAT-502br:`FloorDiv`/`Mod`emit Python-correct*floor*semantics (`(a / b).floor()`and`a - b * (a / b).floor()`), which differ from Rust’s truncating`/`int-div and sign-of-dividend`%`— so they are NOT plain infix.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/enum.Item.html)
- [List](https://docs.rs/enum.ListMutateOp.html)- Mutate - Op
- PMAT-502ap (Tranche 2): no-argument in-place list mutators carried by
`Stmt::ListMutate``Vec`method; all return`None`in Python (so they only appear as expression statements).
- [List](https://docs.rs/enum.ListQueryOp.html)- Query - Op
- PMAT-502u (Tranche 2): list query methods carried by `Expr::ListQuery``Int`;`Index`panics on a missing element (Python`ValueError`).
- [Loop](https://docs.rs/enum.LoopKind.html)- Kind
- POSIX shell loop dialects. PMAT-048 / XPILE-BASHRS-MERGER-001
Layer B. Each variant carries the loop’s control predicate /
item list; the body lives in `Stmt::ShellLoop::body`.
- [NumBuiltin](https://docs.rs/enum.NumBuiltinOp.html)- Op
- PMAT-498 (Tranche 2): scalar numeric builtins carried by
`Expr::NumBuiltin``Abs`takes 1 arg;`Min`/`Max`are variadic (`>= 2`args, PMAT-502cz) and chain`.min`/`.max`over the tail.
- [Pair](https://docs.rs/enum.PairIterKind.html)- Iter - Kind
- PMAT-495 (sprint): the iterator adapter for a `Stmt::ForEachPair`
- [Quoting](https://docs.rs/enum.QuotingStrategy.html)- Strategy
- Per-arg shell quoting choice. Carried by `Expr::QuotedString`so the bashrs-backend renders each arg in the strategy the source indicated. v0.1.0’s bashrs-frontend doesn’t have a real quoting-aware parser yet — it produces`Expr::LitStr`for every arg, and`QuotingStrategy::None`is implicit there. The full strategy set is wired so the v0.2.0 source fold’s real bashrs parser can plug in without IR churn.
- [Radix](https://docs.rs/enum.Radix.html)
- PMAT-502cv: the radix for `hex`/`oct`/`bin`(`Expr::IntRadixStr`).
- [SetOp](https://docs.rs/enum.SetOp.html)
- PMAT-502g (Tranche 2): set-algebra operators carried by `Expr::SetOp``HashSet`method that returns an iterator of borrows, materialized via`.cloned().collect()`into a new owned`HashSet`.
- [SetPred](https://docs.rs/enum.SetPredOp.html)- Op
- PMAT-502ep (Tranche 2): set predicates carried by `Expr::SetPred``bool`. Each maps to a`HashSet`query method; the proper variants additionally require the sets to differ.
- [Source](https://docs.rs/enum.SourceLang.html)- Lang
- [Stmt](https://docs.rs/enum.Stmt.html)
- [StrMethod](https://docs.rs/enum.StrMethodOp.html)- Op
- PMAT-492 (sprint): no-argument Python string transform methods,
carried by `Expr::StrMethod`
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.Type.html)
- MVP type lattice. Will grow as frontends demand it. Keep semantically
minimal; map source-language type idiosyncrasies (Python int bigint
promotion, C signed/unsigned, etc.) at the frontend boundary.
PMAT-455 — `Type`is no longer`Copy`because`Type::List(Box<Type>)`is heap-allocated. Callers that previously relied on`*ty`to dereference / copy now use`.clone()`(cheap — most Type values are leaf variants or 1-deep boxes).
- [UnOp](https://docs.rs/enum.UnOp.html)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [collect_](https://docs.rs/fn.collect_block_idents.html)- block_ - idents
- PMAT-736 (HUNT-V11 V11-6): collect every identifier-position name reachable
from `block`into`acc`— both value references (`Expr::Ident`, a`Call`callee) and receiver names (`xs.append(...)`’s`xs`,`d[k] = v`’s`d`, …), plus binding names (a`let`, a loop var). It is the read-only mirror of the`escape_*`walker above: every`escape_name(x)`there becomes`acc.insert(x)`here, so the two stay structurally identical (both are compiler-checked exhaustive over`Stmt`/`Expr`). Used by the frontend’s nested-function lowering to decide whether a nested`def`is self-recursive and whether it captures an enclosing local — over-collection (a binding name, a lambda param) is harmless there, since the caller only intersects the result with the enclosing scope.
- [escape_](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_rust_reserved_idents.html)- rust_ - reserved_ - idents
- PMAT-573: rewrite every identifier in `module`that collides with a Rust keyword to its raw form`r#kw`, so Python locals/params/functions named`type`/`match`/`loop`/… emit valid Rust (and Ruchy). The Rust-family backends call this on a*cloned*module before emission. Struct/enum type names, struct field names, and method names are left unescaped (a keyword-named class/field/method is a separate, rarer fidelity gap).
- [retype_](https://docs.rs/fn.retype_ffi_float_call_sites.html)- ffi_ - float_ - call_ - sites
- Re-type the call sites of `float_ffi`FFI symbols in`module`to F64 so the float-repr path (print`.0`,`let: f64`, float return) is selected. See the PMAT-931 block above. No-op when`float_ffi`is empty.
