# xpile_meta_hir/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Canonical meta-HIR.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! Every frontend in xpile lowers its language-specific AST to this
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! shared, intentionally minimal IR. The federated approach (see
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! `docs/specifications/xpile-architecture-v1.md`) means we start
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! lossy and grow as hybrid-transpile cases demand.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)
[8](https://docs.rs#8)use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[9](https://docs.rs#9)
[10](https://docs.rs#10)#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[11](https://docs.rs#11)pub struct Module {
[12](https://docs.rs#12)    pub name: String,
[13](https://docs.rs#13)    pub source_lang: SourceLang,
[14](https://docs.rs#14)    pub items: Vec<Item>,
[15](https://docs.rs#15)    pub ffi_boundaries: Vec<FfiBoundary>,
[16](https://docs.rs#16)}
[17](https://docs.rs#17)
[18](https://docs.rs#18)#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[19](https://docs.rs#19)pub enum SourceLang {
[20](https://docs.rs#20)    Python,
[21](https://docs.rs#21)    C,
[22](https://docs.rs#22)    Cpp,
[23](https://docs.rs#23)    Cuda,
[24](https://docs.rs#24)    Ruchy,
[25](https://docs.rs#25)    /// Rust as a source language — keystone for bidirectional Rust↔Ruchy
[26](https://docs.rs#26)    /// and the Rust→GPU paths (Rust→PTX/WGSL/SPIR-V).
[27](https://docs.rs#27)    Rust,
[28](https://docs.rs#28)    /// Lean 4 as a source language — its executable subset (def, partial
[29](https://docs.rs#29)    /// def, inductive, structure, instance, ...) lowers to Rust via the
[30](https://docs.rs#30)    /// code lane. Theorem statements parse via the proof lane separately.
[31](https://docs.rs#31)    Lean,
[32](https://docs.rs#32)    /// POSIX shell (bash / zsh / sh dialects + Makefile / Dockerfile) —
[33](https://docs.rs#33)    /// the bashrs merger domain. PMAT-037 / XPILE-BASHRS-MERGER-001
[34](https://docs.rs#34)    /// adds this variant as scaffold (`bashrs-frontend` produces it,
[35](https://docs.rs#35)    /// `bashrs-backend` consumes it, all other backends return
[36](https://docs.rs#36)    /// `Unsupported`). Per `sub/bashrs-merger.md` Layer B, meta-HIR
[37](https://docs.rs#37)    /// will grow shell-specific `Stmt::Cmd` / `Stmt::Pipeline` etc.
[38](https://docs.rs#38)    /// variants at v0.2.0 — at v0.1.0 a `SourceLang::Shell` `Module`
[39](https://docs.rs#39)    /// is structurally empty (no items / no boundaries), validating
[40](https://docs.rs#40)    /// only that the dispatch and SourceLang lane are wired.
[41](https://docs.rs#41)    Shell,
[42](https://docs.rs#42)    /// WebAssembly text (WAT) as a **source** language — the LIFT half
[43](https://docs.rs#43)    /// of first-class bidirectional native WASM (PMAT-954, the inverse
[44](https://docs.rs#44)    /// of the `Target::Wasm` emit half PMAT-951). `xpile-wasm-frontend`
[45](https://docs.rs#45)    /// produces it: a **lossy DECOMPILATION** of the WAT scalar/control
[46](https://docs.rs#46)    /// subset back to meta-HIR (stack→expression-tree reconstruction).
[47](https://docs.rs#47)    /// Honestly asymmetric — emit is clean, lift is lossy: high-level
[48](https://docs.rs#48)    /// types collapse to the canonical scalar (`i64`→`I64`, `f64`→`F64`,
[49](https://docs.rs#49)    /// `f32`→`F32`, `i32`→`Bool`), and structured control-flow recovery
[50](https://docs.rs#50)    /// (`if`/`block`/`loop`) is refused at this first cut (deferred to
[51](https://docs.rs#51)    /// PMAT-952). The lift's correctness is pinned by an executed
[52](https://docs.rs#52)    /// round-trip **fixed-point** witness: `emit(lift(emit(M))) ==
[53](https://docs.rs#53)    /// emit(M)` (the lift is a right-inverse of emit on its WAT image).
[54](https://docs.rs#54)    /// See `project-bidirectional-wasm`.
[55](https://docs.rs#55)    Wasm,
[56](https://docs.rs#56)}
[57](https://docs.rs#57)
[58](https://docs.rs#58)#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[59](https://docs.rs#59)pub enum Item {
[60](https://docs.rs#60)    Function(Function),
[61](https://docs.rs#61)    /// A module-level constant — Python `NAME = <literal>`. PMAT-502bj
[62](https://docs.rs#62)    /// (Tranche 2). First cut: `int` / `bool` / `float` values (which map
[63](https://docs.rs#63)    /// to a Rust `const`); `str` constants need `&str` (deferred). Rust/
[64](https://docs.rs#64)    /// Ruchy emit `const <name>: <ty> = <value>;`; Lean refuses. The
[65](https://docs.rs#65)    /// frontend records the constant's type so references in function
[66](https://docs.rs#66)    /// bodies type correctly.
[67](https://docs.rs#67)    Const {
[68](https://docs.rs#68)        name: String,
[69](https://docs.rs#69)        ty: Type,
[70](https://docs.rs#70)        value: Expr,
[71](https://docs.rs#71)    },
[72](https://docs.rs#72)    /// PMAT-505a (classes epic, first cut): a Python `@dataclass` / field-only
[73](https://docs.rs#73)    /// class → a Rust struct. `fields` are the annotated members in declaration
[74](https://docs.rs#74)    /// order (`x: int` → `("x", Type::I64)`). Rust/Ruchy emit
[75](https://docs.rs#75)    /// `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct Name { pub <f>: <ty>, … }`;
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    /// Lean refuses (structure encoding deferred). This first cut emits the
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    /// *definition* only — value construction (`Name(a, b)`) and field access
[78](https://docs.rs#78)    /// (`obj.f`) are a follow-up sub-slice (they need a `Type::Struct` variant).
[79](https://docs.rs#79)    Struct {
[80](https://docs.rs#80)        name: String,
[81](https://docs.rs#81)        fields: Vec<(String, Type)>,
[82](https://docs.rs#82)        /// PMAT-506d (classes epic): instance methods → an `impl` block. Each is
[83](https://docs.rs#83)        /// a [`Function`] whose first param is `self` (typed [`Type::Struct`] of
[84](https://docs.rs#84)        /// this struct). Rust/Ruchy emit `impl Name { pub fn m(&self, …) … }`
[85](https://docs.rs#85)        /// (the `self` param emits as `&self`); Lean refuses. First cut:
[86](https://docs.rs#86)        /// read-only `&self` methods (self-mutating ones are rejected upstream).
[87](https://docs.rs#87)        methods: Vec<Function>,
[88](https://docs.rs#88)        /// PMAT-592 (classes epic): the class is `@dataclass(frozen=True)` — a
[89](https://docs.rs#89)        /// frozen dataclass is *hashable* in Python, so it may be used as a
[90](https://docs.rs#90)        /// dict key or set element. When this is set AND every field type is
[91](https://docs.rs#91)        /// itself `Eq + Hash`-capable (`i64`/`bool`/`String`), the Rust/Ruchy
[92](https://docs.rs#92)        /// codegen extends the derive list with `Eq, Hash` (a plain
[93](https://docs.rs#93)        /// `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]` struct cannot be a `HashMap`
[94](https://docs.rs#94)        /// key / `HashSet` element — E0277/E0599). Non-frozen dataclasses are
[95](https://docs.rs#95)        /// unhashable in Python, so they keep the bare derive set. A float
[96](https://docs.rs#96)        /// field disqualifies the struct (`f64` is neither `Eq` nor `Hash`),
[97](https://docs.rs#97)        /// matching the codegen guard. `#[serde(default)]` for back-compat.
[98](https://docs.rs#98)        #[serde(default)]
[99](https://docs.rs#99)        frozen: bool,
[100](https://docs.rs#100)        /// PMAT-648 (classes epic): the class is `@dataclass(order=True)` — Python
[101](https://docs.rs#101)        /// generates `__lt__`/`__le__`/`__gt__`/`__ge__` comparing the fields as a
[102](https://docs.rs#102)        /// tuple (definition order). The Rust/Ruchy codegen adds `PartialOrd` to
[103](https://docs.rs#103)        /// the derive list (lexicographic by field order, matching Python's tuple
[104](https://docs.rs#104)        /// comparison) so `Inst < Inst` etc. compile. `PartialOrd` is sound for
[105](https://docs.rs#105)        /// any comparable field (incl. `f64`); full `Ord` (sorting instances) is a
[106](https://docs.rs#106)        /// deferred follow-up (a float field can't derive `Ord`). Bare
[107](https://docs.rs#107)        /// `@dataclass` / `order=False` keep the non-comparable derive set.
[108](https://docs.rs#108)        /// `#[serde(default)]` for back-compat.
[109](https://docs.rs#109)        #[serde(default)]
[110](https://docs.rs#110)        order: bool,
[111](https://docs.rs#111)    },
[112](https://docs.rs#112)    /// PMAT-513 (Tranche 2): a Python `class C(Enum):` with `NAME = <int literal>`
[113](https://docs.rs#113)    /// members → a Rust enum. `variants` are `(name, discriminant)` in declaration
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    /// order. Rust/Ruchy emit
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    /// `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum C { NAME, … }`;
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    /// member access `C.NAME` → [`Expr::EnumVariant`] (`C::NAME`), and the
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    /// compile-time-known `C.NAME.value` lowers directly to its discriminant
[118](https://docs.rs#118)    /// literal. Enum-typed values reuse [`Type::Struct`] (an enum is just a named
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    /// type at use sites). Lean refuses.
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    Enum {
[121](https://docs.rs#121)        name: String,
[122](https://docs.rs#122)        variants: Vec<(String, i64)>,
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    },
[124](https://docs.rs#124)}
[125](https://docs.rs#125)
[126](https://docs.rs#126)/// PMAT-1059: one `except` clause of a multi-handler statement-form
[127](https://docs.rs#127)/// [`Stmt::TryCatch`] — its caught exception type(s) (empty = catch-all),
[128](https://docs.rs#128)/// optional `as <name>` message binding, and handler statement block.
[129](https://docs.rs#129)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[130](https://docs.rs#130)pub struct TryHandler {
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    pub except_types: Vec<String>,
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    pub bound_name: Option<String>,
[133](https://docs.rs#133)    pub body: Vec<Stmt>,
[134](https://docs.rs#134)}
[135](https://docs.rs#135)
[136](https://docs.rs#136)#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[137](https://docs.rs#137)pub struct Function {
[138](https://docs.rs#138)    pub name: String,
[139](https://docs.rs#139)    pub params: Vec<Param>,
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    pub return_type: Type,
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    /// Function body. A sequence of zero or more [`Stmt`] followed by a
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    /// trailing return expression — the invariant that every function
[143](https://docs.rs#143)    /// terminates by yielding exactly one value, kept explicit.
[144](https://docs.rs#144)    pub body: Block,
[145](https://docs.rs#145)}
[146](https://docs.rs#146)
[147](https://docs.rs#147)impl Function {
[148](https://docs.rs#148)    /// Returns the list of contract IDs that govern this function.
[149](https://docs.rs#149)    /// Drives codegen citation emission (PMAT-011): each ID returned
[150](https://docs.rs#150)    /// here will appear as `// xpile-contract: <ID>` (Rust/Ruchy) or
[151](https://docs.rs#151)    /// `@[xpile_contract "<ID>"]` (Lean) next to the emitted function.
[152](https://docs.rs#152)    ///
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    /// Per v0.1.0's single Layer-1 contract, this returns
[154](https://docs.rs#154)    /// `["C-PY-INT-ARITH"]` if and only if the function body uses any
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    /// i64 arithmetic / bitwise / shift / power / unary-neg operator —
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    /// the operations whose overflow / wrapping the contract bounds.
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    /// Comparisons (`==`, `<`, etc.), logicals (`&&`, `!`), and
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    /// constant-only / call-only bodies don't trigger the citation.
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    pub fn applicable_contracts(&self) -> Vec<&'static str> {
[160](https://docs.rs#160)        let mut ids = Vec::new();
[161](https://docs.rs#161)        if self.uses_int_arithmetic() {
[162](https://docs.rs#162)            ids.push("C-PY-INT-ARITH");
[163](https://docs.rs#163)        }
[164](https://docs.rs#164)        // PMAT-475 (R6): cite the type-translation contracts when the function
[165](https://docs.rs#165)        // takes, returns, or binds a str / list / dict. These contracts exist
[166](https://docs.rs#166)        // on disk (xlate-py-{str,list,dict}-*.yaml) but were never wired into
[167](https://docs.rs#167)        // citation emission, so str/list/dict code shipped UNCITED — the
[168](https://docs.rs#168)        // capability-vs-contract drift (audit-design.md §6). The signal is the
[169](https://docs.rs#169)        // TYPES in play (params + return + body `let`/loop bindings, recursing
[170](https://docs.rs#170)        // into compound types) because these contracts govern the type
[171](https://docs.rs#171)        // translation itself. All core scalars + containers are now wired —
[172](https://docs.rs#172)        // int/str/list/dict/float/set each cite their on-disk contract.
[173](https://docs.rs#173)        let mut tys: Vec<&Type> = self.params.iter().map(|p| &p.ty).collect();
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        tys.push(&self.return_type);
[175](https://docs.rs#175)        collect_block_let_types(&self.body.stmts, &mut tys);
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        if tys.iter().any(|t| type_any(t, &|x| matches!(x, Type::Str))) {
[177](https://docs.rs#177)            ids.push("C-XLATE-PY-STR-TO-RUST-STRING");
[178](https://docs.rs#178)        }
[179](https://docs.rs#179)        if tys
[180](https://docs.rs#180)            .iter()
[181](https://docs.rs#181)            .any(|t| type_any(t, &|x| matches!(x, Type::List(_))))
[182](https://docs.rs#182)        {
[183](https://docs.rs#183)            ids.push("C-XLATE-PY-LIST-TO-VEC");
[184](https://docs.rs#184)        }
[185](https://docs.rs#185)        if tys
[186](https://docs.rs#186)            .iter()
[187](https://docs.rs#187)            .any(|t| type_any(t, &|x| matches!(x, Type::Dict(_, _))))
[188](https://docs.rs#188)        {
[189](https://docs.rs#189)            ids.push("C-XLATE-PY-DICT-TO-HASHMAP");
[190](https://docs.rs#190)        }
[191](https://docs.rs#191)        // PMAT-860 (R6 slice 3): float now has its on-disk contract
[192](https://docs.rs#192)        // (contracts/py-float-arith-v1.yaml), so float-typed code cites it
[193](https://docs.rs#193)        // instead of emitting uncited (the last core scalar to be wired).
[194](https://docs.rs#194)        if tys.iter().any(|t| type_any(t, &|x| matches!(x, Type::F64))) {
[195](https://docs.rs#195)            ids.push("C-PY-FLOAT-ARITH");
[196](https://docs.rs#196)        }
[197](https://docs.rs#197)        // PMAT-861 (R6 slice 4): set now has its on-disk contract
[198](https://docs.rs#198)        // (contracts/xlate-py-set-to-hashset-v1.yaml) — the last container wired,
[199](https://docs.rs#199)        // so int/str/list/dict/float/set all cite their translation contract.
[200](https://docs.rs#200)        if tys
[201](https://docs.rs#201)            .iter()
[202](https://docs.rs#202)            .any(|t| type_any(t, &|x| matches!(x, Type::Set(_))))
[203](https://docs.rs#203)        {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)            ids.push("C-XLATE-PY-SET-TO-HASHSET");
[205](https://docs.rs#205)        }
[206](https://docs.rs#206)        // PMAT-879 (R6): cite the class-translation contract when the function
[207](https://docs.rs#207)        // takes, returns, or binds a class/dataclass (`Type::Struct`). Class
[208](https://docs.rs#208)        // translation was the largest core construct still shipping uncited —
[209](https://docs.rs#209)        // `pub struct Point { … }` emitted with ZERO `// xpile-contract:` line.
[210](https://docs.rs#210)        // The contract (contracts/xlate-py-class-to-struct-v1.yaml) governs
[211](https://docs.rs#211)        // field-order + field-type preservation and read-only `&self` dispatch.
[212](https://docs.rs#212)        if tys
[213](https://docs.rs#213)            .iter()
[214](https://docs.rs#214)            .any(|t| type_any(t, &|x| matches!(x, Type::Struct(_))))
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        {
[216](https://docs.rs#216)            ids.push("C-XLATE-PY-CLASS-TO-STRUCT");
[217](https://docs.rs#217)        }
[218](https://docs.rs#218)        // PMAT-880 (R6): cite the tuple-translation contract when the function
[219](https://docs.rs#219)        // takes, returns, or binds a fixed-arity tuple (`Type::Tuple`). Tuple
[220](https://docs.rs#220)        // code (`(i64, i64)`) shipped uncited — the tuple sibling of the
[221](https://docs.rs#221)        // list/dict/set translation contracts. The contract
[222](https://docs.rs#222)        // (contracts/xlate-py-tuple-to-rust-tuple-v1.yaml) governs arity +
[223](https://docs.rs#223)        // per-position element preservation.
[224](https://docs.rs#224)        if tys
[225](https://docs.rs#225)            .iter()
[226](https://docs.rs#226)            .any(|t| type_any(t, &|x| matches!(x, Type::Tuple(_))))
[227](https://docs.rs#227)        {
[228](https://docs.rs#228)            ids.push("C-XLATE-PY-TUPLE-TO-RUST-TUPLE");
[229](https://docs.rs#229)        }
[230](https://docs.rs#230)        // PMAT-881 (R6): cite the Optional-translation contract when the function
[231](https://docs.rs#231)        // takes, returns, or binds an `Optional[T]`. The Option mapping (None →
[232](https://docs.rs#232)        // Option::None, Some-wrapping at observation, `is None` → `.is_none()`)
[233](https://docs.rs#233)        // is a real semantic boundary that shipped uncited for its Optional-ness
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        // (Optional[str] cited str via its inner type, but not the Option map).
[235](https://docs.rs#235)        // The contract is contracts/xlate-py-optional-to-option-v1.yaml.
[236](https://docs.rs#236)        if tys
[237](https://docs.rs#237)            .iter()
[238](https://docs.rs#238)            .any(|t| type_any(t, &|x| matches!(x, Type::Optional(_))))
[239](https://docs.rs#239)        {
[240](https://docs.rs#240)            ids.push("C-XLATE-PY-OPTIONAL-TO-OPTION");
[241](https://docs.rs#241)        }
[242](https://docs.rs#242)        // PMAT-935 (R6): cite the bool-translation contract when the function
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        // takes, returns, or binds a `bool` (`Type::Bool`). Pure-boolean logic
[244](https://docs.rs#244)        // (`a and b` → `a && b`, `not a` → `!a`) shipped UNCITED — the last core
[245](https://docs.rs#245)        // scalar still emitting with no `// xpile-contract:` line (int/str/float
[246](https://docs.rs#246)        // were already wired; bool closes the scalar set). The contract
[247](https://docs.rs#247)        // (contracts/xlate-py-bool-to-rust-bool-v1.yaml) governs short-circuit
[248](https://docs.rs#248)        // (`&&`/`||`, never the eager `&`/`|`) + operator polarity.
[249](https://docs.rs#249)        if tys
[250](https://docs.rs#250)            .iter()
[251](https://docs.rs#251)            .any(|t| type_any(t, &|x| matches!(x, Type::Bool)))
[252](https://docs.rs#252)        {
[253](https://docs.rs#253)            ids.push("C-XLATE-PY-BOOL-TO-RUST-BOOL");
[254](https://docs.rs#254)        }
[255](https://docs.rs#255)        ids
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    }
[257](https://docs.rs#257)
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    /// True if any expression in the function body uses an op that
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    /// `C-PY-INT-ARITH` governs (overflow-prone arithmetic, bitwise,
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    /// shifts, power, or unary negation). Walks all Stmt + Expr
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    /// reachable from the body.
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    pub fn uses_int_arithmetic(&self) -> bool {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        for stmt in &self.body.stmts {
[264](https://docs.rs#264)            if stmt_has_int_arith(stmt) {
[265](https://docs.rs#265)                return true;
[266](https://docs.rs#266)            }
[267](https://docs.rs#267)        }
[268](https://docs.rs#268)        expr_has_int_arith(&self.body.trailing_return)
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    }
[270](https://docs.rs#270)}
[271](https://docs.rs#271)
[272](https://docs.rs#272)impl Item {
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    /// PMAT-958 (Pillar-A contract-citation-integrity, definition-level
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    /// closure): the contract IDs that govern a *definition-level* item —
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    /// the analog of [`Function::applicable_contracts`] for the `Item`
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    /// kinds that emit a top-level *definition* with no per-function
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    /// citation line of their own.
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    ///
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    /// The function-level surface (top-level `Item::Function` + an
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    /// `Item::Struct`'s methods) already cites via
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    /// [`Function::applicable_contracts`]. The remaining honest gap PMAT-955
[282](https://docs.rs#282)    /// named was the *definition* itself: a method-less `@dataclass`
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    /// (`Item::Struct` with empty `methods`) emitted `pub struct {..}` with
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    /// ZERO `// xpile-contract:` line, because no `Function` ran over it. A
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    /// method-bearing struct cited `C-XLATE-PY-CLASS-TO-STRUCT` only as a
[286](https://docs.rs#286)    /// side effect of its methods' `self: Type::Struct` params — drop the
[287](https://docs.rs#287)    /// last method and the citation vanished.
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    ///
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    /// This returns the definition-level contract for an `Item::Struct`
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    /// unconditionally — every class→struct translation is governed by
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    /// `C-XLATE-PY-CLASS-TO-STRUCT` (field-order + field-type preservation),
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    /// independent of whether the class has methods. `Item::Function` is
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    /// covered by the per-function path and returns nothing here (callers
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    /// cite its `Function::applicable_contracts` directly).
[295](https://docs.rs#295)    ///
[296](https://docs.rs#296)    /// `Item::Const` / `Item::Enum` return nothing: there is no on-disk
[297](https://docs.rs#297)    /// const-translation or enum-translation contract yet (only the
[298](https://docs.rs#298)    /// class/scalar/container families have governing YAMLs). Authoring one
[299](https://docs.rs#299)    /// is the documented follow-up — until then this method returns an empty
[300](https://docs.rs#300)    /// set for them so the derived gate does not over-expect a citation the
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    /// codegen cannot honestly emit.
[302](https://docs.rs#302)    pub fn applicable_contracts(&self) -> Vec<&'static str> {
[303](https://docs.rs#303)        match self {
[304](https://docs.rs#304)            // The per-function path owns Function citations (its body/sig
[305](https://docs.rs#305)            // drives `Function::applicable_contracts`); nothing definition-level.
[306](https://docs.rs#306)            Item::Function(_) => Vec::new(),
[307](https://docs.rs#307)            // Every class→struct translation is governed by the class contract,
[308](https://docs.rs#308)            // method-less or not — this is the definition-level closure.
[309](https://docs.rs#309)            Item::Struct { .. } => vec!["C-XLATE-PY-CLASS-TO-STRUCT"],
[310](https://docs.rs#310)            // No governing const/enum translation contract on disk yet
[311](https://docs.rs#311)            // (follow-up). Empty so the derived gate stays honest.
[312](https://docs.rs#312)            Item::Const { .. } | Item::Enum { .. } => Vec::new(),
[313](https://docs.rs#313)        }
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    }
[315](https://docs.rs#315)}
[316](https://docs.rs#316)
[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// PMAT-475 (R6): true if any node in the type tree satisfies `f`, recursing
[318](https://docs.rs#318)/// into element / key / value / member types of compound types. Lets a
[319](https://docs.rs#319)/// `dict[str, list[int]]` trigger the str, list, AND dict contracts.
[320](https://docs.rs#320)fn type_any(t: &Type, f: &dyn Fn(&Type) -> bool) -> bool {
[321](https://docs.rs#321)    if f(t) {
[322](https://docs.rs#322)        return true;
[323](https://docs.rs#323)    }
[324](https://docs.rs#324)    match t {
[325](https://docs.rs#325)        Type::List(inner) | Type::Set(inner) | Type::Optional(inner) => type_any(inner, f),
[326](https://docs.rs#326)        // PMAT-924: a pointer recurses into its pointee, so a contract keyed on
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        // the pointee type still triggers through a pointer wrapper.
[328](https://docs.rs#328)        Type::Ptr { pointee, .. } => type_any(pointee, f),
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        Type::Dict(k, v) => type_any(k, f) || type_any(v, f),
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        Type::Tuple(elems) => elems.iter().any(|e| type_any(e, f)),
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        _ => false,
[332](https://docs.rs#332)    }
[333](https://docs.rs#333)}
[334](https://docs.rs#334)
[335](https://docs.rs#335)/// PMAT-475 (R6): collect the declared type of every `let` binding (and loop
[336](https://docs.rs#336)/// element type) reachable in a statement list, recursing nested blocks — so a
[337](https://docs.rs#337)/// str/list/dict used only in a local still triggers its contract citation.
[338](https://docs.rs#338)fn collect_block_let_types<'a>(stmts: &'a [Stmt], out: &mut Vec<&'a Type>) {
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    for s in stmts {
[340](https://docs.rs#340)        match s {
[341](https://docs.rs#341)            Stmt::Let { ty, .. } => out.push(ty),
[342](https://docs.rs#342)            Stmt::ForEach { elem_ty, body, .. } => {
[343](https://docs.rs#343)                out.push(elem_ty);
[344](https://docs.rs#344)                collect_block_let_types(body, out);
[345](https://docs.rs#345)            }
[346](https://docs.rs#346)            Stmt::ForEachPair { body, .. } => collect_block_let_types(body, out),
[347](https://docs.rs#347)            Stmt::While { body, .. } => collect_block_let_types(body, out),
[348](https://docs.rs#348)            Stmt::If {
[349](https://docs.rs#349)                then_body,
[350](https://docs.rs#350)                else_body,
[351](https://docs.rs#351)                ..
[352](https://docs.rs#352)            } => {
[353](https://docs.rs#353)                collect_block_let_types(then_body, out);
[354](https://docs.rs#354)                collect_block_let_types(else_body, out);
[355](https://docs.rs#355)            }
[356](https://docs.rs#356)            Stmt::NestedFn { body, .. } => collect_block_let_types(&body.stmts, out),
[357](https://docs.rs#357)            _ => {}
[358](https://docs.rs#358)        }
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    }
[360](https://docs.rs#360)}
[361](https://docs.rs#361)
[362](https://docs.rs#362)fn stmt_has_int_arith(s: &Stmt) -> bool {
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    match s {
[364](https://docs.rs#364)        // PMAT-479 (R10): early return — recurse into the returned expr.
[365](https://docs.rs#365)        Stmt::Return(e) => expr_has_int_arith(e),
[366](https://docs.rs#366)        Stmt::Let { value, .. } | Stmt::Assign { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[367](https://docs.rs#367)        // PMAT-504: a closure binding — recurse into the body expression.
[368](https://docs.rs#368)        Stmt::ClosureLet { body, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(body),
[369](https://docs.rs#369)        // PMAT-736: a named inner fn — recurse into its body block (stmts +
[370](https://docs.rs#370)        // trailing). Its own int arithmetic still cites C-PY-INT-ARITH.
[371](https://docs.rs#371)        Stmt::NestedFn { body, .. } => {
[372](https://docs.rs#372)            body.stmts.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith) || expr_has_int_arith(&body.trailing_return)
[373](https://docs.rs#373)        }
[374](https://docs.rs#374)        // PMAT-494b: tuple unpacking — recurse into the unpacked value.
[375](https://docs.rs#375)        Stmt::LetTuple { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[376](https://docs.rs#376)        Stmt::While { cond, body } => {
[377](https://docs.rs#377)            if expr_has_int_arith(cond) {
[378](https://docs.rs#378)                return true;
[379](https://docs.rs#379)            }
[380](https://docs.rs#380)            body.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[381](https://docs.rs#381)        }
[382](https://docs.rs#382)        // PMAT-478 (R9): if/else statement — recurse cond + both bodies.
[383](https://docs.rs#383)        Stmt::If {
[384](https://docs.rs#384)            cond,
[385](https://docs.rs#385)            then_body,
[386](https://docs.rs#386)            else_body,
[387](https://docs.rs#387)        } => {
[388](https://docs.rs#388)            expr_has_int_arith(cond)
[389](https://docs.rs#389)                || then_body.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[390](https://docs.rs#390)                || else_body.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[391](https://docs.rs#391)        }
[392](https://docs.rs#392)        // PMAT-1058/1059: statement-form try/except — recurse into the body,
[393](https://docs.rs#393)        // the first handler, and every extra handler.
[394](https://docs.rs#394)        Stmt::TryCatch {
[395](https://docs.rs#395)            body,
[396](https://docs.rs#396)            handler,
[397](https://docs.rs#397)            extra_handlers,
[398](https://docs.rs#398)            finally,
[399](https://docs.rs#399)            ..
[400](https://docs.rs#400)        } => {
[401](https://docs.rs#401)            body.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[402](https://docs.rs#402)                || handler.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[403](https://docs.rs#403)                || extra_handlers
[404](https://docs.rs#404)                    .iter()
[405](https://docs.rs#405)                    .any(|h| h.body.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith))
[406](https://docs.rs#406)                || finally.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[407](https://docs.rs#407)        }
[408](https://docs.rs#408)        // PMAT-502bk: loop-control statements carry no expression.
[409](https://docs.rs#409)        Stmt::Continue | Stmt::Break => false,
[410](https://docs.rs#410)        // PMAT-502bw: `print(a, b, …)` — recurse into the argument exprs
[411](https://docs.rs#411)        // (an arithmetic-using arg, e.g. `print(a + b)`, propagates).
[412](https://docs.rs#412)        Stmt::Print { args, .. } => args.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith),
[413](https://docs.rs#413)        // PMAT-458: for-each over a collection. The `iter` and `body`
[414](https://docs.rs#414)        // are recursed; an arithmetic-using collection (e.g.,
[415](https://docs.rs#415)        // `for x in [a+b, c*d]:`) propagates the citation requirement.
[416](https://docs.rs#416)        Stmt::ForEach { iter, body, .. } => {
[417](https://docs.rs#417)            if expr_has_int_arith(iter) {
[418](https://docs.rs#418)                return true;
[419](https://docs.rs#419)            }
[420](https://docs.rs#420)            body.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)        }
[422](https://docs.rs#422)        // PMAT-495: paired for-loop — recurse into iter, the zip operand
[423](https://docs.rs#423)        // (if any), and the body.
[424](https://docs.rs#424)        Stmt::ForEachPair {
[425](https://docs.rs#425)            iter, kind, body, ..
[426](https://docs.rs#426)        } => {
[427](https://docs.rs#427)            if expr_has_int_arith(iter) {
[428](https://docs.rs#428)                return true;
[429](https://docs.rs#429)            }
[430](https://docs.rs#430)            if let PairIterKind::Zip(other) = kind {
[431](https://docs.rs#431)                if expr_has_int_arith(other) {
[432](https://docs.rs#432)                    return true;
[433](https://docs.rs#433)                }
[434](https://docs.rs#434)            }
[435](https://docs.rs#435)            body.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[436](https://docs.rs#436)        }
[437](https://docs.rs#437)        // PMAT-562: three-way zip — recurse into all three iterables + the body.
[438](https://docs.rs#438)        Stmt::ForEachZip3 {
[439](https://docs.rs#439)            iter1,
[440](https://docs.rs#440)            iter2,
[441](https://docs.rs#441)            iter3,
[442](https://docs.rs#442)            body,
[443](https://docs.rs#443)            ..
[444](https://docs.rs#444)        } => {
[445](https://docs.rs#445)            expr_has_int_arith(iter1)
[446](https://docs.rs#446)                || expr_has_int_arith(iter2)
[447](https://docs.rs#447)                || expr_has_int_arith(iter3)
[448](https://docs.rs#448)                || body.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[449](https://docs.rs#449)        }
[450](https://docs.rs#450)        // PMAT-460: list.append() — recurse into the elem expression.
[451](https://docs.rs#451)        Stmt::ListAppend { elem, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(elem),
[452](https://docs.rs#452)        // PMAT-500b: set.add() — recurse into the elem expression.
[453](https://docs.rs#453)        Stmt::SetAdd { elem, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(elem),
[454](https://docs.rs#454)        // PMAT-502av: set.remove()/discard() — recurse into the elem.
[455](https://docs.rs#455)        Stmt::SetRemove { elem, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(elem),
[456](https://docs.rs#456)        // PMAT-502ap: in-place list mutators carry no sub-expression.
[457](https://docs.rs#457)        Stmt::ListMutate { .. } => false,
[458](https://docs.rs#458)        // PMAT-502aq: list.extend() — recurse into the other-list expr.
[459](https://docs.rs#459)        Stmt::ListExtend { other, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(other),
[460](https://docs.rs#460)        // PMAT-502bb: dict.update() — recurse into the other-dict expr.
[461](https://docs.rs#461)        Stmt::DictUpdate { other, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(other),
[462](https://docs.rs#462)        // PMAT-502ar: list.insert() — recurse into index and elem.
[463](https://docs.rs#463)        Stmt::ListInsert { index, elem, .. } => {
[464](https://docs.rs#464)            expr_has_int_arith(index) || expr_has_int_arith(elem)
[465](https://docs.rs#465)        }
[466](https://docs.rs#466)        // PMAT-502eg: list.remove(value) — recurse into the value expr.
[467](https://docs.rs#467)        Stmt::ListRemoveValue { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[468](https://docs.rs#468)        // PMAT-461: indexed assignment — recurse into both index and
[469](https://docs.rs#469)        // value expressions (either may carry arithmetic).
[470](https://docs.rs#470)        Stmt::IndexAssign { indices, value, .. } => {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)            indices.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith) || expr_has_int_arith(value)
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        }
[473](https://docs.rs#473)        // PMAT-466 (v0.2.0 Track 1.C): dict keyed assignment — recurse
[474](https://docs.rs#474)        // into both key and value expressions.
[475](https://docs.rs#475)        Stmt::DictSet { key, value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(key) || expr_has_int_arith(value),
[476](https://docs.rs#476)        // PMAT-533: subscript-receiver append — recurse into index + elem.
[477](https://docs.rs#477)        Stmt::IndexAppend { index, elem, .. } => {
[478](https://docs.rs#478)            expr_has_int_arith(index) || expr_has_int_arith(elem)
[479](https://docs.rs#479)        }
[480](https://docs.rs#480)        // PMAT-727: setdefault-append — recurse into key, default, and elem.
[481](https://docs.rs#481)        Stmt::DictSetdefaultAppend {
[482](https://docs.rs#482)            key, default, elem, ..
[483](https://docs.rs#483)        } => expr_has_int_arith(key) || expr_has_int_arith(default) || expr_has_int_arith(elem),
[484](https://docs.rs#484)        // PMAT-730: nested subscript assign — recurse into each step index + value.
[485](https://docs.rs#485)        Stmt::NestedSubscriptAssign { steps, value, .. } => {
[486](https://docs.rs#486)            steps.iter().any(|(i, _)| expr_has_int_arith(i)) || expr_has_int_arith(value)
[487](https://docs.rs#487)        }
[488](https://docs.rs#488)        // PMAT-1037: field subscript store — recurse into step indices + value.
[489](https://docs.rs#489)        Stmt::FieldIndexAssign { steps, value, .. } => {
[490](https://docs.rs#490)            steps.iter().any(|(i, _)| expr_has_int_arith(i)) || expr_has_int_arith(value)
[491](https://docs.rs#491)        }
[492](https://docs.rs#492)        // PMAT-506c: field assignment — the assigned value may carry int arith.
[493](https://docs.rs#493)        Stmt::FieldAssign { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[494](https://docs.rs#494)        // PMAT-502at: del coll[key] — recurse into the key expression.
[495](https://docs.rs#495)        Stmt::DelItem { key, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(key),
[496](https://docs.rs#496)        // PMAT-1016A: statement-position side-effect call — recurse into it.
[497](https://docs.rs#497)        Stmt::SideEffectCall { call } => expr_has_int_arith(call),
[498](https://docs.rs#498)        Stmt::Assert { cond, msg } => {
[499](https://docs.rs#499)            expr_has_int_arith(cond) || msg.as_ref().is_some_and(expr_has_int_arith)
[500](https://docs.rs#500)        }
[501](https://docs.rs#501)        // PMAT-503a: raise — recurse into the panic message expression.
[502](https://docs.rs#502)        Stmt::Raise { message } => expr_has_int_arith(message),
[503](https://docs.rs#503)        // PMAT-039: shell commands are governed by `C-BASHRS-POSIX-IDEMPOTENCE`,
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        // not `C-PY-INT-ARITH`. The args are `Vec<String>` (literal
[505](https://docs.rs#505)        // tokens) — no arithmetic operands.
[506](https://docs.rs#506)        Stmt::Cmd { .. } => false,
[507](https://docs.rs#507)        Stmt::FileWrite { path, content, .. } => {
[508](https://docs.rs#508)            expr_has_int_arith(path) || expr_has_int_arith(content)
[509](https://docs.rs#509)        }
[510](https://docs.rs#510)        // PMAT-041: pipelines compose Cmds — recurse into each stage
[511](https://docs.rs#511)        // for completeness (currently every stage is a Cmd, so this is
[512](https://docs.rs#512)        // always false in practice).
[513](https://docs.rs#513)        Stmt::Pipeline { stages } => stages.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith),
[514](https://docs.rs#514)        // PMAT-051: shell variable assignment carries a value Expr;
[515](https://docs.rs#515)        // recurse for completeness (currently the value is always
[516](https://docs.rs#516)        // a shell-domain Expr, so this is always false in practice).
[517](https://docs.rs#517)        Stmt::ShellAssign { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[518](https://docs.rs#518)        // PMAT-048: shell loops compose statements; recurse into
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        // body + (where applicable) cond / items.
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        Stmt::ShellLoop { kind, body } => {
[521](https://docs.rs#521)            let kind_has = match kind {
[522](https://docs.rs#522)                LoopKind::For { items, .. } => items.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith),
[523](https://docs.rs#523)                LoopKind::While { cond } | LoopKind::Until { cond } => expr_has_int_arith(cond),
[524](https://docs.rs#524)            };
[525](https://docs.rs#525)            kind_has || body.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith)
[526](https://docs.rs#526)        }
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    }
[528](https://docs.rs#528)}
[529](https://docs.rs#529)
[530](https://docs.rs#530)fn expr_has_int_arith(e: &Expr) -> bool {
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    match e {
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        Expr::Ident(_) | Expr::LitInt(_) | Expr::LitBool(_) | Expr::Unit => false,
[533](https://docs.rs#533)        // PMAT-502dt: a block-expr recurses into its statements + trailing.
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        Expr::Block(b) => {
[535](https://docs.rs#535)            b.stmts.iter().any(stmt_has_int_arith) || expr_has_int_arith(&b.trailing_return)
[536](https://docs.rs#536)        }
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        // PMAT-477 (R8): float arithmetic is governed by float
[538](https://docs.rs#538)        // semantics (IEEE-754 saturation), not C-PY-INT-ARITH's
[539](https://docs.rs#539)        // integer-overflow analysis. Literal carries no operands;
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        // FloatBinOp recurses defensively (float subtrees never carry
[541](https://docs.rs#541)        // int arithmetic in practice).
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        Expr::LitFloat(_) => false,
[543](https://docs.rs#543)        Expr::FloatBinOp { lhs, rhs, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(lhs) || expr_has_int_arith(rhs),
[544](https://docs.rs#544)        Expr::BinOp { op, lhs, rhs } => {
[545](https://docs.rs#545)            if binop_is_int_arith(*op) {
[546](https://docs.rs#546)                return true;
[547](https://docs.rs#547)            }
[548](https://docs.rs#548)            expr_has_int_arith(lhs) || expr_has_int_arith(rhs)
[549](https://docs.rs#549)        }
[550](https://docs.rs#550)        // PMAT-745: the comparison itself is not int *arithmetic* (it yields a
[551](https://docs.rs#551)        // bool), but its int operand may carry arithmetic — recurse into both.
[552](https://docs.rs#552)        Expr::MixedIntFloatCmp { int, float, .. } => {
[553](https://docs.rs#553)            expr_has_int_arith(int) || expr_has_int_arith(float)
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        }
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        Expr::UnOp { op, operand } => {
[556](https://docs.rs#556)            if matches!(op, UnOp::Neg) {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)                return true;
[558](https://docs.rs#558)            }
[559](https://docs.rs#559)            expr_has_int_arith(operand)
[560](https://docs.rs#560)        }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        Expr::IfExpr {
[562](https://docs.rs#562)            cond,
[563](https://docs.rs#563)            then_expr,
[564](https://docs.rs#564)            else_expr,
[565](https://docs.rs#565)        } => {
[566](https://docs.rs#566)            expr_has_int_arith(cond)
[567](https://docs.rs#567)                || expr_has_int_arith(then_expr)
[568](https://docs.rs#568)                || expr_has_int_arith(else_expr)
[569](https://docs.rs#569)        }
[570](https://docs.rs#570)        Expr::Call { args, .. } => args.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith),
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        // PMAT-042: string-literal Expr variants carry no arithmetic
[572](https://docs.rs#572)        // operands; they're governed by C-BASHRS-POSIX-IDEMPOTENCE
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        // (or, for Python `str` literals at v0.2.0, by
[574](https://docs.rs#574)        // C-XLATE-PY-STR-TO-RUST-STRING), not C-PY-INT-ARITH.
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        Expr::LitStr(_) | Expr::QuotedString { .. } => false,
[576](https://docs.rs#576)        // PMAT-451: string concatenation is a str-domain operation;
[577](https://docs.rs#577)        // operands type as `Type::Str` and never contribute to
[578](https://docs.rs#578)        // C-PY-INT-ARITH's overflow analysis. Recurse defensively in
[579](https://docs.rs#579)        // case future lowering ever nests an int-arith expression
[580](https://docs.rs#580)        // inside a string-typed position (unlikely but cheap).
[581](https://docs.rs#581)        Expr::Concat { lhs, rhs } => expr_has_int_arith(lhs) || expr_has_int_arith(rhs),
[582](https://docs.rs#582)        // PMAT-502bg: list concatenation — recurse into both operands.
[583](https://docs.rs#583)        Expr::ListConcat { lhs, rhs } => expr_has_int_arith(lhs) || expr_has_int_arith(rhs),
[584](https://docs.rs#584)        // PMAT-502bh: str.format — recurse into each formatted arg.
[585](https://docs.rs#585)        Expr::StrFormat { args, .. } => args.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith),
[586](https://docs.rs#586)        // PMAT-502cd: `s[i]` over a string — recurse into both operands
[587](https://docs.rs#587)        // (the index may be an arithmetic expression).
[588](https://docs.rs#588)        Expr::StrCharAt { string, index } => {
[589](https://docs.rs#589)            expr_has_int_arith(string) || expr_has_int_arith(index)
[590](https://docs.rs#590)        }
[591](https://docs.rs#591)        // PMAT-502cl: string-chars — recurse into the string expr.
[592](https://docs.rs#592)        Expr::StrChars { string } => expr_has_int_arith(string),
[593](https://docs.rs#593)        // PMAT-502cm: ord/chr — recurse into the value expr.
[594](https://docs.rs#594)        Expr::Ord { value } | Expr::Chr { value } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        // PMAT-502cv: hex/oct/bin — recurse into the value expr.
[596](https://docs.rs#596)        Expr::IntRadixStr { value, .. } | Expr::IntGroupedStr { value, .. } => {
[597](https://docs.rs#597)            expr_has_int_arith(value)
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        }
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        // PMAT-940: grouped float field — recurse into the value expr.
[600](https://docs.rs#600)        // PMAT-941: scientific float field — recurse into the value expr.
[601](https://docs.rs#601)        // PMAT-965: general float field — recurse into the value expr.
[602](https://docs.rs#602)        Expr::FloatGroupedStr { value, .. }
[603](https://docs.rs#603)        | Expr::FloatSciStr { value, .. }
[604](https://docs.rs#604)        | Expr::FloatGeneralStr { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[605](https://docs.rs#605)        // PMAT-942: space-sign numeric field — recurse into the value expr.
[606](https://docs.rs#606)        Expr::SpaceSignStr { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[607](https://docs.rs#607)        Expr::IntFromStrRadix { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[608](https://docs.rs#608)        // PMAT-502am: formatted f-string field — recurse into the value.
[609](https://docs.rs#609)        Expr::FormatSpec { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[610](https://docs.rs#610)        // PMAT-492: string methods are str-domain; recurse into the
[611](https://docs.rs#611)        // receiver and any args defensively (mirrors Concat).
[612](https://docs.rs#612)        Expr::StrMethod { recv, args, .. } => {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)            expr_has_int_arith(recv) || args.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith)
[614](https://docs.rs#614)        }
[615](https://docs.rs#615)        // PMAT-494: tuple literal — recurse into each element (a tuple of
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        // computed ints can carry overflow-prone arithmetic).
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        Expr::TupleLit(elems) => elems.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith),
[618](https://docs.rs#618)        // PMAT-502q: tuple constant-index — recurse into the tuple expr.
[619](https://docs.rs#619)        Expr::TupleIndex { tuple, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(tuple),
[620](https://docs.rs#620)        // PMAT-496: slice — recurse into collection + bound expressions.
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        // PMAT-502r: bounds are optional (open-ended slices).
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        Expr::Slice {
[623](https://docs.rs#623)            collection, lo, hi, ..
[624](https://docs.rs#624)        } => {
[625](https://docs.rs#625)            expr_has_int_arith(collection)
[626](https://docs.rs#626)                || lo.as_deref().is_some_and(expr_has_int_arith)
[627](https://docs.rs#627)                || hi.as_deref().is_some_and(expr_has_int_arith)
[628](https://docs.rs#628)        }
[629](https://docs.rs#629)        // PMAT-498: numeric builtin — recurse into each arg.
[630](https://docs.rs#630)        Expr::NumBuiltin { args, .. } => args.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith),
[631](https://docs.rs#631)        // PMAT-498b: sum — recurse into the list expression.
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        Expr::Sum { list, start, .. } => {
[633](https://docs.rs#633)            expr_has_int_arith(list) || start.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| expr_has_int_arith(s))
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        }
[635](https://docs.rs#635)        // PMAT-502j: all(xs)/any(xs) — recurse into the bool list.
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        Expr::BoolReduce { list, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(list),
[637](https://docs.rs#637)        // PMAT-502m: int(x)/float(x) — recurse into the converted value.
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        Expr::NumCast { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        // PMAT-502ad: str(x) — recurse into the converted value.
[640](https://docs.rs#640)        // PMAT-582: repr(str) — recurse into the value (a string, no int arith).
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        Expr::ToStr { value, .. } | Expr::ReprStr { value } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[642](https://docs.rs#642)        // PMAT-502ak: round(x) — recurse into the rounded value.
[643](https://docs.rs#643)        Expr::RoundToInt { value } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[644](https://docs.rs#644)        // PMAT-502al: round(x, n) — recurse into the value and ndigits.
[645](https://docs.rs#645)        Expr::RoundToDigits { value, ndigits } => {
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            expr_has_int_arith(value) || expr_has_int_arith(ndigits)
[647](https://docs.rs#647)        }
[648](https://docs.rs#648)        // PMAT-612: round(int, n) — recurse into the value and ndigits. The
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        // banker's-rounding arithmetic itself is done in `i128` (guarded), so
[650](https://docs.rs#650)        // the node does not need bigint treatment beyond its operands.
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        Expr::RoundIntToDigits { value, ndigits } => {
[652](https://docs.rs#652)            expr_has_int_arith(value) || expr_has_int_arith(ndigits)
[653](https://docs.rs#653)        }
[654](https://docs.rs#654)        // PMAT-502k: seq * n — recurse into both the sequence and count.
[655](https://docs.rs#655)        Expr::Repeat { seq, n, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(seq) || expr_has_int_arith(n),
[656](https://docs.rs#656)        // PMAT-502c: sorted — recurse into the list expression.
[657](https://docs.rs#657)        Expr::Sorted { list, key, .. } => {
[658](https://docs.rs#658)            expr_has_int_arith(list) || key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| expr_has_int_arith(&k.body))
[659](https://docs.rs#659)        }
[660](https://docs.rs#660)        Expr::Reversed { list } => expr_has_int_arith(list),
[661](https://docs.rs#661)        // PMAT-549/550: gcd/lcm carry int operands (the `%`/`*` are internal).
[662](https://docs.rs#662)        Expr::Gcd { a, b } | Expr::Lcm { a, b } => expr_has_int_arith(a) || expr_has_int_arith(b),
[663](https://docs.rs#663)        // PMAT-551/552: factorial/isqrt carry an int operand (loop arith internal).
[664](https://docs.rs#664)        Expr::Factorial { n } | Expr::Isqrt { n } => expr_has_int_arith(n),
[665](https://docs.rs#665)        // PMAT-553/554: comb/perm carry int operands (the loop arith is internal).
[666](https://docs.rs#666)        Expr::Comb { n, k } | Expr::Perm { n, k } => expr_has_int_arith(n) || expr_has_int_arith(k),
[667](https://docs.rs#667)        Expr::PowMod { base, exp, modulus } => {
[668](https://docs.rs#668)            expr_has_int_arith(base) || expr_has_int_arith(exp) || expr_has_int_arith(modulus)
[669](https://docs.rs#669)        }
[670](https://docs.rs#670)        // PMAT-502cj: list(range(...)) — recurse into the bound exprs.
[671](https://docs.rs#671)        Expr::RangeList { start, stop, .. } => {
[672](https://docs.rs#672)            expr_has_int_arith(start) || expr_has_int_arith(stop)
[673](https://docs.rs#673)        }
[674](https://docs.rs#674)        // PMAT-502cw: set(xs) — recurse into the list expr.
[675](https://docs.rs#675)        Expr::SetFromList { list } => expr_has_int_arith(list),
[676](https://docs.rs#676)        Expr::SetToList { set } => expr_has_int_arith(set),
[677](https://docs.rs#677)        Expr::DictFromPairs { pairs } => expr_has_int_arith(pairs),
[678](https://docs.rs#678)        Expr::DictMerge { entries } => entries
[679](https://docs.rs#679)            .iter()
[680](https://docs.rs#680)            .any(|(k, v)| k.as_ref().is_some_and(expr_has_int_arith) || expr_has_int_arith(v)),
[681](https://docs.rs#681)        // PMAT-502ab: filter — recurse into the list and predicate body.
[682](https://docs.rs#682)        Expr::Filter { list, lambda } => {
[683](https://docs.rs#683)            expr_has_int_arith(list) || expr_has_int_arith(&lambda.body)
[684](https://docs.rs#684)        }
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        // PMAT-502ac: map — recurse into the list and transform body.
[686](https://docs.rs#686)        Expr::Map { list, lambda } => expr_has_int_arith(list) || expr_has_int_arith(&lambda.body),
[687](https://docs.rs#687)        // PMAT-502ai: enumerate/zip — recurse into the source list(s).
[688](https://docs.rs#688)        Expr::Enumerate { list, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(list),
[689](https://docs.rs#689)        Expr::Zip { left, right } => expr_has_int_arith(left) || expr_has_int_arith(right),
[690](https://docs.rs#690)        Expr::ListMinMax {
[691](https://docs.rs#691)            list, key, default, ..
[692](https://docs.rs#692)        } => {
[693](https://docs.rs#693)            expr_has_int_arith(list)
[694](https://docs.rs#694)                || key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| expr_has_int_arith(&k.body))
[695](https://docs.rs#695)                || default.as_ref().is_some_and(|d| expr_has_int_arith(d))
[696](https://docs.rs#696)        }
[697](https://docs.rs#697)        // PMAT-502u: list query — recurse into the list and the arg.
[698](https://docs.rs#698)        Expr::ListQuery { list, arg, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(list) || expr_has_int_arith(arg),
[699](https://docs.rs#699)        // PMAT-502as: list.pop() — recurse into the list and optional index.
[700](https://docs.rs#700)        Expr::ListPop { list, index } => {
[701](https://docs.rs#701)            expr_has_int_arith(list) || index.as_ref().is_some_and(|i| expr_has_int_arith(i))
[702](https://docs.rs#702)        }
[703](https://docs.rs#703)        // PMAT-502au: dict.pop() — recurse into dict, key, and optional default.
[704](https://docs.rs#704)        Expr::DictPop { dict, key, default } => {
[705](https://docs.rs#705)            expr_has_int_arith(dict)
[706](https://docs.rs#706)                || expr_has_int_arith(key)
[707](https://docs.rs#707)                || default.as_ref().is_some_and(|d| expr_has_int_arith(d))
[708](https://docs.rs#708)        }
[709](https://docs.rs#709)        // PMAT-502ax: dict.setdefault() — recurse into dict, key, default.
[710](https://docs.rs#710)        Expr::DictSetDefault { dict, key, default } => {
[711](https://docs.rs#711)            expr_has_int_arith(dict) || expr_has_int_arith(key) || expr_has_int_arith(default)
[712](https://docs.rs#712)        }
[713](https://docs.rs#713)        // PMAT-500: set literal / membership — recurse defensively.
[714](https://docs.rs#714)        Expr::SetLit(elems) => elems.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith),
[715](https://docs.rs#715)        Expr::SetContains { set, elem } => expr_has_int_arith(set) || expr_has_int_arith(elem),
[716](https://docs.rs#716)        // PMAT-502an: list membership — recurse into both sides.
[717](https://docs.rs#717)        Expr::ListContains { list, elem } => expr_has_int_arith(list) || expr_has_int_arith(elem),
[718](https://docs.rs#718)        // PMAT-502o: str substring containment — recurse into both sides.
[719](https://docs.rs#719)        Expr::StrContains { haystack, needle } => {
[720](https://docs.rs#720)            expr_has_int_arith(haystack) || expr_has_int_arith(needle)
[721](https://docs.rs#721)        }
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        // PMAT-502g: set algebra — recurse into both operands.
[723](https://docs.rs#723)        Expr::SetOp { lhs, rhs, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(lhs) || expr_has_int_arith(rhs),
[724](https://docs.rs#724)        // PMAT-502ep: set predicates — recurse into both operands.
[725](https://docs.rs#725)        Expr::SetPred { lhs, rhs, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(lhs) || expr_has_int_arith(rhs),
[726](https://docs.rs#726)        // PMAT-502eq: shallow copy — recurse into the cloned value.
[727](https://docs.rs#727)        Expr::Clone(inner) => expr_has_int_arith(inner),
[728](https://docs.rs#728)        // PMAT-502ew: Option wrapper — recurse into the `Some(e)` payload.
[729](https://docs.rs#729)        Expr::OptionExpr(inner) => inner.as_deref().is_some_and(expr_has_int_arith),
[730](https://docs.rs#730)        // PMAT-721: Optional truthiness — recurse into the value (the `__v != 0`
[731](https://docs.rs#731)        // body is a comparison, never overflowing int arithmetic).
[732](https://docs.rs#732)        Expr::OptionTruthy { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[733](https://docs.rs#733)        // PMAT-724: `x or default` over Optional — recurse into value + default
[734](https://docs.rs#734)        // (the truthiness body is a non-overflowing comparison).
[735](https://docs.rs#735)        Expr::OptionOrDefault { value, default, .. } => {
[736](https://docs.rs#736)            expr_has_int_arith(value) || expr_has_int_arith(default)
[737](https://docs.rs#737)        }
[738](https://docs.rs#738)        // PMAT-502ex: `is None` test — recurse into the tested value.
[739](https://docs.rs#739)        Expr::IsNone { value, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(value),
[740](https://docs.rs#740)        // PMAT-502ez: unwrap recurses into the inner operand.
[741](https://docs.rs#741)        Expr::OptionUnwrap(inner) => expr_has_int_arith(inner),
[742](https://docs.rs#742)        // PMAT-503b: try/except recurses into both the body and the handler.
[743](https://docs.rs#743)        Expr::TryCatch { body, handler, .. } => {
[744](https://docs.rs#744)            expr_has_int_arith(body) || expr_has_int_arith(handler)
[745](https://docs.rs#745)        }
[746](https://docs.rs#746)        // PMAT-506b: a struct literal's field values may contain int arith;
[747](https://docs.rs#747)        // a field read does not by itself.
[748](https://docs.rs#748)        Expr::StructLit { fields, .. } => fields.iter().any(|(_, v)| expr_has_int_arith(v)),
[749](https://docs.rs#749)        Expr::FieldAccess { obj, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(obj),
[750](https://docs.rs#750)        Expr::MethodCall { obj, args, .. } => {
[751](https://docs.rs#751)            expr_has_int_arith(obj) || args.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith)
[752](https://docs.rs#752)        }
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        // PMAT-513: an enum member access is a constant — no int arithmetic.
[754](https://docs.rs#754)        Expr::EnumVariant { .. } => false,
[755](https://docs.rs#755)        // PMAT-455 (v0.2.0 Track 1.B): list literal — recurse into
[756](https://docs.rs#756)        // each element. An int-typed element (`[1, 2, 3]`) doesn't
[757](https://docs.rs#757)        // by itself involve overflow-prone arithmetic, but a list of
[758](https://docs.rs#758)        // computed values (`[a + b, c * d]`) does.
[759](https://docs.rs#759)        Expr::ListLit(elems) => elems.iter().any(expr_has_int_arith),
[760](https://docs.rs#760)        // PMAT-462 (v0.2.0 Track 1.C): dict literal — recurse into
[761](https://docs.rs#761)        // each key + value expression.
[762](https://docs.rs#762)        Expr::DictLit(pairs) => pairs
[763](https://docs.rs#763)            .iter()
[764](https://docs.rs#764)            .any(|(k, v)| expr_has_int_arith(k) || expr_has_int_arith(v)),
[765](https://docs.rs#765)        // PMAT-457 (v0.2.0 Track 1.B): list indexed access. Neither
[766](https://docs.rs#766)        // collection nor index expressions are themselves arithmetic;
[767](https://docs.rs#767)        // recurse defensively for computed indices like `xs[a + b]`.
[768](https://docs.rs#768)        Expr::Index { collection, index } => {
[769](https://docs.rs#769)            expr_has_int_arith(collection) || expr_has_int_arith(index)
[770](https://docs.rs#770)        }
[771](https://docs.rs#771)        // PMAT-466 (v0.2.0 Track 1.C): dict ops. The lookup/membership
[772](https://docs.rs#772)        // operations are not themselves arithmetic; recurse into the
[773](https://docs.rs#773)        // sub-expressions (a computed key or default may carry it).
[774](https://docs.rs#774)        Expr::DictGet { dict, key } => expr_has_int_arith(dict) || expr_has_int_arith(key),
[775](https://docs.rs#775)        // PMAT-502ey: 1-arg dict get — recurse into dict + key.
[776](https://docs.rs#776)        Expr::DictGetOpt { dict, key } => expr_has_int_arith(dict) || expr_has_int_arith(key),
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        Expr::DictGetOr { dict, key, default } => {
[778](https://docs.rs#778)            expr_has_int_arith(dict) || expr_has_int_arith(key) || expr_has_int_arith(default)
[779](https://docs.rs#779)        }
[780](https://docs.rs#780)        Expr::DictContains { dict, key } => expr_has_int_arith(dict) || expr_has_int_arith(key),
[781](https://docs.rs#781)        // PMAT-502v: dict view — recurse into the dict expression.
[782](https://docs.rs#782)        Expr::DictView { dict, .. } => expr_has_int_arith(dict),
[783](https://docs.rs#783)        // PMAT-459 (v0.2.0 Track 1.B): len() of a collection is not
[784](https://docs.rs#784)        // itself arithmetic; recurse defensively into the inner expr.
[785](https://docs.rs#785)        Expr::Len(inner) => expr_has_int_arith(inner),
[786](https://docs.rs#786)        Expr::FileReadAll(inner) => expr_has_int_arith(inner),
[787](https://docs.rs#787)        Expr::FileReadLines(inner) => expr_has_int_arith(inner),
[788](https://docs.rs#788)        // PMAT-045: shell-variable references same disposition.
[789](https://docs.rs#789)        Expr::ShellVar(_) => false,
[790](https://docs.rs#790)        // PMAT-055: shell special parameters same disposition.
[791](https://docs.rs#791)        Expr::ShellSpecial(_) => false,
[792](https://docs.rs#792)        // PMAT-047: command substitution composes a Stmt; recurse
[793](https://docs.rs#793)        // into the inner Stmt for completeness (currently every
[794](https://docs.rs#794)        // such Stmt is a shell-domain Cmd, so this is always
[795](https://docs.rs#795)        // false in practice).
[796](https://docs.rs#796)        Expr::CommandSubstitution(inner) => stmt_has_int_arith(inner),
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    }
[798](https://docs.rs#798)}
[799](https://docs.rs#799)
[800](https://docs.rs#800)fn binop_is_int_arith(op: BinOp) -> bool {
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    matches!(
[802](https://docs.rs#802)        op,
[803](https://docs.rs#803)        BinOp::Add
[804](https://docs.rs#804)            | BinOp::Sub
[805](https://docs.rs#805)            | BinOp::Mul
[806](https://docs.rs#806)            | BinOp::FloorDiv
[807](https://docs.rs#807)            | BinOp::Mod
[808](https://docs.rs#808)            | BinOp::BitAnd
[809](https://docs.rs#809)            | BinOp::BitOr
[810](https://docs.rs#810)            | BinOp::BitXor
[811](https://docs.rs#811)            | BinOp::Shl
[812](https://docs.rs#812)            | BinOp::Shr
[813](https://docs.rs#813)            | BinOp::Pow
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    )
[815](https://docs.rs#815)}
[816](https://docs.rs#816)
[817](https://docs.rs#817)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[818](https://docs.rs#818)pub struct Block {
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    /// Zero or more `let` bindings (and, in the future, control-flow
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    /// statements) executed before the trailing return.
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    /// The expression whose value is the function's return value.
[823](https://docs.rs#823)    pub trailing_return: Expr,
[824](https://docs.rs#824)}
[825](https://docs.rs#825)
[826](https://docs.rs#826)// PMAT-047: PartialEq needed so `Expr::CommandSubstitution(Box<Stmt>)`
[827](https://docs.rs#827)// participates in Expr's existing `PartialEq` derive. Every field
[828](https://docs.rs#828)// of every Stmt variant is itself PartialEq (String, Type, Expr,
[829](https://docs.rs#829)// Vec<Stmt>), so the derive is mechanical.
[830](https://docs.rs#830)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[831](https://docs.rs#831)pub enum Stmt {
[832](https://docs.rs#832)    /// `return <expr>;` as an **early** return — a mid-body return,
[833](https://docs.rs#833)    /// typically inside an [`Stmt::If`] branch (a guard clause:
[834](https://docs.rs#834)    /// `if (n <= 1) { return 1; } return n * …;`). PMAT-479 (R10).
[835](https://docs.rs#835)    ///
[836](https://docs.rs#836)    /// The function's *final* value still flows through
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    /// [`Block::trailing_return`]; this variant is only for the
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    /// non-final returns. Rust/Ruchy emit `return <expr>;` (the trailing
[839](https://docs.rs#839)    /// expression remains the fallthrough value). Lean refuses (early
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    /// return needs a match/monadic encoding; Lean keeps the
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    /// single-trailing-return shape at v0.2.0).
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    Return(Expr),
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    /// `if cond { then_body } else { else_body }` — an if/else as a
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    /// *statement* (not the if-as-let-expression form). PMAT-478 (R9).
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    /// Produced by the decy C frontend for `if (c) { … } else { … }`
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    /// (C has no if-expression); the Python frontend keeps its
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    /// if-as-let lowering for the assignment shape. `else_body` is empty
[848](https://docs.rs#848)    /// for an `if` with no `else`.
[849](https://docs.rs#849)    ///
[850](https://docs.rs#850)    /// Backends: Rust/Ruchy emit `if cond { … } else { … }`; Lean
[851](https://docs.rs#851)    /// refuses (the executable-subset encoding routes branches through
[852](https://docs.rs#852)    /// the if-expression form, not statement-if) at v0.2.0.
[853](https://docs.rs#853)    If {
[854](https://docs.rs#854)        cond: Expr,
[855](https://docs.rs#855)        then_body: Vec<Stmt>,
[856](https://docs.rs#856)        else_body: Vec<Stmt>,
[857](https://docs.rs#857)    },
[858](https://docs.rs#858)    /// `continue;` — Python `continue`. PMAT-502bk (Tranche 2). Skips to
[859](https://docs.rs#859)    /// the next loop iteration. Rust/Ruchy emit `continue;`. The frontend
[860](https://docs.rs#860)    /// rejects it inside a `range(...)` for-loop (which desugars to a
[861](https://docs.rs#861)    /// `while` with a tail counter-increment that `continue` would skip);
[862](https://docs.rs#862)    /// it is allowed inside list/dict for-loops (real Rust `for`) and
[863](https://docs.rs#863)    /// `while` loops. Lean refuses (no loop-control encoding).
[864](https://docs.rs#864)    Continue,
[865](https://docs.rs#865)    /// `break;` — Python `break`. PMAT-502bk (Tranche 2). Exits the
[866](https://docs.rs#866)    /// nearest loop. Rust/Ruchy emit `break;` (always safe). Lean refuses.
[867](https://docs.rs#867)    Break,
[868](https://docs.rs#868)    /// `print(a, b, …, sep=…, end=…)` — Python's `print` builtin.
[869](https://docs.rs#869)    /// PMAT-502bw (Tranche 2); PMAT-502by added `sep`/`end`. Rust/Ruchy
[870](https://docs.rs#870)    /// build a format string joining the args with `sep` and either use
[871](https://docs.rs#871)    /// `println!` (when `end == "\n"`, the Python default) or `print!` with
[872](https://docs.rs#872)    /// `end` appended (any other terminator, e.g. `end=""`). An empty `args`
[873](https://docs.rs#873)    /// (bare `print()`) emits `println!();` (or `print!("…end…")`).
[874](https://docs.rs#874)    /// PMAT-502bx: the frontend admits `I64`/`Str` (incl. f-strings →
[875](https://docs.rs#875)    /// `String`) directly, wraps `F64` via `str(float)` and `Bool` via the
[876](https://docs.rs#876)    /// `str(bool)` desugar, so Python's `2.0`/`True` formatting is matched;
[877](https://docs.rs#877)    /// `sep`/`end` must be string literals (non-literal + `file=` deferred).
[878](https://docs.rs#878)    /// Lean refuses (pure `def`s have no `IO`).
[879](https://docs.rs#879)    Print {
[880](https://docs.rs#880)        args: Vec<Expr>,
[881](https://docs.rs#881)        sep: String,
[882](https://docs.rs#882)        end: String,
[883](https://docs.rs#883)    },
[884](https://docs.rs#884)    /// `let [mut] name: ty = value;` — first binding of `name` in this
[885](https://docs.rs#885)    /// scope. `mutable` is set by the frontend when the same name is
[886](https://docs.rs#886)    /// reassigned later in the function (including inside a [`While`]
[887](https://docs.rs#887)    /// loop body). Rust/Ruchy emission honors it (`let mut` vs `let`)
[888](https://docs.rs#888)    /// to keep `clippy -D unused_mut` happy. PMAT-006.
[889](https://docs.rs#889)    Let {
[890](https://docs.rs#890)        name: String,
[891](https://docs.rs#891)        ty: Type,
[892](https://docs.rs#892)        value: Expr,
[893](https://docs.rs#893)        #[serde(default)]
[894](https://docs.rs#894)        mutable: bool,
[895](https://docs.rs#895)    },
[896](https://docs.rs#896)    /// `name = value;` — reassignment of a name previously introduced
[897](https://docs.rs#897)    /// by [`Stmt::Let`]. PMAT-006.
[898](https://docs.rs#898)    Assign { name: String, value: Expr },
[899](https://docs.rs#899)    /// `let name = |p0: t0, p1: t1, …| { body };` — a first-class closure
[900](https://docs.rs#900)    /// bound to a local. PMAT-504 (Tranche 2). The Python source is
[901](https://docs.rs#901)    /// `name = lambda p0, p1, …: <body>`. Each parameter carries its
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    /// inferred type (`params: Vec<(name, type)>`, possibly empty for a
[903](https://docs.rs#903)    /// nullary `lambda: <body>`); the return type is left to Rust's
[904](https://docs.rs#904)    /// inference (no `-> R` annotation). The closure is then callable as
[905](https://docs.rs#905)    /// `name(args…)` via the existing [`Expr::Call`] machinery (the
[906](https://docs.rs#906)    /// frontend records the return type so the call site types
[907](https://docs.rs#907)    /// correctly). Rust/Ruchy emit `let <name> = |<params>| { <body> };`;
[908](https://docs.rs#908)    /// Lean refuses (first-class functions are a v0.3.0 sub-track).
[909](https://docs.rs#909)    ClosureLet {
[910](https://docs.rs#910)        name: String,
[911](https://docs.rs#911)        /// `(name, type, mutable)` — `mutable` is `true` when the parameter is
[912](https://docs.rs#912)        /// reassigned in the body (PMAT-749), so the backend emits `|mut p: T|`
[913](https://docs.rs#913)        /// (else rustc E0384 "cannot assign to immutable argument").
[914](https://docs.rs#914)        params: Vec<(String, Type, bool)>,
[915](https://docs.rs#915)        body: Expr,
[916](https://docs.rs#916)    },
[917](https://docs.rs#917)    /// PMAT-736 (HUNT-V11 V11-6): a **named** inner function item — Python
[918](https://docs.rs#918)    /// `def inner(p: T, …) -> R: …` nested in a function body, lowered to a
[919](https://docs.rs#919)    /// named Rust `fn` (NOT a closure) so it can **recurse by name**. A closure
[920](https://docs.rs#920)    /// (`Stmt::ClosureLet`) cannot reference its own binding while it is being
[921](https://docs.rs#921)    /// defined, so a self-call `inner(k-1)` inside a `let inner = |k| …` is an
[922](https://docs.rs#922)    /// E0425; a named inner `fn` is in scope for its whole body and recurses
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    /// cleanly. Unlike a closure, a named inner fn **cannot capture** enclosing
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    /// variables (Rust E0434) — the frontend only emits this variant when the
[925](https://docs.rs#925)    /// nested def is self-referential AND captures nothing (else it stays a
[926](https://docs.rs#926)    /// `ClosureLet`, or — recursive + capturing — is rejected with a clear
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    /// message). Rust/Ruchy emit `fn <name>(<params>) -> R { <body> }`; Lean
[928](https://docs.rs#928)    /// refuses (first-class / nested functions are a v0.3.0 sub-track).
[929](https://docs.rs#929)    NestedFn {
[930](https://docs.rs#930)        name: String,
[931](https://docs.rs#931)        /// `(name, type, mutable)` — `mutable` true when the parameter is
[932](https://docs.rs#932)        /// reassigned in the body (PMAT-749), so the backend emits `mut p: T`.
[933](https://docs.rs#933)        params: Vec<(String, Type, bool)>,
[934](https://docs.rs#934)        ret: Type,
[935](https://docs.rs#935)        body: Block,
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    },
[937](https://docs.rs#937)    /// Tuple-destructuring binding — Python `a, b = <expr>`. PMAT-494b
[938](https://docs.rs#938)    /// (sprint). `value` types as [`Type::Tuple`] with arity matching
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    /// `names`. Rust/Ruchy emit `let (a, b, ...) = <value>;`, marking
[940](https://docs.rs#940)    /// `names[i]` `mut` when `mutable[i]` (PMAT-547: a later
[941](https://docs.rs#941)    /// reassignment/augment of an unpacked name); Lean refuses. Nested /
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    /// starred / subscript patterns are not supported at first cut (all
[943](https://docs.rs#943)    /// targets must be plain names). `mutable` is parallel to `names`.
[944](https://docs.rs#944)    LetTuple {
[945](https://docs.rs#945)        names: Vec<String>,
[946](https://docs.rs#946)        mutable: Vec<bool>,
[947](https://docs.rs#947)        value: Expr,
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    },

[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)    /// `{ let __v = <value>; let __p = <list>.iter().position(|__e| *__e == __v).expect("…"); <list>.remove(__p); }`.
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)    /// Distinct from set `.remove` ([`Stmt::SetRemove`], which removes by
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)    /// key); the frontend's receiver type disambiguates. Lean refuses
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)    /// (in-place mutation, same gap as `ListAppend`).
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)    ListRemoveValue { list_name: String, value: Expr },
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)    /// `for var in iter { body }` — Python `for x in xs:` over a
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)    /// non-range iterable. PMAT-458, v0.2.0 Track 1.B.
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)    ///
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)    /// The frontend reserves `range(...)`-shaped iters for the
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)    /// existing Let+While desugaring (PMAT-007); ForEach is for
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)    /// list-typed (and later other collection-typed) iter
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)    /// expressions. The `elem_ty` is the inferred element type of
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)    /// `iter`, threaded so the backend knows what to bind `var` to.
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)    ///
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)    /// Backends:
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)    ///   * Rust / Ruchy: `for var in iter.iter().cloned() { body }`
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)    ///   * Lean: refuses at v0.2.0 first cut — Lean iteration without
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)    ///     `partial def` machinery is a v0.3.0 sub-track (Lean has
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)    ///     no for-loop primitive; `forM` / list-recursion is the
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)    ///     idiomatic encoding, and the body must be encoded as a
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)    ///     monadic action).
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)    ///   * Shell: refuses (already not a Python-flow target).
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)    ///
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)    /// Governing contract: `C-XLATE-PY-LIST-TO-VEC` —
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)    /// iteration_order_preserved Bronze theorem implies the lowered
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)    /// `for x in vec.iter()` produces the same element sequence as
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)    /// the source Python iteration.
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)    ForEach {
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)        var: String,
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)        iter: Expr,

[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)        body: Vec<Stmt>,
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)        /// PMAT-472 (R3): when `iter` is a dict, the loop iterates its
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)        /// **keys** (Python `for k in d:`), so Rust/Ruchy emit
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)        /// `iter.keys().cloned()` instead of `iter.iter().cloned()`,
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)        /// and `elem_ty` is the key type. `false` for the list case.
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)        /// NOTE: HashMap key order is unspecified — a `for k in d:` loop
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)        /// observes keys in arbitrary order (matching CPython ≥3.7 only

[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)        #[serde(default)]
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)        over_keys: bool,
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)        /// PMAT-743 (HUNT-V12 V12-8): when set to a dict name, the loop body

[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)        /// (PMAT-742) — so a SIZE change (inserting a new key / deleting a key)
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)        /// during iteration would silently succeed against the snapshot, whereas
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)        /// Python raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`.
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)        /// Rust/Ruchy emit a runtime size guard: capture `<dict>.len()` before the
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)        /// loop and, after each iteration's body, panic if the length changed (a
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)        /// size-stable VALUE-update — PMAT-742 — leaves it unchanged, so the guard
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)        /// is silent there). `None` for a list iteration or a read-only dict loop.
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)        #[serde(default)]
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)        dict_guard: Option<String>,
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)        /// PMAT-816 (HUNT-V21 #3/4/8): the loop body mutates each element IN

[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)        /// `iter().cloned()` binds `var` to an owned clone, so the mutation was
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)        /// discarded AND `var` is not `mut` (rustc E0596). When set, the backend
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)        /// emits `iter.iter_mut()` so `var` is `&mut elem` and the mutation
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)        /// propagates to the original collection (which is marked `mut`). Only
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)        /// set for a list-typed iterable that is a plain lvalue and a body that
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)        /// mutates `var` via a known mutating method / subscript-assign.
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)        #[serde(default)]
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)        mutate_elems: bool,
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)    },

[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)    /// PMAT-1058 (exceptions epic): a STATEMENT-position `try`/`except` whose
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)    /// arms are side-effecting statement BLOCKS — `try: <stmts> except E [as e]:
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)    /// <stmts>`. The value-producing [`Expr::TryCatch`] covers `try: x = e
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)    /// except: x = e` and `try: return e except: return e`; this covers the

[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)        /// `handler`/`except_types`/`bound_name` fields above). The Err arm

[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)        /// (`handler`/`except_types` empty = catch-all, which SWALLOWS). The

[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)pub struct Param {
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)    pub name: String,
