[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)    /// PMAT-460 (v0.2.0 Track 1.B): set to `true` when the function
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)    /// mutates this parameter in-place (currently only via
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)    /// `xs.append(...)`). Rust/Ruchy backends emit `mut name: T` so
[1488](https://docs.rs#1488)    /// the `.push()` call type-checks. Lean ignores (in-place
[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)    /// mutation isn't supported there at v0.2.0).
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)    #[serde(default)]
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)    pub mutable: bool,
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)}
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)/// MVP type lattice. Will grow as frontends demand it. Keep semantically
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)/// minimal; map source-language type idiosyncrasies (Python int bigint
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)/// promotion, C signed/unsigned, etc.) at the frontend boundary.
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)/// PMAT-455 — `Type` is no longer `Copy` because `Type::List(Box<Type>)`
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)/// is heap-allocated. Callers that previously relied on `*ty` to
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)/// dereference / copy now use `.clone()` (cheap — most Type values
[1500](https://docs.rs#1500)/// are leaf variants or 1-deep boxes).
[1501](https://docs.rs#1501)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[1502](https://docs.rs#1502)pub enum Type {
[1503](https://docs.rs#1503)    /// 64-bit signed integer. The fast path for Python `int` — covers
[1504](https://docs.rs#1504)    /// every case where the frontend can prove the value fits.
[1505](https://docs.rs#1505)    ///
[1506](https://docs.rs#1506)    /// NOTE: `decy-frontend` also lowers C `int` (a 32-bit type) to `I64`
[1507](https://docs.rs#1507)    /// — the backend narrows it to `i32` on the `SourceLang::C` emit path,
[1508](https://docs.rs#1508)    /// and `c_abi_type` maps it back to `c_int` at an FFI boundary. A
[1509](https://docs.rs#1509)    /// genuinely 64-bit C integer is modeled distinctly as [`Type::CLong`]
[1510](https://docs.rs#1510)    /// (PMAT-909) so the FFI ABI is not forced to narrow it.
[1511](https://docs.rs#1511)    I64,
[1512](https://docs.rs#1512)    /// A C `long` / `int64_t` — a 64-bit-ABI integer modeled DISTINCTLY
[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)    /// from the 32-bit-`int`-backed [`Type::I64`] (PMAT-909). decy-frontend
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)    /// produces it for `long` / `long long` / `int64_t` declarations; the
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)    /// FFI manifest maps it to `c_longlong` (a 64-bit C ABI slot) instead
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)    /// of narrowing every C integer to `c_int`, and the Rust/Ruchy backends
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)    /// render it as `i64` (Lean: `Int`). It is value-compatible with `I64`
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)    /// (both ride an `i64` native wrapper) — the only distinction is the C
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)    /// ABI width preserved at a foreign boundary.
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)    CLong,
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)    /// A C `unsigned` / `unsigned int` / `uint32_t` — a 32-bit UNSIGNED
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)    /// integer modeled DISTINCTLY from the signed-`int`-backed [`Type::I64`]
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)    /// (PMAT-918), exactly as [`Type::CLong`] is kept apart from `I64` for the
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)    /// 64-bit width and [`Type::F32`] from [`Type::F64`] for the float widths.
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)    /// decy-frontend produces it for `unsigned` / `unsigned int` / `uint32_t`
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)    /// declarations; the FFI manifest maps it to the UNSIGNED `c_uint` ABI slot
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)    /// (NEVER the signed `c_int` — a value ≥ 2³¹ would otherwise be
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)    /// reinterpreted as negative at the boundary), and the Rust/Ruchy backends
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)    /// render it as `u32` (Lean: `Nat`, the non-negative shape). Unlike the
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)    /// signed C widths, unsigned arithmetic is DEFINED-MODULAR by the C
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)    /// standard (not overflow UB), so the `u32` C-emit path's `wrapping_*`
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)    /// methods are the exact C semantics. Governed by the same on-disk
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)    /// `C-C-INT-ARITH` (the two's-complement modular-arithmetic family).
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)    CUInt,
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)    /// A C `unsigned long` / `unsigned long long` / `uint64_t` — a 64-bit
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)    /// UNSIGNED integer modeled DISTINCTLY from both the 32-bit-unsigned
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)    /// [`Type::CUInt`] (PMAT-918) and the 64-bit-SIGNED [`Type::CLong`]
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)    /// (PMAT-909) (PMAT-921). It is the 64-bit dual of `CUInt` exactly as
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)    /// `CLong` is the 64-bit dual of the 32-bit-signed-`int`-backed `I64`.
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)    /// decy-frontend produces it for `unsigned long` / `unsigned long long` /
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)    /// `uint64_t` declarations; the FFI manifest maps it to the UNSIGNED
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)    /// `c_ulonglong` ABI slot (NEVER the signed `c_longlong` — a value ≥ 2⁶³
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)    /// would otherwise be reinterpreted as negative at the boundary — and
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)    /// NEVER the 32-bit `c_uint`, which would truncate), and the Rust/Ruchy
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)    /// backends render it as `u64` (Lean: `Nat`, the non-negative shape).
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)    /// Like `CUInt`, unsigned arithmetic is DEFINED-MODULAR by the C standard
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)    /// (not overflow UB), so the `u64` C-emit path's `wrapping_*` methods are
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)    /// the exact C semantics. Governed by the same on-disk `C-C-INT-ARITH`.
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)    CULong,
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)    /// Boolean — produced by comparison ops in [`Expr::BinOp`].
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)    Bool,
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)    /// IEEE-754 double — Python `float`. PMAT-477 (R8). Rust/Ruchy emit
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)    /// `f64`; Lean emits `Float`. Arithmetic (`Expr::FloatBinOp`) is
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)    /// plain infix (no overflow/checked path — floats saturate to
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)    /// ±inf, they don't wrap). Comparisons reuse `Expr::BinOp` (plain
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)    /// infix `<`/`==`/… already type-correct for `f64`, yielding
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)    /// `Bool`). No governing contract yet (capability-ahead-of-
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)    /// contract); a `C-PY-FLOAT-ARITH` substrate is queued.
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)    F64,
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)    /// A C `float` — a 32-bit single-precision IEEE-754 float, modeled
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)    /// DISTINCTLY from the 64-bit [`Type::F64`] (PMAT-911), exactly as
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)    /// [`Type::CLong`] is kept apart from [`Type::I64`] for the integer
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)    /// widths. decy-frontend produces it for `float` declarations; the FFI
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)    /// manifest maps it to `c_float` (a 32-bit C ABI slot) instead of
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)    /// narrowing every C float to `c_double`, and the Rust/Ruchy backends
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)    /// render it as `f32` (Lean: `Float`, its only float shape). The C emit
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)    /// path rides `f32` IEEE arithmetic. Like F64 it has no governing
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)    /// contract yet — C float arithmetic cites the queued `C-C-FLOAT-ARITH`
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)    /// (uncited until authored), NOT the Python `C-PY-FLOAT-ARITH` (which a
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)    /// C-sourced `float` must never claim).
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)    F32,
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)    /// Unbounded integer — Python `int`'s native shape. The slow path
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)    /// of contract `C-PY-INT-ARITH`. Rust/Ruchy emit
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)    /// `xpile_bigint::BigInt`; Lean emits `Int` (which is already
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)    /// unbounded). PMAT-012.
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)    BigInt,
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)    /// Owned UTF-8 string — Python `str`'s native shape. PMAT-449,
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)    /// the v0.2.0 Track 1.A foundation
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)    /// ([`sub/v0.2.0-depyler-merger.md`](../../docs/specifications/sub/v0.2.0-depyler-merger.md)).
[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)    ///
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)    /// Distinct from [`Type::ShellString`] (which carries an implicit
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)    /// quoting strategy and bashrs-domain semantics). `Type::Str`
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)    /// values are UTF-8 owned strings — Rust/Ruchy emit `String`,
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)    /// Lean emits `String`. v0.2.0 starts with owned-only; `&str`
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)    /// borrowing is the stretch sub-track 1.D.
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)    ///
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)    /// Currently produced by `depyler-frontend` for Python `str`
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)    /// annotations and `"..."` literals. Other frontends are free to
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)    /// produce it when they wire up real string parsing.
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)    ///
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)    /// Governing contract (Layer 2 translation, code lane): the v0.2.0
[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)    /// `C-XLATE-PY-STR-TO-RUST-STRING` contract once authored.
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)    Str,
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)    /// Typed dictionary / map — Python `dict[K, V]`. PMAT-462,
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)    /// v0.2.0 Track 1.C foundation
[1596](https://docs.rs#1596)    /// ([`sub/v0.2.0-depyler-merger.md`](../../docs/specifications/sub/v0.2.0-depyler-merger.md)
[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)    /// Track 1.C).
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)    ///
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)    /// `Type::Dict(Box<Type>, Box<Type>)` represents Python

[1601](https://docs.rs#1601)    /// Lean `List (K × V)` (first cut — Lean's `Std.HashMap` is a
[1602](https://docs.rs#1602)    /// v0.3.0+ refinement once iteration / lookup encoding lands).

[1604](https://docs.rs#1604)    /// they'd require a `Box<dyn Any>`-style boxing rejected by

[1606](https://docs.rs#1606)    /// contract's `homogeneous_keys_values_rejected` equation.
[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)    ///
[1608](https://docs.rs#1608)    /// At v0.2.0 first cut both `K` and `V` are restricted to
[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)    /// `Type::I64`, `Type::Bool`, or `Type::Str`; nested dicts /
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)    /// lists as values are subsequent sub-tracks.
[1611](https://docs.rs#1611)    ///
[1612](https://docs.rs#1612)    /// Governing contract: `C-XLATE-PY-DICT-TO-HASHMAP` (to be
[1613](https://docs.rs#1613)    /// authored alongside this PR's substrate ratchet).
[1614](https://docs.rs#1614)    Dict(Box<Type>, Box<Type>),
[1615](https://docs.rs#1615)    /// Homogeneous list / vector. PMAT-455, v0.2.0 Track 1.B

[1617](https://docs.rs#1617)    ///
[1618](https://docs.rs#1618)    /// `Type::List(Box<Type>)` represents Python `list[T]` and lowers

[1624](https://docs.rs#1624)    ///

[1629](https://docs.rs#1629)    ///

[1631](https://docs.rs#1631)    /// at depth-13).
[1632](https://docs.rs#1632)    List(Box<Type>),
[1633](https://docs.rs#1633)    /// `Type::Set(Box<Type>)` represents Python `set[T]` and lowers to a

[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)    /// read-side first cut (literal + membership). Lean refuses.
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)    Set(Box<Type>),
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)    /// `Type::Tuple(Vec<Type>)` represents Python `tuple[T0, T1, ...]` and
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)    /// lowers to a Rust/Ruchy anonymous tuple `(T0, T1, ...)`. PMAT-494
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)    /// (sprint), first cut: fixed-arity heterogeneous tuples in return /

[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)    /// at first cut (Prod encoding deferred). Tuple *unpacking* (`a, b =
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)    /// f()`) is a follow-up slice.
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)    Tuple(Vec<Type>),
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)    /// POSIX shell string — quoted-aware string type for the bashrs
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)    /// domain. PMAT-046 / XPILE-BASHRS-MERGER-001 Layer B.
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)    ///
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)    /// Distinct from a generic `String` (which xpile doesn't have at
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)    /// v0.1.0): a `ShellString` value semantically carries an
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)    /// implicit `QuotingStrategy` and a shellcheck-equivalent
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)    /// validity claim. The v0.1.0 type is *load-bearing for future
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)    /// signatures* — when bashrs-frontend gains a real parser that
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)    /// types shell variables, it'll annotate them as
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)    /// `Type::ShellString`. Until then this variant is unused at the
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)    /// surface but present in the IR for the Bronze→Silver
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)    /// refinement of `C-BASHRS-POSIX-IDEMPOTENCE` (the typed POSIX
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)    /// state needed in `contracts/lean/Bashrs.lean` to model
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)    /// concrete shell semantics, not just abstract Outcomes).
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)    ///
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)    /// Other backends refuse `Type::ShellString` via `Unsupported`
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)    /// arms naming the bashrs contract.
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)    ShellString,
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)    /// POSIX exit code (i32 range, conventionally 0..=255). PMAT-046
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)    /// / XPILE-BASHRS-MERGER-001 Layer B.
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)    ///
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)    /// Same posture as `ShellString` — present for future signatures
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)    /// where shell-domain functions need a typed exit status (the
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)    /// Silver-tier Lean model's `Outcome` will carry an `ExitCode`
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)    /// field rather than just an opaque `observable: String`).
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)    ///
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)    /// Other backends refuse `Type::ExitCode` via `Unsupported` arms.
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)    ExitCode,
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)    /// The unit type — Python `None` as a return annotation (a void
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)    /// function). PMAT-502bl (Tranche 2). Rust/Ruchy emit `()`; Lean
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)    /// refuses (a side-effecting void function has no total-function
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)    /// encoding). Carried only by `Function::return_type`.
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)    Unit,
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)    /// PMAT-502ew: Python `Optional[T]` (a value that may be `None`).

[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)    /// (PMAT-502ew) supports it only as a function *return* type, with the
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)    /// returned values wrapped via [`Expr::OptionExpr`] (`Some(x)` / `None`);
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)    /// `Optional` parameters / locals and `is None` flow-narrowing are a
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)    /// deferred follow-up.
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)    Optional(Box<Type>),
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)    /// PMAT-506b (classes epic): a named struct type — a value of a Python
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)    /// `@dataclass` / class lowered via [`Item::Struct`]. Carries the struct's
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)    /// name; Rust/Ruchy emit the bare name (`Point`); Lean refuses (struct
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)    /// values deferred). Produced for struct-typed params/returns/locals,
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)    /// [`Expr::StructLit`] construction, and [`Expr::FieldAccess`] receivers.
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)    Struct(String),
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)    /// PMAT-924: an 8-bit C `char` — modeled DISTINCTLY because it is neither
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)    /// the 32-bit-`int`-backed [`Type::I64`] nor any other integer width. It has
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)    /// no Python analogue, so it appears ONLY as the pointee of a [`Type::Ptr`]
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)    /// (`char*`, the canonical C-string / byte-buffer pointer); a bare `char`
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)    /// value is refused by `decy-frontend`. The FFI manifest maps it to the
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)    /// platform-signedness-honest `c_char` ABI slot. It is not a standalone
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)    /// value type in any code-emit lane (Rust/Ruchy/Lean), only an ABI pointee.
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)    CChar,
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)    /// PMAT-924: a C pointer — the FIRST address-carrying (non-value) ABI token
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)    /// in the meta-HIR, lifting the last decy scalar ceiling
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)    /// (PMAT-909/911/918/921 lifted every integer/float WIDTH; this lifts the
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)    /// pointer INDIRECTION). `decy-frontend` produces it for a trailing `*` on a
[1702](https://docs.rs#1702)    /// scalar base type (`int*`, `char*`, `double*`, …); the pointee is
[1703](https://docs.rs#1703)    /// restricted to an ABI-mappable scalar (the integer/float widths + `CChar`)
[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)    /// — pointer-to-pointer, pointer-to-container, and pointer-to-struct are
[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)    /// REFUSED rather than mis-emitted, exactly as the scalar lifts refused
[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)    /// non-ABI-mappable types. `mutable` distinguishes `int*` (`*mut`, the bare
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)    /// default) from a future `const int*` (`*const`); the FFI manifest maps it
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)    /// to `*mut`/`*const <pointee-ABI-type>` and the Rust/Ruchy backends render
[1709](https://docs.rs#1709)    /// the raw pointer type (sound to DECLARE in a signature — only deref is
[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)    /// `unsafe`). Lean refuses (no total-function pointer model). Carries no
[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)    /// governing contract yet (capability-ahead-of-contract, like F32/F64).
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)    Ptr {
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)        /// `true` for a `*mut` pointer (a bare C `int*`); `false` for a `*const`
[1714](https://docs.rs#1714)        /// pointer (a `const`-qualified pointee, a deferred refinement).
[1715](https://docs.rs#1715)        mutable: bool,
[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)        /// The pointed-to type — restricted to an ABI-mappable scalar.
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)        pointee: Box<Type>,
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)    },
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)}

[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)pub enum Expr {
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)    /// The unit value `()` — the trailing "return" of a void function
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)    /// (Python `-> None`). PMAT-502bl (Tranche 2). Rust/Ruchy emit `()`;
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)    /// Lean refuses. Types as [`Type::Unit`].
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)    Unit,
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)    /// A block expression — zero or more statements followed by a trailing
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)    /// value. PMAT-502dt (Tranche 2). Rust/Ruchy emit `{ <stmts> <trailing> }`;
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)    /// types as the trailing expression's type. The first producer is the
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)    /// multi-statement nested-function body (`ClosureLet`'s body). A reusable
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)    /// primitive for future expression-position comprehensions. Lean refuses.
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)    Block(Box<Block>),
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)    /// Local identifier reference (function parameter or future `let`).
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)    Ident(String),
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)    /// Integer literal, lowered as i64 at the boundary.
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)    LitInt(i64),

[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)    /// `len(collection)` — Python builtin returning the length of a

[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)    ///
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)    /// At v0.2.0 first cut the collection must type as `Type::List(_)`

[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)    ///

[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)    Len(Box<Expr>),
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)    /// PMAT-1074: `open(<path>).read()` — read a whole file to a `str`. Emitted

[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)    /// (missing file → `xpile: FileNotFoundError` = CPython's FileNotFoundError,

[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)    FileReadLines(Box<Expr>),
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)    /// List indexed access — Python `xs[i]`. PMAT-457, v0.2.0 Track 1.B.
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)    ///
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)    /// At v0.2.0 first cut the `index` expression is treated as a
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)    /// non-negative `i64` and the backend coerces to `usize` (Rust /
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)    /// Ruchy) or `Nat` (Lean) at emission. Negative-index semantics
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)    /// (Python's `xs[-1]` = last element) are not supported — the
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)    /// emitted Rust will panic on overflow if `index < 0`.
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)    /// Out-of-range access panics in all three backends, matching
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)    /// Python's `IndexError` posture (Rust: panic in `vec[i]`;
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)    /// Lean: `xs[i]!` panic on `none`).
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)    ///
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)    /// Governing contract: `C-XLATE-PY-LIST-TO-VEC` —
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)    /// `iteration_order_preserved` Bronze theorem implies the lowered
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)    /// `Vec`'s `[i]` produces the same element as the source `list`'s
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)    /// `[i]`.
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)    Index {
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)        collection: Box<Expr>,
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)        index: Box<Expr>,
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)    },
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)    /// Bounded slice — Python `xs[lo:hi]`. PMAT-496 (sprint), first cut:
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)    /// both bounds present, non-negative `i64`, step 1. `of_str` (set by
[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)    /// the frontend from the collection's type) selects the emit shape —
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)    /// list (`of_str=false`) emits `<c>[<lo> as usize..<hi> as usize]
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)    /// .to_vec()`; str (`of_str=true`) emits the same range with
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)    /// `.to_string()`. Result types as the collection's type (List(T) →
[1817](https://docs.rs#1817)    /// List(T); Str → Str). NOTE str slicing is byte-indexed
[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)    /// (ASCII-correct; a non-char-boundary index panics, matching the
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)    /// existing str byte-length posture). PMAT-502r: `lo`/`hi` are
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)    /// `Option` — an absent bound is an open end (`xs[a:]`, `xs[:b]`,
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)    /// `xs[:]`), emitting a half-open / full Rust range (`a..`, `..b`,
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)    /// `..`). PMAT-502bc: `step` carries a **positive integer literal**
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)    /// step over a *list* (`xs[a:b:c]`, `xs[::2]`, …); `None` is the
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)    /// default step of 1. With a step, the list emit becomes
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)    /// `<c>[<range>].iter().step_by(<step>).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>()`.
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)    /// The `xs[::-1]` reverse idiom is lowered to [`Expr::Reversed`]
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)    /// upstream, so a negative `step` never reaches here; other negative
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)    /// steps and stepped *string* slices remain deferred. Lean refuses.
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)    Slice {
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)        collection: Box<Expr>,
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)        lo: Option<Box<Expr>>,
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)        hi: Option<Box<Expr>>,
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)        of_str: bool,
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)        step: Option<i64>,
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)    },

[2215](https://docs.rs#2215)    /// `py_float_repr_block` as `str(float)`: `.0`-if-whole, scientific for a
[2216](https://docs.rs#2216)    /// decimal exponent `< -4` or `>= 16`), then groups the integer-part digit

[2227](https://docs.rs#2227)    /// PMAT-941 (correctness-hunt): a SCIENTIFIC-NOTATION float field — Python
[2228](https://docs.rs#2228)    /// `f"{1234.5:e}"` → `"1.234500e+03"`, `f"{1234.5:.2E}"` → `"1.23E+03"`,
[2229](https://docs.rs#2229)    /// `f"{1e100:e}"` → `"1.000000e+100"` (bare `e`/`E` defaults to 6 decimals).
[2230](https://docs.rs#2230)    /// Rust's `format!("{:.Ne}", x)` renders the right mantissa but a BARE
[2231](https://docs.rs#2231)    /// exponent (`1.234500e3` — no sign, no 2-digit-min zero-pad) and lowercases
[2232](https://docs.rs#2232)    /// `inf`/`nan` even under `{:E}`. So codegen renders to `precision` decimals,

[2235](https://docs.rs#2235)    /// (`inf`/`nan` for lower, `INF`/`NAN` for upper). `upper` selects the `E`

[2244](https://docs.rs#2244)    /// PMAT-965 (correctness-hunt): a GENERAL-float field — Python's `:g` / `:G`
[2245](https://docs.rs#2245)    /// presentation type. `f"{1234.5:g}"` → `"1234.5"`, `f"{123456789:g}"` →
[2246](https://docs.rs#2246)    /// `"1.23457e+08"`, `f"{3.14159:.3g}"` → `"3.14"`, `f"{1000000.0:g}"` →
[2247](https://docs.rs#2247)    /// `"1e+06"`. `:g` is the C-`printf` `%g` rule (also Python's DEFAULT float
[2248](https://docs.rs#2248)    /// presentation): with precision `P` (default 6, clamped to ≥1), let `X` be
[2249](https://docs.rs#2249)    /// the decimal exponent of the value rounded to `P` significant digits; use
[2250](https://docs.rs#2250)    /// FIXED notation with `P-1-X` decimals when `-4 ≤ X < P`, else SCIENTIFIC

[2252](https://docs.rs#2252)    /// Scientific output carries Python's `e±NN` exponent (sign always present,
[2253](https://docs.rs#2253)    /// magnitude zero-padded to ≥2 digits); `inf`/`nan` (upper `INF`/`NAN`) pass
[2254](https://docs.rs#2254)    /// through. Rust's `format!` has no `%g`, so codegen ports the algorithm:
[2255](https://docs.rs#2255)    /// read `X` from a `{:.P-1e}` render, branch, render, strip, fix the
[2256](https://docs.rs#2256)    /// exponent. `upper` selects the `G` presentation (uppercases the result).
[2257](https://docs.rs#2257)    /// Validated byte-identical to CPython over 513k (value × precision) cases.
[2258](https://docs.rs#2258)    /// The general-float companion to [`Expr::FloatSciStr`] / [`Expr::FloatGroupedStr`];
[2259](https://docs.rs#2259)    /// width-combined `:12g` and the `#g` alt flag stay deferred rejects. Lean
[2260](https://docs.rs#2260)    /// refuses (like [`Expr::FloatSciStr`]).
[2261](https://docs.rs#2261)    FloatGeneralStr {
[2262](https://docs.rs#2262)        value: Box<Expr>,
[2263](https://docs.rs#2263)        precision: u32,
[2264](https://docs.rs#2264)        upper: bool,
[2265](https://docs.rs#2265)    },
[2266](https://docs.rs#2266)    /// PMAT-942 (correctness-hunt): the SPACE sign flag ` ` on a numeric field —
[2267](https://docs.rs#2267)    /// Python `f"{5: d}"` → `" 5"`, `f"{-5: d}"` → `"-5"`, `f"{3.14: .2f}"` →
[2268](https://docs.rs#2268)    /// `" 3.14"`, and width/zero-pad combos `f"{5: 05d}"` → `" 0005"`. Python's
[2269](https://docs.rs#2269)    /// ` ` sign option puts a leading SPACE before a non-negative magnitude and a
[2270](https://docs.rs#2270)    /// `-` before a negative one (a `+` that prints a space instead). Rust's

[2272](https://docs.rs#2272)    /// width / zero-pad / precision IDENTICALLY to Python's, and a non-negative
[2273](https://docs.rs#2273)    /// `+`-formatted value carries exactly one leading `+` (a negative carries a
[2274](https://docs.rs#2274)    /// `-`, never a `+`), so codegen renders with the `+` spec and replaces the
[2275](https://docs.rs#2275)    /// FIRST `+` with a space — yielding Python's space-sign output for every
[2276](https://docs.rs#2276)    /// composition. `rust_spec` is the already-`+`-prefixed Rust spec (e.g. `+`,
[2277](https://docs.rs#2277)    /// `+.2`, `+05`, `+8.2`) produced by the frontend's `translate_format_spec`.
[2278](https://docs.rs#2278)    /// SCOPE: decimal int / fixed-point float only — radix-with-space (whose
[2279](https://docs.rs#2279)    /// negatives need sign-magnitude, like [`Expr::IntRadixStr`]) and a bare
[2280](https://docs.rs#2280)    /// space on a float (the whole-float-repr divergence, like bare `+`) stay
[2281](https://docs.rs#2281)    /// deferred rejects, same discipline as PMAT-557/613/941. Lean refuses (like
[2282](https://docs.rs#2282)    /// [`Expr::FloatSciStr`]).
[2283](https://docs.rs#2283)    SpaceSignStr { value: Box<Expr>, rust_spec: String },

[2709](https://docs.rs#2709)        list: Box<Expr>,

[2713](https://docs.rs#2713)    /// List pop — Python `xs.pop()` / `xs.pop(i)`. PMAT-502as (Tranche 2).
[2714](https://docs.rs#2714)    /// An *expression* that removes an element from the receiver and
[2715](https://docs.rs#2715)    /// evaluates to it (so the receiver must be mutable; the frontend
[2716](https://docs.rs#2716)    /// marks it). With no `index`, removes and returns the **last**
[2717](https://docs.rs#2717)    /// element; with an `index`, removes and returns the element at that
[2718](https://docs.rs#2718)    /// position. Both panic when out of range, matching Python's
[2719](https://docs.rs#2719)    /// `IndexError`. The result type is the list's element type.
[2720](https://docs.rs#2720)    ///
[2721](https://docs.rs#2721)    /// Backends:
[2722](https://docs.rs#2722)    ///   * Rust / Ruchy: no index → `(<list>).pop().unwrap()`; with index
[2723](https://docs.rs#2723)    ///     → `(<list>).remove((<index>) as usize)`.
[2724](https://docs.rs#2724)    ///   * Lean: refuses (in-place mutation, same gap as `Stmt::ListAppend`).
[2725](https://docs.rs#2725)    ListPop {
[2726](https://docs.rs#2726)        list: Box<Expr>,
[2727](https://docs.rs#2727)        index: Option<Box<Expr>>,
[2728](https://docs.rs#2728)    },
[2729](https://docs.rs#2729)    /// Dict pop — Python `d.pop(k)` / `d.pop(k, default)`. PMAT-502au
[2730](https://docs.rs#2730)    /// (Tranche 2). An *expression* that removes the entry for `key` and
[2731](https://docs.rs#2731)    /// evaluates to its value (so the receiver must be mutable; the
[2732](https://docs.rs#2732)    /// frontend marks it). With no `default`, panics when the key is
[2733](https://docs.rs#2733)    /// absent, matching Python's `KeyError`; with a `default`, evaluates
[2734](https://docs.rs#2734)    /// to it instead. The result type is the dict's value type.
[2735](https://docs.rs#2735)    ///
[2736](https://docs.rs#2736)    /// Backends:
[2737](https://docs.rs#2737)    ///   * Rust / Ruchy: no default → `(<dict>).remove(&(<key>)).unwrap()`;
[2738](https://docs.rs#2738)    ///     with default → `(<dict>).remove(&(<key>)).unwrap_or(<default>)`.
[2739](https://docs.rs#2739)    ///   * Lean: refuses (in-place mutation, same gap as `Stmt::ListAppend`).
[2740](https://docs.rs#2740)    DictPop {
[2741](https://docs.rs#2741)        dict: Box<Expr>,
[2742](https://docs.rs#2742)        key: Box<Expr>,

[2744](https://docs.rs#2744)    },
[2745](https://docs.rs#2745)    /// Dict get-or-insert — Python `d.setdefault(k, default)`. PMAT-502ax
[2746](https://docs.rs#2746)    /// (Tranche 2). An *expression*: if `key` is present, evaluates to its
[2747](https://docs.rs#2747)    /// value; otherwise inserts `default` under `key` and evaluates to it.
[2748](https://docs.rs#2748)    /// Because the absent case mutates, the receiver must be mutable (the
[2749](https://docs.rs#2749)    /// frontend marks it). The result type is the dict's value type.
[2750](https://docs.rs#2750)    ///
[2751](https://docs.rs#2751)    /// Backends:

[2753](https://docs.rs#2753)    ///     — `.entry` consumes the key, so it is `.clone()`d to keep the
[2754](https://docs.rs#2754)    ///     caller's binding usable (a no-op move for `Copy` keys); the
[2755](https://docs.rs#2755)    ///     trailing `.clone()` lifts the `&mut V` to an owned value.
[2756](https://docs.rs#2756)    ///   * Lean: refuses (in-place mutation, same gap as `Stmt::ListAppend`).
[2757](https://docs.rs#2757)    DictSetDefault {
[2758](https://docs.rs#2758)        dict: Box<Expr>,
[2759](https://docs.rs#2759)        key: Box<Expr>,
[2760](https://docs.rs#2760)        default: Box<Expr>,
[2761](https://docs.rs#2761)    },
[2762](https://docs.rs#2762)    /// Unary operation — `not x` (logical, Bool → Bool) or `-x`

[2764](https://docs.rs#2764)    UnOp { op: UnOp, operand: Box<Expr> },
[2765](https://docs.rs#2765)    /// String literal — the unquoted / "raw token" form. PMAT-042 /

[2788](https://docs.rs#2788)    QuotedString {

[2792](https://docs.rs#2792)    /// Shell variable reference (`$NAME` or `${NAME}`). PMAT-045 /

[2794](https://docs.rs#2794)    ///
[2795](https://docs.rs#2795)    /// The carried `String` is the variable name *without* the
[2796](https://docs.rs#2796)    /// leading `$` and *without* the optional braces. bashrs-backend
[2797](https://docs.rs#2797)    /// renders as `$NAME` by default. POSIX-legal name predicate
[2798](https://docs.rs#2798)    /// (alphanumeric + underscore, no leading digit) is enforced
[2799](https://docs.rs#2799)    /// at parse time, so a reachable `ShellVar` is always
[2800](https://docs.rs#2800)    /// renderable as bareword.
[2801](https://docs.rs#2801)    ///
[2802](https://docs.rs#2802)    /// Same cross-domain disposition as the other Layer B Expr
[2803](https://docs.rs#2803)    /// variants: produced only by `bashrs-frontend`, consumed only
[2804](https://docs.rs#2804)    /// by `bashrs-backend`; rust/ruchy/lean refuse via
[2805](https://docs.rs#2805)    /// `Unsupported(...)` naming `C-BASHRS-POSIX-IDEMPOTENCE`.
[2806](https://docs.rs#2806)    ShellVar(String),
[2807](https://docs.rs#2807)    /// POSIX shell special parameter (`$1`..`$9`, `$0`, `$@`, `$*`,
[2808](https://docs.rs#2808)    /// `$#`, `$?`, `$$`, `$!`, `$-`). PMAT-055.
[2809](https://docs.rs#2809)    ///
[2810](https://docs.rs#2810)    /// The carried `String` is the single-character name *without*
[2811](https://docs.rs#2811)    /// the leading `$`. Distinct from `Expr::ShellVar` because
[2812](https://docs.rs#2812)    /// special parameters are positional / runtime values set by

[2814](https://docs.rs#2814)    /// parser tags them via this variant rather than ShellVar so

[2816](https://docs.rs#2816)    /// separately.
[2817](https://docs.rs#2817)    ///
[2818](https://docs.rs#2818)    /// bashrs-backend renders as `$<name>` (no braces — they're
[2819](https://docs.rs#2819)    /// single-char so braces add nothing). Other backends refuse
[2820](https://docs.rs#2820)    /// via `Unsupported(...)` naming `C-BASHRS-POSIX-IDEMPOTENCE`.
[2821](https://docs.rs#2821)    ShellSpecial(String),
[2822](https://docs.rs#2822)    /// Shell command substitution (`$(cmd)`). PMAT-047 /
[2823](https://docs.rs#2823)    /// XPILE-BASHRS-MERGER-001 Layer B (Expr-side, composes Stmt
[2824](https://docs.rs#2824)    /// into Expr).
[2825](https://docs.rs#2825)    ///
[2826](https://docs.rs#2826)    /// The nested `Box<Stmt>` is typically a `Stmt::Cmd` (or future
[2827](https://docs.rs#2827)    /// `Stmt::Pipeline`). bashrs-backend renders by recursing into
[2828](https://docs.rs#2828)    /// the inner statement and wrapping with `$(...)`.
[2829](https://docs.rs#2829)    ///
[2830](https://docs.rs#2830)    /// IR-shape only at v0.1.0: bashrs-frontend's hand-rolled parser
[2831](https://docs.rs#2831)    /// doesn't recognise `$(...)` syntax yet (it'd require a real

[2833](https://docs.rs#2833)    /// v0.2.0 source fold's bashrs parser produces this variant

[2843](https://docs.rs#2843)/// Per-arg shell quoting choice. Carried by `Expr::QuotedString` so

[2845](https://docs.rs#2845)/// indicated. v0.1.0's bashrs-frontend doesn't have a real

[2857](https://docs.rs#2857)    /// are suppressed.

[2984](https://docs.rs#2984)    /// `.split(sep, maxsplit)` → `.splitn((maxsplit) as usize + 1, &(sep)[..])
[2985](https://docs.rs#2985)    /// .map(|s| s.to_string()).collect::<Vec<String>>()` (List(Str), 2 args).
[2986](https://docs.rs#2986)    /// Python's `maxsplit` caps the number of *splits*, so the part count is
[2987](https://docs.rs#2987)    /// `maxsplit + 1` (Rust `splitn` takes the part count). PMAT-518.
[2988](https://docs.rs#2988)    SplitN,
[2989](https://docs.rs#2989)    /// `.rsplit(sep, maxsplit)` → `.rsplitn((maxsplit) as usize + 1, &(sep)[..])
[2990](https://docs.rs#2990)    /// .map(|s| s.to_string()).collect::<Vec<String>>()` THEN reversed
[2991](https://docs.rs#2991)    /// (List(Str), 2 args). PMAT-644. Like [`SplitN`] but splits from the RIGHT,
[2992](https://docs.rs#2992)    /// capping at `maxsplit` splits; Rust's `rsplitn` yields parts right-to-left,
[2993](https://docs.rs#2993)    /// so the collected Vec is reversed to restore Python's left-to-right order.
[2994](https://docs.rs#2994)    RSplitN,
[2995](https://docs.rs#2995)    /// `.split()` (no arg) → `.split_whitespace().map(|s| s.to_string())
[2996](https://docs.rs#2996)    /// .collect::<Vec<String>>()` (List(Str), 0 args). PMAT-502co. Python's
[2997](https://docs.rs#2997)    /// no-arg split runs on any whitespace and drops empty fields, exactly
[2998](https://docs.rs#2998)    /// like Rust's `split_whitespace`.
[2999](https://docs.rs#2999)    SplitWhitespace,
[3000](https://docs.rs#3000)    /// `.join(xs)` → `xs.join(&(sep)[..])` (Str, 1 list arg). PMAT-492d.
[3001](https://docs.rs#3001)    /// NOTE the **receiver/arg inversion**: Python `sep.join(xs)` has the
[3002](https://docs.rs#3002)    /// separator as receiver, but Rust's `[String]::join` has the list as
[3003](https://docs.rs#3003)    /// receiver — so backends emit the arg as the Rust receiver.
[3004](https://docs.rs#3004)    Join,
[3005](https://docs.rs#3005)    /// `.replace(old, new)` → `.replace(&(old)[..], &(new)[..])`
[3006](https://docs.rs#3006)    /// (Str, 2 args). PMAT-502b.
[3007](https://docs.rs#3007)    Replace,
[3008](https://docs.rs#3008)    /// `.replace(old, new, count)` → `.replacen(&(old)[..], &(new)[..],
[3009](https://docs.rs#3009)    /// (count) as usize)` — replace the first `count` occurrences (Str, 3 args).
[3010](https://docs.rs#3010)    /// PMAT-517.
[3011](https://docs.rs#3011)    ReplaceN,
[3012](https://docs.rs#3012)    /// `.lstrip()` → `.trim_start().to_string()` (Str, 0 args). PMAT-502l.
[3013](https://docs.rs#3013)    LStrip,
[3014](https://docs.rs#3014)    /// `.rstrip()` → `.trim_end().to_string()` (Str, 0 args). PMAT-502l.
[3015](https://docs.rs#3015)    RStrip,
[3016](https://docs.rs#3016)    /// `.find(sub)` → `.find(&(sub)[..]).map(|__i| __i as i64).unwrap_or(-1)`
[3017](https://docs.rs#3017)    /// (**Int**, 1 arg) — byte index of the first match, or `-1`. PMAT-502l.
[3018](https://docs.rs#3018)    /// (Python's `.find` is a *char* index; for ASCII — the v0.1.0 subset —
[3019](https://docs.rs#3019)    /// byte and char indices coincide.)
[3020](https://docs.rs#3020)    Find,
[3021](https://docs.rs#3021)    /// `.count(sub)` → `.matches(&(sub)[..]).count() as i64` (**Int**, 1 arg)
[3022](https://docs.rs#3022)    /// — count of non-overlapping occurrences. PMAT-502l.
[3023](https://docs.rs#3023)    Count,
[3024](https://docs.rs#3024)    /// `.index(sub)` → byte index of the first match (**Int**, 1 arg).
[3025](https://docs.rs#3025)    /// PMAT-502bi. Like [`StrMethodOp::Find`] but **panics** when the
[3026](https://docs.rs#3026)    /// substring is absent (matching Python's `ValueError`, vs `find`'s
[3027](https://docs.rs#3027)    /// `-1`): `.find(&(sub)[..]).map(|__i| __i as i64).expect(…)`.
[3028](https://docs.rs#3028)    /// (ASCII subset — byte index = char index.)
[3029](https://docs.rs#3029)    StrIndex,
[3030](https://docs.rs#3030)    /// `.rfind(sub)` → byte index of the **last** match, or `-1` (**Int**, 1
[3031](https://docs.rs#3031)    /// arg). PMAT-545. The reverse-search mirror of [`StrMethodOp::Find`]:
[3032](https://docs.rs#3032)    /// `.rfind(&(sub)[..]).map(|__i| __i as i64).unwrap_or(-1)`.
[3033](https://docs.rs#3033)    /// (ASCII subset — byte index = char index.)
[3034](https://docs.rs#3034)    Rfind,
[3035](https://docs.rs#3035)    /// `.rindex(sub)` → byte index of the **last** match, or **panic** on
[3036](https://docs.rs#3036)    /// absence (Python `ValueError`). PMAT-545. The reverse-search mirror of
[3037](https://docs.rs#3037)    /// [`StrMethodOp::StrIndex`]: `.rfind(&(sub)[..]).map(|__i| __i as i64)
[3038](https://docs.rs#3038)    /// .expect(…)`. (ASCII subset — byte index = char index.)
[3039](https://docs.rs#3039)    RIndex,
[3040](https://docs.rs#3040)    /// `.isdigit()` → `(!(s).is_empty() && (s).chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()))`
[3041](https://docs.rs#3041)    /// (**Bool**, 0 args). PMAT-502ag. Python returns `False` for the empty
[3042](https://docs.rs#3042)    /// string, so the empty guard is required (a vacuous `.all()` is `true`).
[3043](https://docs.rs#3043)    IsDigit,
[3044](https://docs.rs#3044)    /// `.isnumeric()` → `(!(s).is_empty() && (s).chars().all(|c| c.is_numeric()))`
[3045](https://docs.rs#3045)    /// (**Bool**, 0 args). PMAT-643. Broader than `isdigit` — Rust's
[3046](https://docs.rs#3046)    /// `char::is_numeric()` covers the Unicode Number categories (Nd/Nl/No),
[3047](https://docs.rs#3047)    /// matching Python's `str.isnumeric()`. Shares the empty-guard "all chars
[3048](https://docs.rs#3048)    /// match" shape with [`StrMethodOp::IsDigit`].
[3049](https://docs.rs#3049)    IsNumeric,
[3050](https://docs.rs#3050)    /// `.isalpha()` → `(!(s).is_empty() && (s).chars().all(|c| c.is_alphabetic()))`
[3051](https://docs.rs#3051)    /// (**Bool**, 0 args). PMAT-502ag.
[3052](https://docs.rs#3052)    IsAlpha,
[3053](https://docs.rs#3053)    /// `.isspace()` → `(!(s).is_empty() && (s).chars().all(|c| c.is_whitespace()))`
[3054](https://docs.rs#3054)    /// (**Bool**, 0 args). PMAT-502ag.
[3055](https://docs.rs#3055)    IsSpace,
[3056](https://docs.rs#3056)    /// `.isalnum()` → `(!(s).is_empty() && (s).chars().all(|c| c.is_alphanumeric()))`
[3057](https://docs.rs#3057)    /// (**Bool**, 0 args). PMAT-502di. Shares the empty-guard "all chars match"
[3058](https://docs.rs#3058)    /// shape with [`StrMethodOp::IsDigit`].
[3059](https://docs.rs#3059)    IsAlnum,
[3060](https://docs.rs#3060)    /// `.isupper()` → `((s).chars().any(|c| c.is_uppercase()) && !(s).chars()
[3061](https://docs.rs#3061)    /// .any(|c| c.is_lowercase()))` (**Bool**, 0 args). PMAT-502di. Python's
[3062](https://docs.rs#3062)    /// rule: at least one cased char AND no lowercase among the cased chars
[3063](https://docs.rs#3063)    /// (so `"A1".isupper()` is `True`, `"".isupper()` is `False`).
[3064](https://docs.rs#3064)    IsUpper,
[3065](https://docs.rs#3065)    /// `.islower()` → the lowercase mirror of [`StrMethodOp::IsUpper`]
[3066](https://docs.rs#3066)    /// (**Bool**, 0 args). PMAT-502di.
[3067](https://docs.rs#3067)    IsLower,
[3068](https://docs.rs#3068)    /// `.isascii()` → `(s).is_ascii()` (**Bool**, 0 args). PMAT-695. True iff
[3069](https://docs.rs#3069)    /// every char is in the ASCII range (U+0000..=U+007F). The empty string is
[3070](https://docs.rs#3070)    /// `True` in both Python and Rust (`"".is_ascii()` is `true`), so — unlike
[3071](https://docs.rs#3071)    /// the `isdigit`-family predicates — no empty guard is needed.
[3072](https://docs.rs#3072)    IsAscii,
[3073](https://docs.rs#3073)    /// `.capitalize()` → first char upper-cased, the rest lower-cased
[3074](https://docs.rs#3074)    /// (**Str**, 0 args). PMAT-502ah. Emits a block that pops the first
[3075](https://docs.rs#3075)    /// char (`to_uppercase`) and lower-cases the remainder; the empty
[3076](https://docs.rs#3076)    /// string maps to `""` (matching Python).
[3077](https://docs.rs#3077)    Capitalize,
[3078](https://docs.rs#3078)    /// `.title()` → title-case: the first alphabetic char of each word is
[3079](https://docs.rs#3079)    /// upper-cased, the rest lower-cased; any non-alphabetic char is a word
[3080](https://docs.rs#3080)    /// boundary (**Str**, 0 args). PMAT-502aj. Emits a fold that tracks
[3081](https://docs.rs#3081)    /// "previous char was alphabetic", matching Python's exact semantics
[3082](https://docs.rs#3082)    /// (e.g. `"it's".title()` → `"It'S"`).
[3083](https://docs.rs#3083)    Title,
[3084](https://docs.rs#3084)    /// `.rjust(width)` → right-justify in a field of `width` (space-padded
[3085](https://docs.rs#3085)    /// on the left) (**Str**, 1 int arg). PMAT-502aw. Emits
[3086](https://docs.rs#3086)    /// `format!("{:>1$}", <recv>, (<width>) as usize)`. Rust's format width
[3087](https://docs.rs#3087)    /// is a *minimum* — a longer string is returned unchanged, exactly
[3088](https://docs.rs#3088)    /// matching Python (no truncation). A non-default fill char is deferred.
[3089](https://docs.rs#3089)    RJust,
[3090](https://docs.rs#3090)    /// `.ljust(width)` → left-justify (space-padded on the right)
[3091](https://docs.rs#3091)    /// (**Str**, 1 int arg). PMAT-502aw. Emits
[3092](https://docs.rs#3092)    /// `format!("{:<1$}", <recv>, (<width>) as usize)`.
[3093](https://docs.rs#3093)    LJust,
[3094](https://docs.rs#3094)    /// `.removeprefix(p)` → the string with a leading `p` removed, else

[3098](https://docs.rs#3098)    RemovePrefix,
[3099](https://docs.rs#3099)    /// `.removesuffix(p)` → trailing `p` removed, else unchanged (**Str**,
[3100](https://docs.rs#3100)    /// 1 arg). PMAT-502cq. Like [`StrMethodOp::RemovePrefix`] with

[3102](https://docs.rs#3102)    RemoveSuffix,
[3103](https://docs.rs#3103)    /// `.swapcase()` → upper↔lower each char (**Str**, 0 args). PMAT-502cr.
[3104](https://docs.rs#3104)    /// Emits `(<recv>).chars().map(|__c| if __c.is_uppercase() {
[3105](https://docs.rs#3105)    /// __c.to_lowercase().collect::<String>() } else if __c.is_lowercase() {
[3106](https://docs.rs#3106)    /// __c.to_uppercase().collect::<String>() } else { __c.to_string() })
[3107](https://docs.rs#3107)    /// .collect::<String>()` — non-cased chars are left unchanged, matching
[3108](https://docs.rs#3108)    /// Python.
[3109](https://docs.rs#3109)    SwapCase,
[3110](https://docs.rs#3110)    /// `.zfill(width)` → left-pad with `0` to `width` chars, **sign-aware**
[3111](https://docs.rs#3111)    /// (a leading `-`/`+` stays first, zeros are inserted after it)
[3112](https://docs.rs#3112)    /// (**Str**, 1 int arg). PMAT-502cs. A string already ≥ `width` is
[3113](https://docs.rs#3113)    /// returned unchanged. Block-form codegen (receiver used several times).
[3114](https://docs.rs#3114)    ZFill,

[3116](https://docs.rs#3116)    /// (**Str**, 1 int arg). PMAT-502cu. Matches CPython's parity-dependent
[3117](https://docs.rs#3117)    /// bias `left = marg/2 + (marg & width & 1)` (so `"ab".center(5)` →
[3118](https://docs.rs#3118)    /// `"  ab "`, not Rust `{:^}`'s right-bias). Already-wide → unchanged.
[3119](https://docs.rs#3119)    /// Block-form codegen.
[3120](https://docs.rs#3120)    Center,
[3121](https://docs.rs#3121)    /// `.partition(sep)` → the 3-tuple `(before, sep, after)` split at the

[3123](https://docs.rs#3123)    /// `match (recv).split_once(&(sep)[..]) { Some((__a, __b)) =>
[3124](https://docs.rs#3124)    /// (__a.to_string(), (sep).to_string(), __b.to_string()), None =>
[3125](https://docs.rs#3125)    /// ((recv).to_string(), String::new(), String::new()) }` — when `sep` is

[3127](https://docs.rs#3127)    Partition,

[3132](https://docs.rs#3132)    RPartition,

[3302](https://docs.rs#3302)// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[3303](https://docs.rs#3303)// PMAT-573: reserved-identifier escaping for the Rust-family backends.
[3304](https://docs.rs#3304)//
[3305](https://docs.rs#3305)// A Python program may legally name a variable / parameter / function
[3306](https://docs.rs#3306)// after a word that is a *Rust* keyword but NOT a Python keyword —
[3307](https://docs.rs#3307)// `type`, `match`, `loop`, `move`, `ref`, `mut`, `box`, `final`, … (and
[3308](https://docs.rs#3308)// lowercase `true`/`false`, which Python spells `True`/`False`). Emitted
[3309](https://docs.rs#3309)// verbatim those break `rustc` ("expected identifier, found keyword
[3310](https://docs.rs#3310)// `type`"), violating the xpile invariant transpile-success ⟹ valid Rust.
[3311](https://docs.rs#3311)//
[3312](https://docs.rs#3312)// The fix is a single IR pre-pass (run by the Rust and Ruchy backends on
[3313](https://docs.rs#3313)// a cloned module before emission) that rewrites every *identifier-
[3314](https://docs.rs#3314)// position* string to the Rust raw form `r#name`. Doing it on the data —
[3315](https://docs.rs#3315)// once, at every binding AND every reference — guarantees the two never
[3316](https://docs.rs#3316)// drift, which a per-emit-site escape could not. The walker is exhaustive
[3317](https://docs.rs#3317)// (no wildcard arm) so a future `Expr`/`Stmt` variant fails to compile
[3318](https://docs.rs#3318)// here until its identifier positions are classified — the completeness
[3319](https://docs.rs#3319)// is compiler-enforced. Raw identifiers are a Rust-family feature (Rust +
[3320](https://docs.rs#3320)// Ruchy share the keyword set and `r#` syntax); Lean uses a different
[3321](https://docs.rs#3321)// keyword set and does not call this.
[3322](https://docs.rs#3322)// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[3323](https://docs.rs#3323)
[3324](https://docs.rs#3324)/// True for Rust 2021 strict + reserved keywords that ARE escapable as a
[3325](https://docs.rs#3325)/// raw identifier (`r#kw`). Excludes the four keywords that cannot be raw
[3326](https://docs.rs#3326)/// (`crate`/`self`/`Self`/`super`) — leaving those unescaped also keeps the
[3327](https://docs.rs#3327)/// special-cased `self` method receiver intact — and the contextual
[3328](https://docs.rs#3328)/// keywords (`union`/`macro_rules`) that are already valid bare identifiers.
[3329](https://docs.rs#3329)/// Including the Rust keywords that are *also* Python keywords (`if`, `for`,
[3330](https://docs.rs#3330)/// `return`, …) is harmless: those can never reach us as a Python
[3331](https://docs.rs#3331)/// identifier, so the arm is never taken.
[3332](https://docs.rs#3332)fn is_rust_raw_keyword(name: &str) -> bool {
[3333](https://docs.rs#3333)    matches!(
[3334](https://docs.rs#3334)        name,
[3335](https://docs.rs#3335)        "as" | "break"
[3336](https://docs.rs#3336)            | "const"
[3337](https://docs.rs#3337)            | "continue"
[3338](https://docs.rs#3338)            | "dyn"
[3339](https://docs.rs#3339)            | "else"
[3340](https://docs.rs#3340)            | "enum"
[3341](https://docs.rs#3341)            | "extern"
[3342](https://docs.rs#3342)            | "false"
[3343](https://docs.rs#3343)            | "fn"
[3344](https://docs.rs#3344)            | "for"
[3345](https://docs.rs#3345)            | "if"
[3346](https://docs.rs#3346)            | "impl"
[3347](https://docs.rs#3347)            | "in"
[3348](https://docs.rs#3348)            | "let"
[3349](https://docs.rs#3349)            | "loop"
[3350](https://docs.rs#3350)            | "match"
[3351](https://docs.rs#3351)            | "mod"
[3352](https://docs.rs#3352)            | "move"
[3353](https://docs.rs#3353)            | "mut"
[3354](https://docs.rs#3354)            | "pub"
[3355](https://docs.rs#3355)            | "ref"
[3356](https://docs.rs#3356)            | "return"
[3357](https://docs.rs#3357)            | "static"
[3358](https://docs.rs#3358)            | "struct"
[3359](https://docs.rs#3359)            | "trait"
[3360](https://docs.rs#3360)            | "true"
[3361](https://docs.rs#3361)            | "type"
[3362](https://docs.rs#3362)            | "unsafe"
[3363](https://docs.rs#3363)            | "use"
[3364](https://docs.rs#3364)            | "where"
[3365](https://docs.rs#3365)            | "while"
[3366](https://docs.rs#3366)            | "async"
[3367](https://docs.rs#3367)            | "await"
[3368](https://docs.rs#3368)            | "abstract"
[3369](https://docs.rs#3369)            | "become"
[3370](https://docs.rs#3370)            | "box"
[3371](https://docs.rs#3371)            | "do"
[3372](https://docs.rs#3372)            | "final"
[3373](https://docs.rs#3373)            | "macro"
[3374](https://docs.rs#3374)            | "override"
[3375](https://docs.rs#3375)            | "priv"
[3376](https://docs.rs#3376)            | "try"
[3377](https://docs.rs#3377)            | "typeof"
[3378](https://docs.rs#3378)            | "unsized"
[3379](https://docs.rs#3379)            | "virtual"
[3380](https://docs.rs#3380)            | "yield"
[3381](https://docs.rs#3381)    )

[3384](https://docs.rs#3384)/// Rewrite a single identifier-position string in place: a Rust keyword
[3385](https://docs.rs#3385)/// becomes its raw form `r#kw`; anything else (the overwhelming common
[3386](https://docs.rs#3386)/// case) is left untouched. Idempotent — `r#type` is not itself a keyword.
[3387](https://docs.rs#3387)fn escape_name(name: &mut String) {
[3388](https://docs.rs#3388)    if is_rust_raw_keyword(name) {
[3389](https://docs.rs#3389)        *name = format!("r#{name}");
[3390](https://docs.rs#3390)    }
[3391](https://docs.rs#3391)}
[3392](https://docs.rs#3392)
[3393](https://docs.rs#3393)fn escape_sortkey(k: &mut SortKey) {
[3394](https://docs.rs#3394)    escape_name(&mut k.param);
[3395](https://docs.rs#3395)    escape_expr(&mut k.body);
[3396](https://docs.rs#3396)}
[3397](https://docs.rs#3397)
[3398](https://docs.rs#3398)/// Escape every identifier-position string reachable from `e`.
[3399](https://docs.rs#3399)fn escape_expr(e: &mut Expr) {
[3400](https://docs.rs#3400)    match e {
[3401](https://docs.rs#3401)        // The core reference site.
[3402](https://docs.rs#3402)        Expr::Ident(name) => escape_name(name),
[3403](https://docs.rs#3403)        // Direct call-by-name — escape the callee so it matches the
[3404](https://docs.rs#3404)        // (escaped) function definition name.
[3405](https://docs.rs#3405)        Expr::Call { callee, args } => {
[3406](https://docs.rs#3406)            // PMAT-823 (HUNT-V24 PROP-CM-02): a qualified static/classmethod
[3407](https://docs.rs#3407)            // callee `Class::method` — escape only the METHOD segment if it is a
[3408](https://docs.rs#3408)            // Rust keyword (the def was escaped by `escape_function`, so the call
[3409](https://docs.rs#3409)            // must agree: `Reg::r#match`). `escape_name` on the whole `Reg::match`
[3410](https://docs.rs#3410)            // is a no-op (it isn't a bare keyword). A non-qualified callee (a
[3411](https://docs.rs#3411)            // free fn) is escaped whole, as before.
[3412](https://docs.rs#3412)            match callee.rsplit_once("::") {
[3413](https://docs.rs#3413)                Some((class, method)) => {
[3414](https://docs.rs#3414)                    let class = class.to_string();
[3415](https://docs.rs#3415)                    let mut method = method.to_string();
[3416](https://docs.rs#3416)                    escape_name(&mut method);
[3417](https://docs.rs#3417)                    *callee = format!("{class}::{method}");
[3418](https://docs.rs#3418)                }
[3419](https://docs.rs#3419)                None => escape_name(callee),
[3420](https://docs.rs#3420)            }
[3421](https://docs.rs#3421)            for a in args {
[3422](https://docs.rs#3422)                escape_expr(a);
[3423](https://docs.rs#3423)            }
[3424](https://docs.rs#3424)        }
[3425](https://docs.rs#3425)        // Leaves: no sub-expression and no identifier field. (Enum/struct/
[3426](https://docs.rs#3426)        // method/field names are type-level and left unescaped — a Python
[3427](https://docs.rs#3427)        // class/field named after a keyword is a separate, rarer case.)
[3428](https://docs.rs#3428)        Expr::Unit
[3429](https://docs.rs#3429)        | Expr::LitInt(_)
[3430](https://docs.rs#3430)        | Expr::LitFloat(_)
[3431](https://docs.rs#3431)        | Expr::LitBool(_)
[3432](https://docs.rs#3432)        | Expr::LitStr(_)
[3433](https://docs.rs#3433)        | Expr::QuotedString { .. }
[3434](https://docs.rs#3434)        | Expr::ShellVar(_)
[3435](https://docs.rs#3435)        | Expr::ShellSpecial(_)
[3436](https://docs.rs#3436)        | Expr::EnumVariant { .. } => {}
[3437](https://docs.rs#3437)        Expr::Block(b) => {
[3438](https://docs.rs#3438)            for s in &mut b.stmts {
[3439](https://docs.rs#3439)                escape_stmt(s);
[3440](https://docs.rs#3440)            }
[3441](https://docs.rs#3441)            escape_expr(&mut b.trailing_return);
[3442](https://docs.rs#3442)        }
[3443](https://docs.rs#3443)        Expr::FloatBinOp { lhs, rhs, .. }
[3444](https://docs.rs#3444)        | Expr::BinOp { lhs, rhs, .. }
[3445](https://docs.rs#3445)        | Expr::Concat { lhs, rhs }
[3446](https://docs.rs#3446)        | Expr::ListConcat { lhs, rhs }
[3447](https://docs.rs#3447)        | Expr::SetOp { lhs, rhs, .. }
[3448](https://docs.rs#3448)        | Expr::SetPred { lhs, rhs, .. } => {
[3449](https://docs.rs#3449)            escape_expr(lhs);
[3450](https://docs.rs#3450)            escape_expr(rhs);
[3451](https://docs.rs#3451)        }
[3452](https://docs.rs#3452)        // PMAT-745: int/float exact comparison — escape both operands.
[3453](https://docs.rs#3453)        Expr::MixedIntFloatCmp { int, float, .. } => {
[3454](https://docs.rs#3454)            escape_expr(int);
[3455](https://docs.rs#3455)            escape_expr(float);
[3456](https://docs.rs#3456)        }
[3457](https://docs.rs#3457)        Expr::UnOp { operand, .. } => escape_expr(operand),
[3458](https://docs.rs#3458)        Expr::IfExpr {
[3459](https://docs.rs#3459)            cond,
[3460](https://docs.rs#3460)            then_expr,
[3461](https://docs.rs#3461)            else_expr,
[3462](https://docs.rs#3462)        } => {
[3463](https://docs.rs#3463)            escape_expr(cond);
[3464](https://docs.rs#3464)            escape_expr(then_expr);
[3465](https://docs.rs#3465)            escape_expr(else_expr);
[3466](https://docs.rs#3466)        }
[3467](https://docs.rs#3467)        Expr::StrFormat { args, .. } | Expr::NumBuiltin { args, .. } => {
[3468](https://docs.rs#3468)            for a in args {
[3469](https://docs.rs#3469)                escape_expr(a);
[3470](https://docs.rs#3470)            }
[3471](https://docs.rs#3471)        }
[3472](https://docs.rs#3472)        Expr::StrCharAt { string, index } => {
[3473](https://docs.rs#3473)            escape_expr(string);
[3474](https://docs.rs#3474)            escape_expr(index);
[3475](https://docs.rs#3475)        }
[3476](https://docs.rs#3476)        Expr::StrChars { string } => escape_expr(string),
[3477](https://docs.rs#3477)        Expr::Ord { value } | Expr::Chr { value } => escape_expr(value),
[3478](https://docs.rs#3478)        Expr::IntRadixStr { value, .. }
[3479](https://docs.rs#3479)        | Expr::IntGroupedStr { value, .. }
[3480](https://docs.rs#3480)        | Expr::FloatGroupedStr { value, .. }
[3481](https://docs.rs#3481)        | Expr::FloatSciStr { value, .. }
[3482](https://docs.rs#3482)        | Expr::FloatGeneralStr { value, .. }
[3483](https://docs.rs#3483)        | Expr::SpaceSignStr { value, .. }
[3484](https://docs.rs#3484)        | Expr::IntFromStrRadix { value, .. }
[3485](https://docs.rs#3485)        | Expr::FormatSpec { value, .. }
[3486](https://docs.rs#3486)        | Expr::NumCast { value, .. }
[3487](https://docs.rs#3487)        | Expr::ToStr { value, .. }
[3488](https://docs.rs#3488)        | Expr::ReprStr { value }
[3489](https://docs.rs#3489)        | Expr::RoundToInt { value } => escape_expr(value),
[3490](https://docs.rs#3490)        Expr::StrMethod { recv, args, .. } => {
[3491](https://docs.rs#3491)            escape_expr(recv);
[3492](https://docs.rs#3492)            for a in args {
[3493](https://docs.rs#3493)                escape_expr(a);
[3494](https://docs.rs#3494)            }
[3495](https://docs.rs#3495)        }
[3496](https://docs.rs#3496)        Expr::TupleLit(elems) | Expr::ListLit(elems) | Expr::SetLit(elems) => {
[3497](https://docs.rs#3497)            for el in elems {
[3498](https://docs.rs#3498)                escape_expr(el);
[3499](https://docs.rs#3499)            }
[3500](https://docs.rs#3500)        }
[3501](https://docs.rs#3501)        Expr::TupleIndex { tuple, .. } => escape_expr(tuple),
[3502](https://docs.rs#3502)        Expr::Slice {
[3503](https://docs.rs#3503)            collection, lo, hi, ..
[3504](https://docs.rs#3504)        } => {
[3505](https://docs.rs#3505)            escape_expr(collection);
[3506](https://docs.rs#3506)            if let Some(l) = lo {
[3507](https://docs.rs#3507)                escape_expr(l);
[3508](https://docs.rs#3508)            }
[3509](https://docs.rs#3509)            if let Some(h) = hi {
[3510](https://docs.rs#3510)                escape_expr(h);
[3511](https://docs.rs#3511)            }
[3512](https://docs.rs#3512)        }
[3513](https://docs.rs#3513)        Expr::Sum { list, start, .. } => {
[3514](https://docs.rs#3514)            escape_expr(list);
[3515](https://docs.rs#3515)            if let Some(s) = start {
[3516](https://docs.rs#3516)                escape_expr(s);
[3517](https://docs.rs#3517)            }
[3518](https://docs.rs#3518)        }
[3519](https://docs.rs#3519)        Expr::BoolReduce { list, .. }
[3520](https://docs.rs#3520)        | Expr::Reversed { list }
[3521](https://docs.rs#3521)        | Expr::SetFromList { list }
[3522](https://docs.rs#3522)        | Expr::Enumerate { list, .. } => escape_expr(list),
[3523](https://docs.rs#3523)        Expr::RoundToDigits { value, ndigits } | Expr::RoundIntToDigits { value, ndigits } => {
[3524](https://docs.rs#3524)            escape_expr(value);

[3527](https://docs.rs#3527)        Expr::Repeat { seq, n, .. } => {

[3531](https://docs.rs#3531)        Expr::Sorted { list, key, .. } => {

[3537](https://docs.rs#3537)        Expr::Gcd { a, b } | Expr::Lcm { a, b } => {

[3541](https://docs.rs#3541)        Expr::Factorial { n } | Expr::Isqrt { n } => escape_expr(n),
[3542](https://docs.rs#3542)        Expr::Comb { n, k } | Expr::Perm { n, k } => {

[3546](https://docs.rs#3546)        Expr::PowMod { base, exp, modulus } => {

[3551](https://docs.rs#3551)        Expr::RangeList { start, stop, .. } => {

[3555](https://docs.rs#3555)        Expr::SetToList { set } => escape_expr(set),
[3556](https://docs.rs#3556)        Expr::DictFromPairs { pairs } => escape_expr(pairs),
[3557](https://docs.rs#3557)        Expr::DictMerge { entries } => {

[3698](https://docs.rs#3698)/// Escape every identifier-position string reachable from `s`.
[3699](https://docs.rs#3699)fn escape_stmt(s: &mut Stmt) {
[3700](https://docs.rs#3700)    match s {
[3701](https://docs.rs#3701)        Stmt::Return(e) => escape_expr(e),
[3702](https://docs.rs#3702)        Stmt::Let { name, value, .. } | Stmt::Assign { name, value } => {

[3705](https://docs.rs#3705)        }
[3706](https://docs.rs#3706)        Stmt::ClosureLet { name, params, body } => {

[3712](https://docs.rs#3712)        }
[3713](https://docs.rs#3713)        // PMAT-736: a named inner fn — escape its name + param names, then walk

[3715](https://docs.rs#3715)        Stmt::NestedFn {

[3723](https://docs.rs#3723)                escape_stmt(st);
[3724](https://docs.rs#3724)            }

[3727](https://docs.rs#3727)        Stmt::LetTuple { names, value, .. } => {

[3730](https://docs.rs#3730)            }

[3732](https://docs.rs#3732)        }

[3975](https://docs.rs#3975)/// PMAT-736 (HUNT-V11 V11-6): collect every identifier-position name reachable
[3976](https://docs.rs#3976)/// from `block` into `acc` — both value references (`Expr::Ident`, a `Call`
[3977](https://docs.rs#3977)/// callee) and receiver names (`xs.append(...)`'s `xs`, `d[k] = v`'s `d`, …),
[3978](https://docs.rs#3978)/// plus binding names (a `let`, a loop var). It is the read-only mirror of the
[3979](https://docs.rs#3979)/// `escape_*` walker above: every `escape_name(x)` there becomes
[3980](https://docs.rs#3980)/// `acc.insert(x)` here, so the two stay structurally identical (both are
[3981](https://docs.rs#3981)/// compiler-checked exhaustive over `Stmt`/`Expr`). Used by the frontend's
[3982](https://docs.rs#3982)/// nested-function lowering to decide whether a nested `def` is self-recursive
[3983](https://docs.rs#3983)/// and whether it captures an enclosing local — over-collection (a binding name,
[3984](https://docs.rs#3984)/// a lambda param) is harmless there, since the caller only intersects the
[3985](https://docs.rs#3985)/// result with the enclosing scope.
[3986](https://docs.rs#3986)pub fn collect_block_idents(block: &Block, acc: &mut std::collections::HashSet<String>) {
[3987](https://docs.rs#3987)    for s in &block.stmts {
[3988](https://docs.rs#3988)        collect_idents_stmt(s, acc);
[3989](https://docs.rs#3989)    }
[3990](https://docs.rs#3990)    collect_idents_expr(&block.trailing_return, acc);
[3991](https://docs.rs#3991)}
[3992](https://docs.rs#3992)
[3993](https://docs.rs#3993)fn collect_idents_sortkey(k: &SortKey, acc: &mut std::collections::HashSet<String>) {
[3994](https://docs.rs#3994)    acc.insert(k.param.clone());
[3995](https://docs.rs#3995)    collect_idents_expr(&k.body, acc);
[3996](https://docs.rs#3996)}
